passages.heading: Minutes | Page 1
passages.text:
FSEC (Faculty Senate Executive Committee) Meeting Minutes Date: Wednesday, September 17, 2025 - Time: 10:00 AM – 12:00 noon Pastore Hall, Room 224 Remote option via ZOOM Action Items: Staff will post the Acronym Glossary on the FS webpage.
Committee liaisons need to be sure drafts of proposed legislation are taken up by appropriate review committees in a timely fashion.
FSEC members should be prepared to make suggestions for the remaining Joint Committee open seats on 9/24.
FS Pres. and staff will develop a calendar of “guest appearances” at FSEC weekly meetings for the remainder of fall semester.
The Coordinator and Specialist will assign appropriate Kuali access to the student CASC representative. 1.
Call to Order - FS President Williams called the meeting to order at 10:01.
VP Preisser and Sens.
Daniels, Meenach, Trimm and Van Wyk were present. 2.
Minutes - Minutes of the 9/10/25 meeting were tabled. 3.
Priority Items 3.1 Sept. 11 Senate Orientation - Re-cap - It was generally agreed that the event went very well.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 1
passages.text:
Some key points to stress on 9/18 include the necessity for remote attendees to log in using a URI account, and the logistics of transitioning away from using the term “report” when addressing proposed legislation (“bills”).
It was also noted that not all senators attended and this is especially concerning where newly elected members are concerned.
It was noted that some legitimate scheduling conflicts are being encountered, some of which are unavoidable given the timing of elections in relation to setting course schedules, etc.
Lack of familiarity with senate jargon becomes evident in conversations with new members, and staff was asked to put the FSEC’s “acronym glossary” on the FS website as a resource for all. 3.2 Meeting planning - Sept. 18 FS Meeting - see agenda - the agenda was discussed and key FSEC in-meeting duties were addressed.
FS Pres.
Williams will note during the meeting that a move away from the “Consent Agenda” is desired, and unless the senate finds itself struggling to complete business in the time allowed, this tool may not be used this year.
Staff will assist with assembling a brief slide deck regarding the four new initiatives under Item 6.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 1
passages.text:
The University President will offer a report, including a budget presentation. 3.2.1 Finalize travel path for introduced legislation - All four items under Item 6 on the agenda (c - f) will require CBUM review.
Some projects, like the streamlining initiative, will require endorsements from entities outside the senate committee structure (college curriculum chairs, for example).
The OIGE has already been consulted on the Gen Ed “partials” proposal and TAAC will be asked to review and comment on the SGO-related initiatives.
The Honors Program is prepared to endorse the “graduating with distinction” proposal at the 9/18 meeting. 4.
Continued Items 4.1.
Faculty Concerns submitted through the FS Webpage - No new concerns. 4.2.
Committee Assignment Updates - Finalize Joint Committees - Specific vacancies were discussed and some appointments were finalized.
A COB representative to JAPROA is still needed along with two faculty member representatives each on the IPC and University Conduct Board.
The CASC and GEC Chairs need to assign a member as liaison to JCODL. 1

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 2
passages.text:
Pres.
Williams will correspond with those Chairs about this need.
FSEC members were asked to be prepared to make suggestions for the remaining seats on 9/24. 4.3.
Reviving work of restructured JCODL - No new report. 5.
New Items 5.1.
Develop a visitor schedule for fall FSEC meetings - suggestions for special visits include the AVP of Facilities Karl Calvo; AVP Adams regarding the NECHE accreditation review; various standing and joint committee chairs - JCSC Chair Reyes might be especially timely; a discussion with Interim Dean Mouw re: the external review of the Graduate School.
Other suggestions included Dean Libutti re: URI Cares; AVP Lavan re: JCODL and JAPROA; AAUP representatives to discuss the national AAUP report on AI; Ray Wang, the new Library Interim Dean; and CIO Fariello as the university moves toward adoption of sweeping IT policy updates. 5.2. “Weaponization” of overlap concern in newly proposed courses - A complaint about a CASC approval delay related to perceived overlap concerns was discussed and several points were made in response.
First, it was noted that proposers in Kuali must not confuse a CASC “table” or "send back” with a rejection.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 2
passages.text:
These steps are often taken when a relatively straightforward piece of additional supporting documentation is needed, and it does not generally presage rejection of a proposal.
Second, proposal quality matters and “overlap statements” must be thorough and substantiated.
Third, the CASC review is too late in the approval process for overlap concerns to be meaningfully addressed.
CASC has consistently and systematically tried to push this issue “down the chain” to the college and department curriculum committees where it can be better grappled with.
The overlap discussion highlighted for FSEC members the need for faculty to be trained in the curriculum process.
Most “information” shared in the departments about initiating proposals is simply “lore” passed down by word of mouth.
The online resources available tend to focus on the technical aspects of Kuali rather than on best practices in creating curricular proposals.
More standardized guidance is probably needed. 5.3.
How Honors sections get approved - a concern was raised to FSEC by a faculty member about a lack of vetting for H-section courses (“H” suffix courses, not HPR courses).

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 2
passages.text:
FSEC agreed they did not have enough information or examples to assemble a response and will need to circle back to the source before taking up the issue again. 5.4.
Student access to Kuali - the Student Senate has not had a CASC representative in recent years but does have a member willing to serve this year.
In order to contribute to committee work, access to Kuali would be required.
Kuali use is otherwise reserved for faculty and select administrators.
Staff will explore technological options, granting either “view only” access or access at the lowest permissions level as appropriate.
Pres.
Williams will also have an informal conversation with the student about the norms of confidentiality and circumspection in committee work. 6.
Updates 6.1.
Updates (meetings with administrators, other committee meetings) 6.1.1 Policy Reviews - APC met 9/16 - The agenda included the Research Misconduct Policy and the Conflict of Interest and Commitment Policy, both of which were approved. 2

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 3
passages.text:
The Conflict of Interest and Commitment Policy draft had contained complicated language about Honoraria which was stricken.
The VPAF’s team will subsequently work toward developing a set of procedures to address concerns about honoraria.
A policy related to course material adoption has been tagged for development this year.
FS Pres.
Williams plans to assert the Faculty Senate’s full purview in development of this policy.
In terms of other updates, Pres.
Williams noted he has requested a meeting with CIO Fariello to talk about issues like the university’s relationship to the Google “universe” and if/how/when it might detangle from it, and faculty concerns around administrator permissions in computing, among other things.
He has also corresponded with ITS about Brightspace concerns and has asked for advance notice to Senate leadership and more nuanced messaging around such tech changes/updates.
A brief update on the Centers/Institutes restructuring work was also provided.
A re-worked draft will be shared with FSEC when the document has been edited. 6.2 FOIA/APRA training for faculty - no update. 7.
New Business – Open for additional items not listed in the agenda.
Sen.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 3
passages.text:
Trimm asked about the status of the mutual defense compact that the faculty senate acted on last spring and other efforts to coordinate with public New England institutions in response to federal actions and other threats.
Pres.
Williams noted that various leadership changes and other variables led to a “quiet summer” in this regard and it is as yet unclear if coordinated activities will ramp up again in AY 2025-2026.
Sen.
Trimm noted that, in the meantime, the AAUP has promoted some initiatives aimed at networking campuses across the country and this includes a “sanctuary campus network” that is focused on dealing with ICE activity.
More information is available for those interested. 8.
Closing Remarks – Recap of decisions made, action items, and plans for the next meeting.
None 9.
Adjournment - the meeting adjourned at 11:58 am. 3

passages.text:
FSEC (Faculty Senate Executive Committee) Meeting Minutes Date: Wednesday, September 10, 2025 - Time: 10:00 AM – 12:00 noon Pastore Hall, Room 224 Remote option via ZOOM Action Items: In preparation for the Orientation meeting, FSEC members were asked to prep approx. 2 mins each regarding the standing committees to which they serve as liaison.
Staff will help finalize the slide presentations and will have sample curricular reports and a manual revision proposal ready for display.
If any FSEC members think of any crucial information that needs to be addressed, they should add a note or comment to the slides or working document.
Staff to update the UM with Chapter 5 amendments asap.
Sen.
Daniels will look into the new Faculty Concern (re: IT concerns) submitted via the webpage form and report back.
All FSEC members are asked to consider appropriate appointments to the various Joint Committees and make recommendations. 1.
Call to Order - FS President Williams called the meeting to order at 10:01.
Sens.
Daniels, Meenach, Trimm and Van Wyk were present. 2.
Minutes for Review 2.1.
FSEC Minutes of 8/27/25 - The minutes were approved as edited. 3.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 1
passages.text:
Priority Items 3.1 Sept. 11 Senate Orientation - see agenda; discuss roles, presentations, etc.
The agenda was reviewed and suggestions/instructions for presenters were offered.
There will be two slide presentations and staff will help finalize these materials.
Logistics will be emphasized (transition to webinars; attending in person, when possible; using a URI login and bringing a device for electronic voting, making a sign-in sheet available for non-members to speak, etc.). 3.2 Sept. 18 - First Regular Senate Meeting - see draft agenda - The agenda was approved as edited for posting as early as Friday 9/12/25.
It was agreed that several key pieces of anticipated legislation should be previewed at the September meeting. 3.3 Advance agenda setting for fall semester FS meetings - FSEC considered the fall reports that have become standard, either via a UM requirement or as a matter of custom and agreed that in addition, some current initiatives might make other reports appropriate and timely.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 1
passages.text:
These include a discussion with the Graduate School about their external review; a discussion with the AVP of facilities about campus improvement projects; and a conversation about the upcoming NECHE accreditation, likely led by Sue Adams.
It was suggested that these visits likely all warrant a preparatory dialog with FSEC during a regular meeting.
Other things that might rise to the senate’s attention later in the year (in addition to the as yet unknown) include the overhaul of various IT Policies (Endpoint Protection, Acceptable Use, etc.), potential promulgation of an AI Policy (which must include faculty during development), and the possible need for a new Resolution on Academic Freedom.
In a related discussion specific to the AI Policy, it was noted that a task force appears to be in place and it includes faculty, although FSEC members were unsure how appointments occurred. 3.4 Presidential Information Report on Chapter 5 Amendments (Diversity Council) - A report was offered last spring that eliminated several Presidential Committees and replaced them with a single new group to be called The Diversity Council.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 1
passages.text: The senate accepted these amendments but noted the shortcomings in the re-write (no details regarding membership, meetings, 1

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 2
passages.text:
quorums, charge, staffing, etc).
As additional details do not appear to be forthcoming, staff was advised to update the Manual accordingly in hopes that the SCLC can make progress this year in fleshing out details of the new group, with further amendments to possibly come at a later date. 4.
Continued Items 4.1.
Faculty Concerns submitted through the FS Webpage - there was one new concern pertaining to limitations placed on members of departments with local administrator access for IT purposes and related to the risks associated with deviating from the approved software list.
Sen.
Daniels, as CTI liaison, will follow up with the CIO about this (cc.
Pres.
Williams) and report back. 4.2.
Committee Assignment Updates - Standing committees are finalized.
FSEC discussed Joint Committee memberships - A couple of suggestions were made regarding vacancies and FSEC members were asked to continue to study the list (needs identified in red) and be prepared to finalize well in advance of the October senate meeting. 4.3.
Reviving work of restructured JCODL - no new report. 5.
New Items 5.1.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 2
passages.text:
FOIA/APRA Training for Faculty - some faculty have asked if they can gain access to some level of training regarding public records related to their roles at a state university.
Pres.
Williams will discuss this with the Provost’s office to determine feasibility. 5.2.
Classroom Matters: greater attention is needed to the physical set-up as a benefit or drawback to different instructional choices.
The need for FSEC to interface with a Facilities Administrator has already been discussed.
The Space Allocation Committee and Joint Classroom Steering Committee both have representatives from that office as members.
An idea for a Senate Forum with JCSC and SAC to give senators a chance to voice concerns about space needs was floated.
FSEC noted they may wish to confer with the JCSC Chair Reyes in advance. 6.
Updates 6.1.
Updates (meetings with administrators, other committee meetings) 6.1.1 Policy Reviews - Research Policies: The comment period on the Financial Conflict of Interest in Research and Conflict of Commitment in Research policies has closed.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 2
passages.text:
The next APC meeting is 9/16 and the Research Misconduct Policy is on that agenda for action along with the aforementioned. 6.2 Other - RE: AI Policy Development, the FS President and VP met with AAUP representatives about the report on AI issued by the national office.
FS leadership’s concern is that AAUP’s understandable focus on the intrusion of AI into curricular matters might mean that all the other big-picture concerns about AI might go unaddressed by faculty.
Local leaders agreed to get more up to speed on the report itself and other ramifications of AI and reconvene at a future date.
UCAS is being re-branded as URI CARES (the acronym standing for the Center for Career and Experiential Learning; Academic Enhancement Center; Retention and Academic Success; Exploratory Studies (which includes undergraduate advising and First Year Experience); and Student-Athlete Support Services).
Faculty have been keen to see the use of “college” disappear from the UCAS mission and this reorganization under a directorship seems to make sense.
The community will be hearing more in the coming days. 2

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 3
passages.text: The FS President and VP have learned that the traditional schedule for budget hearings suggests that Senate leadership should be prepared to submit a formal budget request by December. In a recent meeting with the Vice Provost, FS Pres. Williams noted that the lapse in the university‘s membership in AACU (American Association of Colleges and Universities) is unacceptable given the challenges facing the humanities and social sciences and the need for exposure to model general education programs as the university approaches a reaccrediting year. This should be a university-wide value supported at the university level. 7. Report of the Coordinator – Several senators, especially from among the newly elected, have reached out to express concern about meeting attendance, noting that teaching obligations impede their ability to attend full meetings in person. While the UM is clear that attendance at monthly meetings is mandatory, the FSEC agreed that more and better messaging regarding this obligation is called for. It was also noted that a legitimate scheduling issue does exist in that fall teaching schedules are generally already set by the time colleges hold their elections. The idea of moving the election cycle earlier in the year was discussed. It was further noted that there are additional structural timing issues affecting the senate in that committee chairs are typically named in August, after teaching assignments for fall semester are well-established and it is too late to find per course instructors. This is likely part of the reason why so few chairs receive course releases in fulfillment of their mandated adjustment to regular duties. 8. New Business – Open for additional items not listed in the agenda. None 9. Adjournment - the meeting adjourned at 11:59 am. 3

FSEC (Faculty Senate Executive Committee) Meeting Minutes Date: Wednesday, September 24, 2025 - Time: 10:00 AM – 12:00 noon Pastore Hall, Room 224 - Remote option via ZOOM Action Items: FSEC needs to check back in with Jack Humphrey (re: 7-week and 14-week cross enrollment accommodation in Ecampus and technical solutions to build out the 2nd grade option proposal, if approved).
SGO related legislation needs to be customized depending on the timeline his team determines is workable.
FSEC members shall help round out Joint Committee memberships and come up with three people to serve on the Nominating Committee (from among members whose terms are expiring in May).
Staff will alert relevant committee chairs of initial reporting responsibilities coming up in October and November.
Staff will also ensure that brief summaries of standard curricular reports are on-screen during senate meetings.
Chairs of these committees are to be reminded that oral remarks on these reports should be kept to a bare minimum.
Pres.
Williams will invite VP Benson and/or AVP Calvo to FSEC on 10/8 to discuss facility upgrades and projects around campus and Pres.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 1
passages.text:
Williams will arrange for an administrator to introduce legislation pertaining to eliminating the budget impact statement requirement. 1.
Call to Order - FS President Williams called the meeting to order at 10:01.
VP Preisser and Sens.
Daniels, Meenach, Trimm and Van Wyk were present. 2.
Guest: Jack Humphrey, Sr.
Assoc.
Director, Enrollment Services - Associate Director Humphrey joined the meeting to talk about the FSEC proposal regarding the second grade option that was introduced to the senate on 9/18.
The hope was that the Ecampus system would accommodate automation of a replacement grade at any point in a student’s enrollment, but this is not easily accomplished and implementation of any changes to Sections 8.33.30 - 8.33.32 of the university manual could be delayed.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 1
passages.text:
Complicating factors include: a number of individual programs have their own restrictions and special rules which would require individual attention; there may be situations where it does not benefit (or even harms) a student if the grade replacement is automatic; technical complexities are especially problematic for re-admitted students; if students are re-taking courses three or more times, there should be notice to/permission from department chairs and/or program directors.
A related conversation about the university’s migration of certain business process software took place, but it appears that any transition to a new student information system is some years away, so solving the subject problem in the current Peoplesoft platform needs to be a priority.
The FSEC proposal, as introduced, speculated that implementation could occur for fall, 2026, but AD Humphrey explained timelines for registration and catalog publication that could preclude hitting this target.
Fall, 2027 may be more realistic.
He is meeting with his team and IT staffers soon and hopes to provide a practicable timeframe sometime thereafter.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 1
passages.text:
Assuming the senate dockets a vote on the bill in November, 2025, the legislation will need to include language about the date it will take effect.
Addressing another item of common interest, AD Humphrey provided an update on the calendar alignment project (URI Online with the traditional calendar) that started last year.
A “phase 2” of that project still requires senate action.
The creation of sessions within terms that would enable students to concurrently enroll in both 7-week and 14-week courses still needs to be implemented, and this effort is complicated by the fact that once the enrollment platform accommodates cross-enrollment, the billing, financial aid and other business platforms will also 1

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 2
passages.text:
require adjustments.
It had been anticipated that this change would be fully rolled out in fall, 2027 but it may not be finalized until fall, 2028.
FS President Williams noted that given the complexity of the project from a budget and administration perspective, FS leaders will need to talk to administrators about where this project now lies in terms of priorities. 3.
Minutes - Minutes of the 9/10/25 and 9/17/25 meetings - The minutes were approved as edited. 4.
Priority Items 4.1 Meeting Re-cap - Sept. 18 FS Meeting - see agenda - FSEC members have received favorable feedback from faculty and administrators alike about the efficiency, effectiveness, and general tone of the meeting.
Procedural next steps for some of the legislation introduced, including timelines for other committee reviews, were discussed.
The curricular streamlining initiative, in particular, was discussed and it was noted that the college curriculum chairs and FSEC members need access to the proposed spreadsheet asap so that Appendix E language can be developed and so that feedback from appropriate units can be received.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 2
passages.text:
Also, it was noted that one of the programs approved as part of a curricular report may need further attention.
FS President Williams, with support from Sen Meenach, will follow up with the proposers to determine a course of action. 4.2 Advance Planning for October Senate meeting - see draft agenda - The draft agenda was reviewed and it was noted that it is a very full agenda.
A number of committee reports are required at the October meeting per the university manual, but it was agreed that these should be essentially split in half with some committees reporting in October and others in November.
Staff will advise Chairs as appropriate.
There was some concern that the senate may need to revert back to a “consent agenda” if curricular reports cannot be kept brief.
Staff will plan to provide a summary sheet slide for each report and liaisons should remind committee chairs that they need only say 1-2 sentences about each report before taking questions.
Pres.
Williams will remind senators of their obligation to review these matters in detail ahead of each meeting and, where possible, pass concerns or questions along in advance so they might be resolved before eating up meeting time.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 2
passages.text:
Key action items will include approving the Joint Committees memberships list and forming a three-member Nominating Committee.
FSEC members were advised to brainstorm nominees for next time. 5.
Continued Items 5.1 Faculty Concerns submitted through the FS Webpage - Four new concerns had been submitted.
It was agreed that the FS officers will bring up a parking-related concern with relevant administrators.
Regarding a question about the federal landscape, FSEC considered pushing additional communications highlights regarding the senate’s efforts in this regard and/or asking the VP RED or Provost to provide a brief update on faculty-specific issues during a future senate meeting.
Regarding course modalities, FSEC agreed that more messaging around the senate’s work on this front last year might be in order, especially to benefit new senators and faculty who were not involved in those efforts.
Finally, it seems there is some misunderstanding surrounding the “Concerns” form available on the website.
Pres.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 2
passages.text:
Williams will remind senators at the next meeting that it is available for the use of all faculty and not just those in the senate. 5.2 Committee Assignment Updates - Finalize Joint Committees - Only a few seats remain unresolved.
FSEC members were encouraged to review the list, which highlights current needs, and be prepared to finalize nominations at the next meeting. 6.
New Items 6.1 Scheduling VP Abby Benson and AVP Calvo to visit FSEC re: Facilities - Pres.
Williams noted a recent facilities presentation at the PSC meeting was very interesting and definitely something faculty 2

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 3
passages.text:
would want and need to hear about.
Pres.
Williams will invite the VP and AVP to an FSEC meeting first (tentatively 10/8), with the understanding that a briefing at the full senate should follow. 6.2 Draft language to delete Budget Impact Statement from proposed program review i.
Find current UM Chapter 8, Section III language here - There were no objections to the draft language but it was noted that the issues surrounding the requirement arose via administrators.
It thus seems appropriate that the proposal be introduced by an ex officio member (preferably the VP of Administration and Finance).
The desired timeframe would be to take action on the language in November. 7.
Updates 7.1 Updates (meetings with administrators, other committee meetings) FS Pres.
Williams is meeting with the current University Ombud to discuss ways of moving forward with the permanent restructuring of the office and the effort to secure a new Ombud.
Pres.
Williams recently met with AVP Libutti about the overhaul and rebranding of UCAS as URI CARES.
The CBUM and its Chair, Sen.
Mitkowski will need to be involved in this transition as multiple sections of the University Manual will be affected.
Pres.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 3
passages.text:
Williams also recently met with the Provost and Vice Provost Adams regarding restructuring the university’s approach to Centers and Institutes and they hope to refine a draft for distribution soon.
Pres.
Williams attended the President’s Stewardship Council meeting yesterday and noted that several important matters were discussed, including: trouble-shooting H-1B visa issues; the possibility of a government shutdown and the need for all PI’s to focus on processing grant drawdowns asap; and the changing landscape for federal grants and projects generally.
Other matters included a “shout-out” from University President Parlange regarding the successful start to the Faculty Senate’s legislative year and an introduction to the NECHE reaccrediting process that is kicking off for conclusion in 2027.
Other updates included big changes that are coming to the bookstore as a new vendor has been secured for operations there.
Faculty should pay close attesntion to course material offerings during this transition, especially if they are pressured to move toward “for a fee” versions of resources they currently use for free.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 3
passages.text:
Faculty may also want to pay close attention to changes coming in the HR realm as the state migrates to new software and systems.
Apparently, a roughly one-month black-out of new hiring functionality is imminent and this could affect many departments and offices. 7.2 Reviving work of restructured JCODL - tabled 8.
Report of the Coordinator – Sen.
Preisser has offered to help draft the new Appendix E as the curricular streamlining initiative moves forward.
Staff will ensure he and other relevant parties (CASC, etc.) have access to working documents.
A very preliminary draft to new language related to using “college liaisons” to improve shared governance at the college level will also be shared so that FSEC members can contribute.
That effort began last spring and seems ready to be revisited. 9.
New Business – Open for additional items not listed in the agenda.
None 10.
Closing Remarks – Recap of decisions made, action items, and plans for the next meeting.
None 11.
Adjournment - the meeting adjourned at 12:02 pm. 3

FSEC (Faculty Senate Executive Committee) Meeting Minutes Date: Wednesday, October 01, 2025 - Time: 10:00 AM – 12:00 noon Pastore Hall, Room 224 Remote option via ZOOM Action Items: Staff will recruit an unassigned senator to serve on CASC asap to fill a vacancy.
Staff will summarize the proposed travel path for all FSEC-introduced legislation so that the FS Pres. and committee liaisons can attend to timely reviews.
FSEC members should be prepared to finalize the list of Joint Committee appointments next week.
In preparation for the 10/29 meeting in Green Hall, FSEC members should consider and be prepared to suggest agenda items or talking points on 10/8.
Members are encouraged to continue reviewing the Graduate School report for further discussion.
Staff will circle back with the Provost’s Chief of Staff to see if UM Chapter 2 revisions can move forward.
Pres.
Williams will create a list of “required syllabus statements” and provide to TAAC so the committee might assist the administration in creating an online repository of such statements and enumerating best practices regarding their accessibility to students.
Pres.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 1
passages.text:
Williams will correspond with Enrollment Services (looping in the CASC and CoEd) regarding the decision to grant Enrollment Services the temporary authority to update credit fields for specific CoED classes ,with the understanding that the College will bring a formal proposal forward asap (effective Fall 2026) to permanently resolve the “forced overload” issue. 1.
Call to Order - FS President Williams called the meeting to order at 10:01.
VP Preisser and Sens.
Daniels, Meenach, Trimm and Van Wyk were present. 2.
Minutes - Minutes of the 9/24/25 FSEC meeting were approved unanimously as edited.
The 9/18/25 Faculty Senate meeting minutes were approved with one abstention. 3.
Priority Items 3.1 CASC member needed due to senator resignation - A nominee was suggested and staff will reach out to determine their willingness and ability to serve. 3.2 Ensuring all proposed legislation is formally approved by FSEC and distributed to relevant committees i.
Gen Ed Partials (UM 8.20.12 - 14) - Fully approved by FSEC on 8/27.
Scheduled for senate vote 11/20/25.
The following committees shall review: General Education (GEC); Constitution, By-Laws and University Manual (CBUM).

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 1
passages.text:
Committees should provide written comments and/or a record of a vote to recommend legislation as-is to the full senate by 11/3/25.
Courtesy reviews of the draft shall be extended to the University President and Provost and to the OIGE. ii.
Graduating with Distinction (UM 8.22.40) - Fully approved by FSEC 10/1/25.
Scheduled for senate vote 11/20/25.
The following committees shall review: Teaching, Advising and Admissions (TAAC); Constitution, By-Laws and University Manual (CBUM).
Committees should provide written comments and/or a record of a vote to recommend legislation as-is to the full senate by 11/3/25.
Courtesy reviews of the draft shall be extended to the University President and Provost, Office of Enrollment Services, and the Honors Program. iii.
Curricular Streamlining - Spreadsheet approved by FSEC.
UM Appendix E language approved as draft 10/1/25 with caveat that Sen.
Preisser and staff finalize and make available next week.
Draft must be reviewed by CASC, GEC, the Graduate Council, and CBUM.
Courtesy reviews by all college deans and curriculum committees should also be extended, in addition to 1

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 2

the offices of the President and Provost and Enrollment Services.

A stated goal in the report was to significantly increase graduate enrollment but faculty are right to be skeptical about how this might come to pass.
Many departments have experienced declines in their full-time faculty lines and wonder where the resources will come from to support this increase.
Other suggestions, like eliminating the Graduate Council’s role in the course approval process seem to run counter to the long-standing principle of faculty involvement in curricular matters.
Assertions about “branding” also seem misguided as graduate programs tend to attract their students via college- or department- specific outreach and not through an overarching administrative unit.
A number of other practical considerations would seem to limit the report’s stated aspirations.
These include recent decreases and eliminations in federal funds (and unpredictable access to existing funds), and limits on international students’ ability to access programs.

Vice Provost for Advancement of Teaching and Learning, and Assoc.
Professor of Education Shane Tutwiler, Chair, Joint Committee for Academic Program Review and Outcomes Assessment (JAPROA) joined the meeting.
AVP Lavan started off by outlining the work of the ATL office, noting that it supports the work of committees like JAPROA and JCODL in an advisory and consultative way.
Some history and background was provided on the work of prior iterations of these committees and by former key staffers in the ATL office.
AVP Lavan and Chair Tutwiler stressed that the faculty-led committees retain the authority to conduct reviews within well-established processes, but the scope of that authority seems to confuse some faculty members.
It was noted that JAPROA is a newer committee that only experienced its first full operational year in AY24-25.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 1
passages.text:
Committee members too struggled with the line between “advising” and “approving.” In short, when an undergraduate program is proposed by a department or college, the outcomes assessment portion of that proposal is assigned to JAPROA, which undertakes its work with assistance from the ATL office.
Also, the office has been developing a “Manual” or handbook that outlines the academic program review process which should become a valuable resource for departments undergoing reviews.
Chair Tutwiler noted that the guidance is drawn from Chapter 8 of the University Manual and the committee is keenly interested in simplifying the process to make it easier for departments to undertake.
He considers the work of his committee to be invaluable in guiding metaprocesses and ensuring that the university, through all aggregated academic units, continues to learn from self-study and reflection, and therefore improves and succeeds.
While JAPROA’s role involves providing feedback on outcomes assessments, they can only adopt and forward recommendations, but the final decisions always rest in the departments.

Now that the university has sunset its administrative committee responsible for providing guidance and advice during the transition, it is unclear what how the BAC should focus its efforts.
It has no administrative counterpart and no clear nexus of cooperation with key administrators.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 1
passages.text:
Past President Walls noted that models from peer institutions were used in developing the legislation that created the BAC.
Faculty-forward institutions like Tufts have a long history of having a permanent, standing committee responsible for weighing in on budget matters.
Given that implementation details of the new budget model remain unavailable, it was agreed that new processes and procedures still hold the potential to negatively impact faculty (through program consolidations and other potential outcomes).
It thus seems important to keep the committee active.
It was noted that a retired faculty member for many years tracked revenues by source, especially state support for the university, and university expenditures.
Continuation of such tracking might be a worthwhile task for a committee of faculty.
The Committee also serves to act as a second set of eyes on decision making and is a formal body that can hear faculty concerns and advocate on their behalf.
Uncertainty around the person or office that should serve as a contact or administration representative for the Committee has been a source of frustration.

Relocating MPS to College of Education - Continued to next week. ii.
Other - Most FSEC members attended a meeting last week with representatives of the Public Safety Advisory Committee and were reassured by Chief Jagoda’s approach to working with local, state, and federal law enforcement.
They also addressed other issues such as speeding tickets on campus. 7.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 3
passages.text:

Trimm provided a draft document for review pertaining to copyright notices, as relates to required syllabus statements.
Some edits were made in real time and some concerns were offered for further consideration.
FSEC members noted the “clock is ticking” in that the Provost's office will be communicating with faculty soon with guidance on required syllabus statements and this may or may not be ready in time for incorporation.
It is important that the document be reviewed by relevant committees and administrators and the language needs to be correct and supportable, even if that takes a little longer.
Sen.
Trimm was authorized to pass the draft to the TAAC and to share with other administrators in ATL, Student Affairs, etc. as needed.

Williams will share it with the Provost’s office with a request that the Office of General Counsel also conduct a review. 9.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 3

FSEC (Faculty Senate Executive Committee) Meeting Minutes Date: Wednesday, December 10, 2025 - Time: 10:00 AM – 12:00 noon Pastore Hall, Room 224 - Remote option via ZOOM Action Items: Pres.
Williams will liaise with relevant parties (ACC, enrollment services, student advising) to secure a recommendation on resolving the AY 27-28 calendar issue (lack of an advising day preceding the start of classes).
Sen Preisser will meet with FS staff next week about recruiting a graduate student worker, organizing information around college by-laws and planning related action items, and other timely matters.
Pres.
Williams will liaise with CBUM with instructions for the committee to draft and recommend language updating Sec. 8.20.73 pertaining to transfer credits and Certificates.
Sen.
Trimm will follow up with the FS Specialist and the CASC Chair about next steps in standardizing catalog descriptions of programs.
Sen.
Van Wyk will act as point-person on transmitting a final ‘response document’ to the SCLC regarding their diversity subcommittees proposal.
Sen.
Van Wyk will also draft talking points regarding recruiting survey design experts from among the faculty (for discussion by FSEC in January).
Pres.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 1
passages.text:
Williams will share CBUM’s concerns about UM Chapter 2 with VP Adams. 1.
Call to Order - Pres.
Williams called the meeting to order at 10:00 AM.
VP Preisser and Senators Meenach, Van Wyk, Trimm and Daniels and Past President Walls were present. 2.
Minutes for approval - The following were approved as edited. i.
Minutes of the 11/19/25 FSEC meeting and the 12/3/25 FSEC meeting. 3.
Priority Items 3.1 Meeting Prep - 12/11/25 Faculty Senate Meeting - FSEC members reviewed the agenda and discussed presentation roles, slide assembly, and time-sensitive announcements that should be part of Pres.
Williams’ address. 3.2 AY 27-28 Calendar Issue - missing advising day - The calendar for AY 27-28 was approved some time ago, but questions were raised this week about the fact that a fall advising day is not included.
It was noted that, given the lateness of the Labor Day holiday in September 2027, it was an exceptionally difficult year for designing a calendar.
Some FSEC members noted the lack of an advising day could seriously affect new students and they advocated for finding a way to reinsert it in the calendar.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 1
passages.text:
Should the university decide to add the advising day, thereby delaying the start of classes by one day, some options, like eliminating the Columbus Day or day before Thanksgiving holiday, do exist.
FSEC agreed to re-assign the 27-28 calendar to the ACC to develop a recommendation to resolve the issue. 3.3 Future Legislation Update i.
Establishing College Liaisons - FSEC is still waiting for reactions to the proposal from college deans.
For future discussion. ii.
College By-Laws - An initial step involves figuring which schools and colleges actually have by-laws.
Last year, FS Pres.
Walls started compiling all by-laws documents but staff is unsure if his collection is exhaustive.
A number of questions exist around the senate’s role in the by-laws initiative - like the extent of purview the senate has, if any, over what happens in the colleges, and how the mechanisms for adoption, maintenance, and enforcement of by-laws actually work.
FSEC members agreed that if UM language is to be introduced regarding college governance structures via by-laws, it must be led by faculty, rather than by the administration.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 1
passages.text: During the discussion, it was noted that there are some avenues of recourse for faculty who might currently 1

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 2
passages.text:
be affected by either a lack of clear by-laws or by any given college’s failure to honor their by-laws.
Senior, tenured faculty should take up these issues directly with their deans; the office of the Ombuds can be consulted; or a conversation with the Provost can be had.
FSEC will continue its work on this issue. 3.4 JCODL next steps - continued discussion forthcoming as a draft becomes available. 3.5 Amend UM 8.20.73 (Request from Past FS President Mike Rice) - FSEC members agreed with Sen.
Rice’s assertion that current language is overdue for updating.
The matter will be assigned to CBUM to draft something that might be introduced at the January senate meeting. 3.6 Proposal to update attendance policy to account for special medical needs (inquiry from Sen.
Martin; see UM 8.51.15).
FSEC was made aware of a situation where a student with special medical needs does not feel accommodated by the attendance policies.
It was noted that the typical route to resolution involves students approaching their assistant dean who creates medically necessary exceptions. res.
Williams will reach out to Sen.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 2
passages.text:
Martin for additional details and then reach out to VP Reynolds to see if her office might issue some reminders to faculty about best practices. 3.7 CASC proposal to standardize program descriptions and program requirements - Sen.
Trimm noted that as the university approaches reaccreditation, catalog descriptions of both programs and courses become even more important.
The CASC would like to see increased standardization, especially in program descriptions.
It has discussed pushing a template or other resources to ensure that all adequate descriptors of programs (credits and courses required, for example) are listed.
It was agreed that CASC and the Graduate Council could push a clear set of standards that could be implemented for all new programs; existing programs would need to be brought into conformity as revisions or updates are made.
Sen.
Trimm will follow up with staff and the CASC Chair about next steps. 4.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 2
passages.text:
Continued Items 4.1 Faculty Concerns submitted through the FS Webpage - No new concerns. 4.2 Chapter 2 revision – current 11/2/25 version - Broad agreement with administrators has been reached about some key aspects of the chapter (for example, the university president as the conduit of all official communications between the BOT and the university community generally).
Pres.
Williams reported the draft is thus inching closer to a presentation date with the full senate.
FSEC awaits a final, presentation-quality draft. 4.3 Recruiting Survey Design Experts - Sen.
Van Wyk will have a set of talking points for discussion in January. 4.4 SCLC proposal re.
Subcommittees - Sen.
Van Wyk drafted a response to the proposal which FSEC agreed should be sent to the committee Chair on behalf of FSEC.
FSEC members will review and comment on the draft response and Sen.
Van Wyk will act as point-person on transmitting the final document. 4.5 Committee Assignment Updates, if any - Joint Committees - As part of the 12/11/25 FS agenda, the senate will be asked to approve a new member of JAPROA from CELS.
No other appointments have been made.
CBUM has a new Chair following Sen.
Mitkowski’s resignation. 5.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 2
passages.text:
Updates 5.1 Updates (meetings with administrators, other committee meetings) - Pres.
Williams met with CBUM as they reviewed legislation pertaining to the budget impact statement reviews for degrees and the so-called ‘third attempts’ at courses.
Some comments on the third attempts bill have been 2

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 3
passages.text:
incorporated and there were no changes recommended to the budget statements bill.
The committee also provided feedback on the college by-laws initiative and the updates to UM Chapter 2.
Pres.
Williams will bring their concerns to Vice Provost Adams.
Weekly meetings between VP Adams and Pres.
Williams continue, and other topics of discussion recently included advancing the work aimed at modernizing the office of the Ombuds.
The university President’s office is being asked to provide a ‘punchlist’ of outstanding issues so that the SCLC and others involved in that initiative can wrap up their work.
Other topics covered in the most recent meeting with VP Adams included cross enrollment between the traditional calendar and the online accelerated one, the use of AI in Starfish, the organizational structure of the senate office following the departure of Vice Provost Bodah, some curricular matters contained in recent reports, and the senate’s participation in URI Day at the Statehouse.
Pres.
Williams noted that the recent PSC meeting centered around KPI’s and he had raised some questions specific to metrics related to articles published in journals within the top 10% of cited journals.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 3
passages.text:
His concern had been that this metric potentially excluded non-STEM faculty.
He has since received additional information that allays some of those fears for arts and humanities faculty but concerns about the use of the metrics are not completely resolved.
Other metrics, like PhD conferrals, also had a lack of clarity and, according to current metrics, it does not seem that, in most cases, the targets can be met. i.
APC Meeting - 12/9/25 - a key policy under review at the December meeting was the Sexual Misconduct policy.
Faculty noted some implications for both pedagogy and research for such a policy and FSEC members agreed a broader conversation is likely needed. ii.
Relocating MPS to College of Education - Questions remain about the specifics of this proposal.
Key questions include how both funds and KPI’s are assigned.
All departments, including those outside COEdu, should receive both credit for their academic contribution to the program as well as actual funds proportionate to their contribution. ii.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 3
passages.text:
Copyrights policy/Required Syllabus Statements - As FSEC has not yet received feedback from the OGC, the start of the spring semester is expected to see messaging from the Provost’s office that mirrors what faculty received in the fall.
It is hoped that an approved (by the General Counsel’s office) copyright statement will be ready for Fall 2026. iii.
Centers and Institutes -- the matter of KPI credit - this issue was discussed briefly as part of item 3.1 on this agenda.
The issue of granting KPI credit to all participating colleges and not just the host college continues to be problematic for those centers and institutes that cut across organizational units. 6.
Report of the Coordinator - Staff noted the ongoing need to hire a graduate student for office help and updated the group on the office’s efforts to archive Senate records in the digital commons. 7.
New Business – Open for additional items not listed in the agenda.
None 8.
Adjournment - the meeting adjourned at 11:45 am. 3

passages.text:
FSEC (Faculty Senate Executive Committee) Meeting Minutes Date: Wednesday, October 22, 2025 - Time: 10:00 AM – 12:00 noon Pastore Hall, Room 224 - Remote option via ZOOM Action Items: FSEC members should feel free to add topics for discussion before the 10/29 meeting in Green Hall.
FS Pres.
Williams will continue to follow up regarding joint committee appointments and staff will issue formal appointment letters for the assignments finalized at the 10/16 FS meeting.
President Williams raised questions pertaining to the roles of SLOAA, JAPROA and College Business Officers that will need to be resolved before an amendment regarding eliminating required budget impact statements can move forward.
He will reach out to the ATL office for answers. 1.
Call to Order - FS President Williams called the meeting to order at 10:01.
VP Preisser and Sens.
Daniels, Meenach, Trimm and Van Wyk were present, along with ex officio member Ted Walls. 2.
Minutes for approval - Minutes of the 10/15/25 meeting - The minutes were approved as edited. 3.
Guests at 11:15 AM: Dan Moos, Chief of Staff to Vice President for Administration and Finance Benson, and Karl Calvo - AVP Facilities.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 1
passages.text:
AVP Calvo offered a slide presentation explaining how his office is structured into divisions dealing with long range planning and design, current operations, small projects, and large-scale construction.
Major projects planned include construction of additional undergraduate dorms, on-going improvements at the Bay Campus, and a new bio-medical sciences building, among others.
Of particular interest to FSEC were the future of the University Library and the need for additional graduate- and international-student housing.
Other issues the conversation touched upon included parking, lighting and other infrastructure improvements (like water treatment facilities and re-paving).
Google Maps layers of the university’s geographic information system were briefly discussed and it was noted that better mapping and better messaging about maps available would help address needs like understanding ease of access for members of the disabilities community and things like gender neutral restroom availability.
Classroom issues were also discussed, especially appropriateness of available spaces in relation to teaching style.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 1
passages.text:
This process is complex and involves Dean-level requests for fit-outs of specific spaces, but also typically involves the JCSC, building managers, IT Services and CMS.
While the process may or may not have been well-coordinated in the past, AVP Calvo encouraged concerned faculty to reach out with specific concerts about their instructional spaces going forward.
Questions were asked about the wrap-up of the consultative process which led to the recently adopted Campus Master Plan, and whether all members of consultative committees had an opportunity to express their opinions of the draft plan.
Specifically, a final meeting of the committee was never convened and it is not clear whether originally planned broader ‘testing’ of the plan with campus groups as outlined by Sasaki happened.
It was conceded that given the outside consultants involved in the project, coordination may not have been as robust as it could have been and AVP Calvo offered to inquire about why the final meeting was not convened..
The conversation ended with a discussion of the library.
It was noted that faculty have grave concerns about the library’s current condition and its future.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 1
passages.text:
AVP Calvo explained that the library’s location has been problematic from the start in that it was built over a stream and this has created ongoing issues with moisture in the building.
Several small projects are planned in the near term (HVAC, air handlers, roof - to deal with features/equipment that have reached the end of their useful life), but the university is also planning a $45 million renovation which will be a longer term project, perhaps in conjunction with the state archives. 1

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 2
passages.text:
4.
Priority Items 4.1 Relocating MPS to College of Education - see program - The program was created by the Graduate School and is offered through URI Online and is not located within any other degree granting college.
As the program is now ready to graduate its first class, a question arose about which college would host these graduates.
It was agreed administratively that for this December’s graduation event, the graduates could participate through the College of Education but a permanent solution is needed.
A proposal has been filed in Kuali to formalize the MPS in the College of Education.
FSEC members noted that the program involves Certificates from at least five colleges and many more departments so it is difficult to understand how the CoEdu was chosen over the other colleges involved.
The Executive Committee also had concerns related to the level of faculty control over this program, and how its revenue generation will be allocated.
For example, if housed wholly in Education, is the program a budget line therein, or does its revenue go to URI Online, or does it get divided among the other colleges that manage the certificates leading to this degree?

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 2
passages.text:
Could it lead to more faculty lines in Education?
FSEC members agreed much more information is needed beyond that provided in the Kuali submission and the Grad Council and other reviewers can be expected to have similar questions.
Pres.
Williams will correspond with the proposers to solicit more detail and to offer a heads-up that heavy scrutiny by faculty and the senate might be expected. 4.2 Green Hall Meeting Prep (10/29) - discuss agenda items - suggested so far: the Graduate School Report; the Diversity Council; IT/System Administrator permissions; ICE on campus and the need for a proactive policy; the Federal Compact; the rebranding of UCAS.
Pres.
Williams noted he and VP Preisser met with administrators yesterday and addressed some of these issues.
Other ideas for the joint conversation included a possible joint resolution on the Fannon Family gift, and the on-going effort to consolidate the 7- and 14-week calendars.
FSEC members should feel free to add topics to this possible agenda between now and 10/29. 4.3 Meeting Recap October 16 Senate meeting - see agenda - The meeting was generally efficient and productive.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 2
passages.text:
The informational reports that were not delivered can be held until November.
FSEC agreed that other committee reports can wait until mid-year or as needed. i.
Status of four proposed Bills - The FSEC proposals are all expected to move forward, with some possible tweaks based on feedback from senators and review committees. ii.
FSEC role at senate meetings - FSEC agreed that in the interest of time, Executive Committee members should defer to other senators during discussion/debate at senate meetings except when explanatory comments about items being discussed are required for clarity. 4.4 Set weekly meeting schedule for spring semester - Starting in January, FSEC meetings will be held on Wednesdays from 11 - 1. 5.
Continued Items 5.1 Faculty Concerns submitted through the FS Webpage - New Concerns - Staff will request gluten-free items at senate receptions.
Pres.
Williams will work with CTI Chair Wallace and liaison Daniels to address related IT issues referenced by submitters.
FS Leadership will ask for better information about gender neutral restroom availability to be made available to the community, and that they consider the need for additional such facilities.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 2
passages.text:
Some faculty took umbrage at the request that they donate time “off the clock” to events like Homecoming and asked that the administration be reminded that work-life balance should be part of the community’s culture.
This led to a broader 2

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 3
passages.text:
discussion about faculty service generally and the fact that it is still not valued by the administration as it should be.
It was noted that some departments do a better job at fostering a culture of service than others and this often relates to some degree to the size of the department and the resources available. 5.2 Committee Assignment Updates - Finalize Joint Committees - Most assignments have been made but inquiries are still outstanding for a couple of seats.
FS Pres.
Williams will continue to follow up and staff will issue formal appointment letters. 5.3 Elimination of Budget Impact Statement Requirement - In drafting the change to UM 8.85.14, President Williams noted some related questions pertaining to the roles of SLOAA, JAPROA and College Business Officers that will need to be resolved before this amendment is discussed on the floor.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 3
passages.text:
He will reach out to the ATL office and if answers are forthcoming, this legislation may still be introduced in November. 5.4 Might we also introduce legislation to either A) prevent students from repeating the same class more than twice (i.e., taking it more than three times) at URI; or B) require 'permission of instructor' for the second retake and beyond?
These issues were discussed through the lens of recent conversations around bills to modify the Second Grade Option UM language.
They are separate and distinct but related.
Introducing independent legislation dealing with the third (or more) attempt at a course seems advised.
There is a perception that “permission of instructor” is often the solution but there is still a coding burden that will fall upon Enrollment Services to carve out exceptions for dissertations, independent studies, etc.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 3
passages.text:
Other issues will also need to be sorted (transfering in credit for a third attempt from another institution, for example) but FSEC will continue to discuss with the intention of advancing legislation later this year. 5.5 New library matters - Discussion ensued on a variety of challenges currently faced by the University Libraries. 5.6 Honors Program modification and HPR 403 Honors Reflections new course - Pres.
Williams briefed FSEC on the contents of two proposals recently put forward by the Honors Program. 6.
Updates 6.1 Updates (meetings with administrators, other committee meetings) i.
JCODL Updates - Meeting with relevant parties on 10/16/25 - The draft legislation was reviewed and is still being revised. ii.
Other - The FS Pres. and VP met with the University President, Provost and Vice Provost on 10/21.
Of note, they discussed: issues around the 7- and 14-week calendar merger and it was noted that the 7-week accelerated calendar is primarily a graduate-level option so FSEC’s concerns about concurrent enrollment by undergraduates may be minimized.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 3
passages.text:
There was a continuing conversation about the Diversity Council and there was agreement that safety and transparency need to be balanced as decisions about the quality and quantity of this committee’s outreach are made. 7.
Report of the Coordinator – None. 8.
New Business – Open for additional items not listed in the agenda. 8.1 Chapter 2 revision -- draft supplied by Green Hall; current text - FSEC members should review and be prepared to discuss next time.
A redline version can be requested but the document might be more easily digested as is. 9.
Closing Remarks – Recap of decisions made, action items, and plans for the next meeting.
None. 10.
Adjournment - The meeting adjourned at 12:20 pm. 3

FSEC (Faculty Senate Executive Committee) Meeting Minutes Date: Friday, January 16, 2026 - Time: 12:30 pm – 2:30 pm Fully Remote Meeting via ZOOM Action Items: Staff will create a QR code to display at the senate meeting for the BAC budget survey.
Also for the 1/22 senate meeting, Pres.
Williams will add a brief description of the decision-making process around the December final exams changes to his announcements and offer a brief opportunity for discussion.
Pres.
Williams will seek clarification regarding the composition of the Library Dean search committee.
Pres.
Williams will come up with some examples of non-curricular offerings to provide during the discussion of JCODL updates.
Pres.
Williams will discuss the need for better contingency planning campus-wide at his next meeting with the Vice Provost. 1.
Call to Order - Pres.
Williams called the meeting to order at 12:33 AM.
VP Preisser and Senators Meenach, Van Wyk, Trimm and Daniels were present. 2.
Minutes for approval - The following minutes were approved as edited. i.
Minutes of the 12/17/25 FSEC meeting. ii.
Minutes of the 12/11/25 FS meeting 3.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 1
passages.text:
Priority Items (20 minutes) 3.1 For Action - January 22, 2026 senate meeting - Following extensive discussion, the agenda was approved for posting.
Main discussion points included: recruitment and eligibility for the FS VP position as the election is coming up in February; all legislation docketed for action; presentation logistics related to the UM Chapter 2 administrative report (introduction only); and the proposal by the Calendar Committee to rectify the Advising Day problem in the AY 27-28 calendar.
It was agreed that some extra time might need to be dedicated to the Honors Program discussion.
The TAAC has recommended the Kuali proposal as it stands and the presentation is expected to be fairly detailed.
FSEC expects the matter to be introduced at the January meeting and voted on in February, but if senators are comfortable proceeding, it is eligible for action on 1/22.
The TAAC also plans to put forward a recommendation regarding syllabus statements.
It does not affect the UM and is not a bill but should be formalized in some way, perhaps as a Resolution.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 1
passages.text:
If time allows, FSEC would like to discuss the College Liaisons proposal and the JCODL updates under new business. 3.2 Advance Planning - URI Day at the Statehouse - (3/26/26) - The goal of the event is not so much to have conversations with elected representatives about specific legislative or budgetary priorities, but to build support for URI generally.
FSEC members are strongly encouraged to attend if their schedules allow. 3.3 AY 27-28 Calendar Issue - missing advising day - Discussed as part of the 1/22 agenda discussion.
The Committee has worked with Enrollment Services to provide a fall semester advising day that does not conflict with the Labor Day holiday. 3.4 Future Legislation Update i.
Establishing College Liaisons - While legislation isn’t ready, FSEC agreed the initiative is important and has been in the works for a long time.
If the change is to affect the composition of the senate starting in Fall, 2026, it needs to be introduced, discussed, and approved soon.
Pres.
Williams will present the overarching plan under new business on 1/22. 1

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 2
passages.text:
ii.
College By-Laws - FSEC members generally agreed that this priority is secondary to the creation of Liaisons since pursuing the standardization of By-laws across all colleges is likely a project best handled by the Liaisons.
CBUM has opined that the Senate, through the UM, has the authority to mandate college by-laws.
FSEC members agreed this seems like an important project in that consistency, parity, and procedural transparency would all be well-served by the effort. 3.5 JCODL next steps - continued discussion - FS Pres.
Williams asked the senate for feedback regarding non-curricular offerings and received very little.
It was noted that universities around the country are struggling with the same issue as traditional enrollments decline; they see an opportunity for expansion through these non-standard courses and programs.
FSEC members agreed that some standards need to be set regarding workloads and compensation as well as pedagogy and curricular expectations.
Some offerings cross departments so oversight by departments alone is not a solution.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 2
passages.text:
It was agreed that the senate should circle back at their next meeting and have a brief (10 minutes) discussion about the need for a standardized process and the senate’s role in ensuring that.
Examples of existing programs and/or courses will be provided. 3.6 New Discussion: UM Chapter 8 as relates to the recent final exam change (Request from a senator).
Pres.
Williams noted that the Provost’s office, likely through Vice Provost Adams, might be expected to issue an after-action report regarding this change, including how the decisions were made, the timeline, and and an assessment of the effects of the change on students and faculty.
FSEC members noted that the incident has revealed a need for more contingency planning at the university.
It was suggested that the senate work with the administration to develop a set of procedures and recommendations as a guidance document for future emergencies.
FS Pres.
Williams will talk to the administration about this.
Other related ideas included a possible campus-wide survey about the recent event.
There was general agreement that such a project would most appropriately be taken on by the ATL office.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 2
passages.text:
FSEC also expressed concerns about DAI-related issues in the pivot to an online exam model and noted that students expressed frustration regarding the incurrence of unexpected costs at the end of the term to cover proctoring software. 3.7 CASC proposal to standardize program descriptions and program requirements (Trimm) - The FS Specialist and CASC Chair recently met with the Catalog Coordinator in Enrollment Services to discuss how descriptions are used by students and advisors.
Staff is working on a document that will offer a recommended template for crafting descriptions which should be implemented university-wide. 4.
Continued Items 4.1 Faculty Concerns submitted through the FS Webpage - Two new concerns discussed.
One pertained to the security of exams given the rapidly rolled-out change to formats in December.
The other pertained to training mandates for faculty (especially for online pedagogy) that are burdensome for faculty.
FS Pres.
Williams hopes to address the decision-making process around the changes to fall finals at the January senate meeting.
Regarding the training mandate for online pedagogy, it was noted that updates to the JCODL committee charge will soon be enacted.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 2
passages.text:
This topic is well within their wheelhouse and should be taken up by the committee. 4.2 Chapter 2 revision – current 11/2/25 version - The revision is complete and FSEC agreed it is ready for presentation at the 1/22 meeting.
CBUM had a couple of questions about the text and if there 2

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 3
passages.text:
are any questions or concerns from the floor, there will be time to get answers/revisions in advance of acceptance of the revisions at the February meeting. 5.
Updates 5.1 Updates (meetings with administrators, other committee meetings) i. 1/13/26 APC Meeting - FS Pres.
Williams reported that the APC had voted to approve the Sexual Misconduct policy for recommendation to the President and the BOT.
On behalf of faculty, he was comfortable with the approved draft, especially in regards to changes that update “mandatory reporting” requirements.
In the current document, not all faculty would meet the definition of a mandatory reporter.
The policy, upon approval, will be scheduled for re-review in one year. ii. 1/13/26 PSC Meeting - Pres.
Williams noted the PSC had received updates regarding the university budget and other legislative affairs.
The current recommended budget calls for an approximately three percent increase for the URI operating budget and additional funds for facilities.
The university’s legislative affairs team is working on an advocacy platform that would make it easier for interested parties to get in touch with their legislators.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 3
passages.text:
There is also a proposal to exempt URI from the state’s FTE cap which has a lot of support. iii.
Centers and Institutes -- Pres.
Williams will provide a draft of the changes proposed to existing legislation and a series of slides for this presentation on 1/22.
The proposal is being introduced and will not be docketed for a vote until February at the earliest. iv.
SCLC proposal re.
Subcommittees - Sen.
Van Wyk volunteered to respond to the proposal on behalf of FSEC.
Several comments had been offered on the draft and it has now been revised and transmitted to the Committee Chair. v.
Other - VP Preisser noted he recently met with J.
Humphrey regarding the UM amendments approved this year and how they affect eCampus and Enrollment Services generally.
The meeting revealed that currently, students auditing a course do not have access to eCampus, Brightspace or other tools.
A technical solution is being enacted that will provide for access and the details should be available soon.
Also at the meeting, the 7- and 14- week calendar alignment project was discussed.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 3
passages.text:
A pilot program is nearly ready for launch: it would involve a four-year trial period for three programs which would then be assessed for lessons learned and possible expansion (with senate approval). 6.
Report of the Coordinator i.
AEC Update - The CoEdu Dean survey has been launched and the AEC has been compensated for this year’s work. ii.
Legislation Update - All bills from fall semester now appear on the website.
FSEC members were asked to spot-check any legislation they have been following closely.
Related UM amendments have now also been made. 7.
New Business – Open for additional items not listed in the agenda. i.
Senate appointments to Library Dean search - The administration is putting together a search committee in hopes of having a new dean seated for the fall 2026 semester.
Nominees must be faculty members but are not required to be senators.
A couple of suggestions were made regarding people to reach out to.
It was agreed that the Humanities must be represented on the committee as its disciplines have a disproportionately large presence among users of physical collections. ii.

FSEC (Faculty Senate Executive Committee) Meeting Minutes Date: Wednesday, December 03, 2025 - Time: 10:00 AM – 12:00 noon Pastore Hall, Room 224 - Remote option via ZOOM Action Items: In his next meeting with VP Adams, Pres.
Williams will discuss advancing the UM Chapter 2 updates and will also discuss a means for disseminating information on single-use bathroom locations and a way of reporting needs in that area.
He will also renew the request for a response from the General Counsel’s office regarding the copyright syllabus statement.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 1
passages.text:
Minutes for approval - The following minutes were tabled. i.
Minutes of the 11/19/25 FSEC meeting ii.

Priority Items 3.1 Agenda Setting - 12/11/25 Faculty Senate Meeting - The agenda was reviewed and ultimately approved.
The new Centers and Institutes legislation will be introduced as time allows.
FS Pres.
Williams will create a Power Point presentation.
The very drafty legislation pertaining to college liaisons will be held for introduction until January.
Three FSEC bills are scheduled for a vote.
