passages.heading: Minutes | Page 1
passages.text:
Additional informational reports were also discussed and it was noted that a CBUM update will not be provided due to the recent resignation of the Chair. 3.2 Meeting Re-cap - November 20 Senate Meeting - It was agreed that the meeting was productive and while it was very well attended generally, the number of voting senators in attendance actually declined from prior months.
Senate attendance will continue to be monitored.
There also seemed to be some confusion regarding student-senate and graduate student association representatives.
Those organization leaders are ex officio FS members but other members of those organizations are not.
While all members of the university community should feel free to attend FS meetings, everyone should be aware of the conventions of conduct on the Senate floor.. 3.3 Chapter 2 revision – The current 11/2/25 version is still under review and being actively discussed with VP Adams.
An ongoing area where draft language stands to be improved relates to faculty representation on various search committees.
Another area targeted for clean up pertains to official communications with the BOT.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 1
passages.text:
Clarification around faculty members’ ability to reach out to Board members and/or speak at BOT meetings is needed.
While such communication is always permitted, ‘official positions’ must always be articulated via a set “chain of command” in both directions (from the University community to the Board and vice 1

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 2
passages.text:
versa).
The nexus for such communication is the University President.
This system provides protection for faculty against board member intrusion and also protects the Board itself from the hazards of mixed messages.
Pres.
Williams will continue to work with VP Adams to ensure the intent is clear in the language and agreeable to all parties. 3.4 Recruiting Survey Design Experts -- Sen.
Van Wyk volunteered to formalize this idea into a concrete proposal that FSEC hopes will make its way to the full Senate at the January meeting. 3.5 Stock-taking of major projects at midyear (see Appendix) 3.6 Do relevant committees have documents they need for the projects to be on track?
Discussed as part of Item 3.1 above. 4.
Continued Items 4.1 Faculty Concerns submitted through the FS Webpage - One new concern had been submitted and it related to the use of a Starfish AI content creator feature.
FSEC members shared the concern about use of AI in an advising platform, especially as relates to protection of confidential information, and in terms of optics (it could look to students like a person cannot be bothered to respond to them).

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 2
passages.text:
It was suggested that this specific issue is part of a larger critique that faculty are starting to voice around the uncritical adoption of AI at the university.
Pres.
Williams will discuss the matter in his upcoming meeting with VP Adams. 4.2 Committee Assignment Updates - One additional member (from CELS) has been recruited to JCAPROA, for Senate approval on 12/11. 4.3 Future Legislation Update - The following were discussed as part of Item 3.1 above. i.
Establishing College Liaisons ii.
Third and fourth attempt legislation iii. ‘President’s List’ legislation 5.
Updates 5.1 Updates (meetings with administrators, other committee meetings) i.
PSC Meeting - 12/2/25 - Pres.
Williams reported that the meeting was dominated by a discussion of the KPI’s associated with the four priorities set forth in the strategic plan.
PSC members had discussed progress toward the targeted metrics and strategies to improve performance.
Pres.
Williams noted that over-reliance on certain journal publication citations could negatively affect non-science disciplines.
It was also noted that PhD conferral data could also be problematic.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 2
passages.text:
Presenters at the PSC meeting were clear that no changes to the current KPI’s and associated targets are being considered. ii.
Relocating MPS to College of Education - Concerns had been relayed to the College and FS Pres.
Williams plans to further discuss those concerns with VP Adams.
While this move can be rationalized as simply an administrative bundling, faculty fear such moves could become a norm and several departments could be negatively affected.
In cases where certificates from a variety of departments and colleges are assembled into a degree, there does not seem to be an adequate mechanism in place to ensure degree conferral comes from the most appropriate place.
FSEC would like to hear more from affected faculty members and will try to solicit feedback. iii.
Centers and Institutes Discussion - The Chair of the CIRC had offered comments on the draft.
Those suggestions and others from FSEC members need to be incorporated into the draft.
FSEC agreed that this overhaul of the centers and institutes model will need to be explained over the course of several senate meetings.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 2
passages.text:
The goal is to introduce the initiative, providing background on the work done over the last year and half, along with the bigger picture goals of the proposed update, before diving into the details of the specific language.
If time allows, the matter will be introduced on 12/11 2

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 3
passages.text:
with a vote on UM amendments expected in February or thereafter.
Emphasizing to faculty that existing centers will be treated as ‘grandfathered’ will be important. iv.
Other - Pres.
Williams reported that the administration’s initial reaction to a requested senate budget increase was generally supportive.
There was agreement around the need to ‘professionalize’ the service work done by the senate officers in furtherance of shared governance and achievement of the priority goals set forth in the strategic plan.
Demonstrating respect for the FS’s partnership role through appropriate compensation of officers is expected to build a more collegial ethos of cooperation.
It is hoped that improved compensation will help open a larger pipeline of competent and interested faculty to flow into leadership roles.
In other business, Pres.
Williams noted that the FTE cap imposed on the university by the State continues to be problematic and administrators are lobbying hard to eliminate it or at least increase it.
FSEC members agreed that, given the small percentage of the university budget that the state is responsible for, their ability to dictate employee numbers seems unreasonable. 6.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 3
passages.text:
Report of the Coordinator - The Coordinator will discuss matters related to the FS budget and the Kuali contract renegotiation with the officers separately. 7.
New Business – Open for additional items not listed in the agenda. i.
SCLC proposal re.
Subcommittees - Initial reactions to the proposal included concerns related to the fact that subcommittee structures have not traditionally functioned well and the sheer number of subcommittees suggested may prove unwieldy.
Focusing on intersectionality might help to reduce the number and also ensure that work is not being duplicated.
Additional questions were raised about reporting structures for new groups and the extent of UM language that would need to be drafted, reviewed, and approved to enact the proposal.
It was also noted that a few years ago, the SCLC did a comprehensive survey to map the campus communities that might be focused on diversity, equity, or inclusion matters and it was unclear if the current proposal draws upon that work.
FSEC will continue to discuss the proposal at next week’s meeting and Sen.
Van Wyk, as SCLC liaison, will communicate questions and concerns to the committee. 8.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 3
passages.text:

None 9.

Vote Feb. ‘26 at earliest. 2.

passages.text:
6.

These need to be discussed with the Honors Program before the updates can be presented to the senate. 11.

Cross-enrollment - FSEC agreed it has, with the help of the ACC, done all that the Senate can on this issue until the Administration provides detailed guidance.
The idea of a ‘graduate-level-only’ initial roll-out was floated and has the support of administration partners.

Williams to discuss with VP Adams in next week’s meeting. 12.
Senate budget - Expansion of officer compensation is a priority.

Required syllabus statements, Copyright statement - With no response yet from the General Counsel’s office on the copyright statement, the draft language cannot be on the 12/11 agenda for action, but can be referenced as in-progress by the TAAC. 14.
Completeness of Follett list for course adoptions - Pres.

passages.text:

Minutes of the 02/06/26 meeting.

Priority Items 3.1 Multiple paid resources for communications (CTI issue) The CTI has collected multiple examples of duplicate paid resources and is discussing options for streamlining, sharing, or eliminating resources to address the wasteful overlap.
The CTI is expected to produce a recommendation, but in the meantime, faculty should be reminded to keep an eye on budgets, especially in this constrained year, and be alert to any items their department or college may be unnecessarily paying for if like resources already exist in the community. 3.2 Future Legislation Updates i.
Honors update of UM 8.60.10 - 8.65.12 to comport with the approved TAAC bill - Honors Director deBruin has agreed to draft amendments to the relevant Manual sections which will require subsequent review by CBUM and TAAC.
A quick turnaround has been requested so the Manual language and recent legislation are not out of comportment for long. ii.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 1
passages.text:
Establishing College Liaisons - In consideration of the timeline for colleges to select senators for AY 26-27 and the fact that the draft UM language still needs a lot of work, it was agreed that this initiative will likely need to be a summer project.
If adequate progress is made by FSEC (with substantial concurrence from the college Deans) over the break, this legislation could advance to the senate floor early in the fall semester, thereby leaving plenty of time to accommodate reapportionments (if necessary) prior to the next election cycle. iii.

The bill was drafted at the behest of the Graduate 1

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 2
passages.text:
School.

Regarding the calendar alignment project and the move to an 8-year planning cycle for academic calendars (rather than a 6-year cycle), it was noted that required online calendars also need to be approved formally this year, but in the future, they may be rolled into the overall calendar effort.

APC - APC met on 2/10/26 and reviewed policies related to remote work and protecting minors.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 2
passages.text:

Commencement schedule - FSEC assignments (Tabled to 2/20/26) v.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 3
passages.text: with proposers to correct deficiencies. FSEC members discussed a possible need to reconfigure the curriculum committees to guarantee adequate review of programs. VP Preisser will work with staff and try to develop a concept plan for grappling with this challenge. vi. It was noted that the BAC would be an appropriate vehicle for such a task and FSEC looks forward to hearing the results of their recent survey. 6. Report of the Coordinator i. passages.heading: Minutes | Page 1
passages.text:

Call to Order - Pres.
Williams called the meeting to order at 12:31 pm.
VP Preisser and Senators Meenach, Van Wyk, Trimm and Daniels were present. 2.
Minutes for approval - i.
Minutes of the 1/16/26 FSEC meeting - tabled. 3.
Priority Items (40 minutes) 3.1 Re-cap - January 22, 2026 senate meeting.
Everyone agreed that FSEC might want to reconsider January meeting dates as the ‘triple-whammy’ of the first day of classes, followed by a senate meeting, followed by an FSEC meeting had proven to be a lot.
In terms of the meeting itself, FSEC noted that faculty need to pay more attention to curricular matters.
Lengthy discussions about course proposals could be averted if they are studied in advance and concerns are addressed with relevant parties before the proposals ever reach the senate floor.
There was concern expressed that the new budget model might lead to an escalation of conflicts involving departments or colleges having competing claims of ‘ownership’ of certain content areas.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 1
passages.text:
FSEC members expected questions about ‘college liaisons’ as it is a new and complex idea, but were a little surprised at the tone of the inquiry.
There was agreement that, while there is a clear need due to existing deficiencies, every effort must be made to make the case without alienating any college or group specifically.
Broad statements about standardizing communications channels are apt to be the best proactive messages.
FSEC remains committed to the initiative and agreed that it doesn’t have to be perfect out of the gate, but could be launched and refined/revisited over time. 3.2 CBUM Editorial Reports (Updating references to the BIS Program and the Alan Shawn Feinstein College of Education and Professional Studies).
The two reports were approved unanimously by FSEC and will be docketed for the Feb. 19 senate meeting. 3.3 Future Legislation Updates i.
Establishing College Liaisons - Based on feedback at the senate meeting, the draft will require revision and detailed feedback from deans is also still outstanding. 1

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 2
passages.text:
ii.
College By-Laws - Not all colleges have by-laws and some of those colleges do not see them as necessary or required.
FSEC agreed that the liaisons initiative is a higher priority and perhaps the by-laws could be a project for that group, once established. iii.
Chapter 8 amendments related to 7 & 14 week calendar alignment - there has been productive back-and-forth regarding the draft and Vice Provost is refining it now.
A draft should be available in time for FSEC to approve it and include it on the 2/19 FS agenda for approval. 3.4 Update - December final exam changes - Pres.
Williams will circle back with the administration about their ability to produce some kind of after-action report so that the senate can close the loop on this. 3.5 Advance Planning - 2/19/26 FS meeting - FSEC took a first look at the draft agenda, noting there is still plenty of time to refine it before it must be posted.
Chief Jagoda has confirmed that he is available to offer a brief campus safety update at the February meeting.
Legislation passed earlier this year will also be back on the agenda for amendment to include effective dates.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 2
passages.text:
A first look at JCODL-related UM revisions will likely be added to the February agenda.
FSEC had hoped to get to this initiative as a ‘new business’ item on the January agenda but ran out of time.
There has not been a lot of feedback offered regarding the non-credit-bearing offerings and if it is discerned that faculty don’t feel too strongly about it, it will not be included in the legislation. 4.
Continued Items 4.1 Faculty Concerns submitted through the FS Webpage - One new concern was discussed and it pertained to the Online Pedagogy Training offered by ATL.
FSEC has expressed concerns before with the amount of training faculty is subjected to which becomes burdensome and starts to impact productivity.
In terms of the specific training referenced, some FSEC members had been through the process and found the time burden in this specific case was actually an investment in their course as it helped them ‘front-load’ all the work of setting up their online courses.
It seemed like individuals were having very different experiences with this training.
Pres.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 2
passages.text:
Williams noted there are actually four paths to online pedagogy certification and FSEC probably needs clarification regarding the specific experience of this commenter before they proceed.
However, in general terms, he can reach out, through the Provost’s office, to determine if ATL and Online programs are adequately staffed to conduct the training effectively and if they have a good process to gather feedback, conduct program review, and implement improvements when necessary. 5.
Updates 5.1 Updates (meetings with administrators, other committee meetings) i. ‘Survey Design Advising Team’ - JVW Proposal - An important goal is to set up a system that is sustainable, not overly complex or cumbersome, and doesn’t require a lot of management or oversight.
Recruiting an adequate number of design experts at the start will be key.
FSEC agreed that the option of simply listing the volunteers with brief bios regarding their expertise and allowing a “surveyors choice” process to play out might be the simplest process to implement.
The list could be randomized and updated regularly to ensure fairness.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 2
passages.text:
Offering a feedback form would help the senate stay attuned to when the volunteers are becoming overburdened.
It was agreed that this is a great service for the senate to offer and, if implemented well, it could be an enduring resource.
There was a discussion around deciding where this resource lives, i.e. should the description, forms, etc. be available via the senate’s website, the Provost’s, or both?
Since it is expected to be used by College Deans and other administrators, among others, some presence with the administration is important.
FSEC agreed that the service is being provided by the faculty senate and should live on its pages but a link must be 2

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 3
passages.text:
available from the Provost’s page.
The goal is to set this up over the coming weeks and start recruiting volunteers.
Once established, a presentation could be made to the full senate (target March meeting).
Some suggestions regarding potential volunteers of offices to contact for help in recruitment were made and Sen.
Van Wyk will follow up. ii.
Chapter 2 revision – Current Draft and CBUM comments - This will be on the Feb.
FS docket for acceptance of the Presidential Report.
Pres.
Williams has worked closely with VP Adams on the draft and that effort has been very productive.
He still has three outstanding issues that need to be resolved prior to the 2/19 meeting.
First, the Assoc.
Vice Provost for Academic Personnel is not mentioned in Chap. 2 which means faculty cannot assert any role in the recruitment and selection of candidates to fill this role.
Related, the Vice Provost for Academic Resource Management is mentioned in Chp. 2 but the Faculty Senate is precluded from appointing a faculty member to sit on the search and review committees.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 3
passages.text:
Faculty would seem to be particularly vested in these two positions, but there are many other assistant and associate vice pres. and Vice Provost positions that the faculty senate is losing its ability to participate in selecting and this is concerning.
Second, the Dean of Students is not mentioned and this seems important.
Finally, in the description of the University President’s role, there is no reference to the university manual being a controlling document and this should be corrected. iii.
Senate appointments to Library Dean search - Pres.
Williams has received clarification regarding the appointment of Library faculty and will proceed with the appointments from among the broader university faculty.
He is still seeking candidates and is interested in making sure users of physical collections - not just digital collections - are represented.
In a related discussion, senate leadership has expressed concern about the use of search firms and their taking liberties with initial culls of candidates.
The search committees expect to participate fully at every step and this feels like an affront.
The Vice Provost has agreed to bring these concerns to the Provost and President. iv.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 3
passages.text:
Copyright statement - the General Counsel’s office is still looking at this.
It obviously didn’t make the Vice Provost’s announcement for the start of the spring semester so the goal now is to have something finalized in time for a Fall 2026 announcement. v.
Commencement schedule - There will be eight events (two Friday, three each Saturday and Sunday).
FSEC members are encouraged to share the Grand Marshal role and Pres.
Williams would like to settle on a schedule soon so the event organizers can be informed and have correct information for contact and program purposes. vi.
URI at the Statehouse - the Senate will not have a booth or table at the March 26 event but will fully participate otherwise.
Staff was asked to procure some sort of button or pin that can be worn to the event as a representation of the Faculty Senate.
A bus will be available but FSEC members should feel free to drive. vii.
Other - Pres.
Williams met with Vice Provost Adams today and discussed, among other things, a change that is proposed in how faculty are awarded emeritus status.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 3
passages.text:
The changes affect Chapter 7 of the University Manual and the proposal calls for insertion of language that would require faculty to have served ‘honorably and meritoriously’ during their years of service.
The same language would apply to Deans and other administrators who seek emeritus status.
Apparently the intention of the change is to allow the status to be bestowed on individuals who may not meet the 10-years-of-service minimum who might still qualify under the new provision.
FSEC members agreed some clarification is needed to specify some process for establishing ‘honorable and meritorious’ service 3

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 4
passages.text: - including definitions or examples and an assignment of roles so it is clear who is making the determination. 6. Report of the Coordinator i. Effective Dates of Legislation - staff will create a process to help ensure all UM revisions have an ‘effective date’ as part of the bill going forward. ii. Student worker hiring update - two graduate students have been interviewed and a third is coming in next week. It looks like the senate office will get 10 - 15 hours of help per week. iii. Outreach re: Legislation - The senate has been busy with a lot of UM amendments this year and it doesn’t appear that adequate outreach is occurring as the office has spent a lot of time answering questions and making corrections to proposals that don’t comply with new protocols. FSEC (Faculty Senate Executive Committee) Meeting Minutes Date: Friday, February 6, 2026 - Time: 12:30 pm – 2:30 pm Pastore Hall, Room 224 - Remote option via ZOOM Action Items: FS Pres.
Williams will remind the Honors Director that formal legislation amending UM Sec. 8.60.10 - 8.65.12 will need to be presented to the Faculty Senate asap for comportment with the TAAC bill approved at the January meeting.
Staff will format the draft Chapter 2 amendment to mimic the bill template and create a version that can be shared with the senate.
The FS Pres. and VP will continue to refine the ‘College Liaisons’ legislation.
Staff will convert the administration’s draft 7- & 14- week calendar alignment language to a formal bill with line numbers and an effective date and send it to CBUM for review.
It will be introduced at the 2/19 FS meeting.
The FS Pres. and VP will discuss the framework for CASC’s proposal to standardize program descriptions with the Vice Provost and chart a path forward.
The FS Pres. will address the SCLC’s concerns about the UDC in his next meeting with the University President and Provost. 1.
Call to Order - Pres.
Williams called the meeting to order at 12:30 pm.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 1
passages.text:
VP Preisser and Senators Meenach, Van Wyk, Trimm and Daniels were present. 2.
Minutes for approval - The following were approved as edited. i.
Minutes of the 1/23/26 and 1/30/26 FSEC meetings ii.
Minutes of the 1/22/26 FS meeting 3.
Priority Items 3.1 New ‘home’ for the Interdisciplinary Neuroscience Graduate Programs update - Faculty have expressed concern that the details of this administrative move raise concerns about preferential treatment within colleges and administrators’ ability to replace program leaders at will with no input or involvement from faculty.
FSEC members noted that dean interference in curriculum would certainly rise to the level of senate involvement, but there may be no clear path for senate involvement in these personnel changes.
It was suggested that affected personnel contact their union and that the FSEC continue to monitor similar activity and be ready to respond to instances of encroachment into faculty rights. 3.2 Future Legislation Updates i.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 1
passages.text:
Honors to update UM 8.60.10 - 8.65.12 to comport with the TAAC bill approved on 1/22 - Given that Honors as an Academic Experience has now been created in Kuali, some of the language in these sections can likely be pared down.
FS Pres.
Williams will remind the Honors Director that a formal bill will need to be presented to the Faculty Senate asap. ii.
Establishing College Liaisons - FSEC officers are still trying to convey to both deans and senators the myriad benefits of having a defined interface between the senate and the colleges.
A more structured information conduit would improve communications in both directions.
Currently, although senators are expected to take information back to their departments and bring concerns forward to the senate from them, the results on the ground are disparate and are generally found wanting in departments not currently represented in the senate.
The mechanics of adding a liaison to each college are still being debated and the goal is an equitable solution that honors the apportionment formula as stated in the By-Laws.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 1
passages.text:
It was noted that the COE Dean has invited a brief ‘senate update’ at the next all-college meeting and it is hoped that other colleges may follow suit.
Such practice could help fill the communications gap until Liaisons can be ensconced in the Manual.
FSEC members agreed that the real 1

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 2
passages.text:
benefits of having liaisons may not emerge until 3 or 4 years after the roles are created, as it may take that long for representatives to realize the degree to which governance standards and norms across colleges are lacking and to develop remedies. iii.
Chapter 8 amendments related to 7- & 14-week calendar alignment - Staff will convert the administration’s draft to a formal bill and send it to CBUM for review.
It will be introduced at the 2/19 FS meeting but no vote will be held before March 12. iv. approval of academic calendars 8 years in advance - The ACC has drafted a proposal based on needs expressed by the Graduate School.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 2
passages.text:
The draft will require review and support from CBUM and already has support from Online and Summer Programs. v. adjusting due date for final grades - discussed as part of Item 3.4 below. 3.3 Missing Classroom Database - Update - The Chairs of the CTI and JCSC are working to restore and update the data and will circle back with FSEC as needed. 3.4 Review Next Senate Agenda - 2/19/26 FS meeting - Several items were substantively discussed, especially the presentation of UM Chapter 2, the proposed amendments to previously approved FSEC Bills #4 and #5, the logistics of the VP election, and the addition of an initial discussion on adjusting the due date of final grades to accommodate calculation of academic standing, if time allows.
The agenda was ultimately approved unanimously with the following added to the draft.
It was noted that the agenda can still be amended next Friday if necessary. i.
Add Senate approval of a new CHILD Institute ii.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 2
passages.text:
Online calendars 2028-2031 3.5 Advance Planning - AY 26-27 FS meeting schedule (tabled until after the 2/19 VP election) 3.6 Connecting UDC with SCLC - FSEC’s concerns about the SCLC ‘subcommittees’ proposal have been conveyed to the Committee and liaison Van Wyk met with a committee representative recently.
Frustration about the UDC was expressed in that the SCLC would not have proposed new overlapping groups if it had confidence that their activities and initiatives might already be covered by the UDC.
Getting any information about the UDC’s current efforts has proven challenging.
If communication is a key stumbling block, FSEC felt that a joint meeting of some sort would help break the impasse.
A meeting of full committees might prove unwieldy right away so it was agreed that a 6-person event might be an option as an opening effort.
It would involve the UDC Co-Chairs, the SCLC Chair and liaison, and the FS Pres. and VP.
The SCLC would like to propose that their committee have a representative or liaison to the UDC to help ensure consistent communications.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 2
passages.text:
The FS Pres. will address some of these concerns in his next meeting with University leadership. 3.7 Staffing IPC and SAC - The IPC has been staffed and the Coordinator has corrected a communication error related to updating the membership.
A couple of the SAC appointees have seemingly declined their appointments.
Staff will get up to date information and work with the FS President to fill all seats. 3.8 Grade dispute procedures (8.26.13) and academic dishonesty procedures (8.27.17) 4.
Continued Items 4.1 Faculty Concerns submitted through the FS Webpage - One new concern was discussed.
It pertained to the composition of the search committee for the new Library Dean and the fact that only two library faculty have been appointed to the committee.
It was noted that the library is unique and the dean is unlike the deans of the colleges in many ways, especially given that the constituency for the library includes the entire community.
FSEC felt it important to ensure faculty from across the user base 2

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 3
passages.text:
of the library were represented in the search.
FS Pres.
Williams will reach out to the commenter.
In the meantime, FSEC has a member serving on the committee who will keep FSEC apprised of progress. 5.
Updates (30 minutes) 5.1 Updates (meetings with administrators, other committee meetings) i.
MPS rehoming update - no new report. ii. ‘Survey Design Advising Team’ - (JVW) - Prepare for March Introduction to FS - Sen.
Van Wyk is close to having materials ready for presentation to the senate and to post to the FS webpage.
A link to resources will be provided on the Provost’s page as well. iii.
Copyright statement - no update.
Remains under review by the Deputy General Counsel. iv.
Commencement schedule - FSEC assignments (Tabled to 2/20) v.
Chapter 2 UM amendments - Status of revisions/Bill Formatting - Staff will convert the current proposed language into an actionable bill and docket for the 2/19 FS meeting.
However, some requested modifications have not yet been agreed to by the administration and if no further progress is made over the next week or so, this might be tabled to the March meeting for action. vi.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 3
passages.text:
Changes to qualifications for emeritus status - The current draft language is being revised and will be re-shared when ready. vii.
Brightspace purge - It was noted that saving course shells and grade books is very straightforward but saving student work can be cumbersome.
There may be short cuts for bulk saves from Brightspace and ITS is exploring that.
FSEC members agreed that even with the new limitations, the capacity of the system to retain information far exceeds past practices.
Also, savings from freeing up data storage capacity could help to pay for proctoring modules that could benefit students greatly and the absence of which currently stands to create hardship and inequity for some. viii.
Other 6.
Report of the Coordinator i.
Senate elections and FSEC elections - Staff has received an all-faculty list from the IR office for AY 25-26 and is working on sorting it by college so apportionment can be calculated.
FSEC members are encouraged to keep recruiting VP and other Executive Committee candidates and staff is working on a flyer for distribution to all senators. ii.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 3
passages.text:
Kuali Contract - A proposal was received from Kuali and advanced to the Vice Provost who has requested options, including a calendar-year renewal in lieu of a fiscal year one and the separation of additional “Build” modules from the base CMS contract.
Staff is working on these modifications. 7.
New Business – Open for additional items not listed in the agenda. i. multiple paid resources for communications (CTI issue) Tabled to 2/13. ii.
CASC work on program description standardization - the FS Specialist joined the discussion and provided some background on the identification of the need to create consistency and standardization of program descriptions.
This was identified as a need some time ago but has become especially concerning with NECHE reaccreditation looming which significantly increases scrutiny of the catalog.
Staff has worked closely with Enrollment Services and the CASC Chair to develop guidance but advice on the best method for communicating this guidance is now required.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 3
passages.text:
FSEC members noted that the nexus with accreditation provides an opportunity for the Provost’s office to be involved in rolling out the guidance which gives some weight to its importance and may help compel compliance.
The idea of presenting the guidance as a Bill (likely an Appendix E amendment) or a Resolution was discussed, as 3

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 4
passages.text: was the notion of creating Kuali rules such that program proposals could not advance unless the guidance template is followed. Programs would not be required to amend descriptions all at once, but over time, as changes are proposed, they would be brought into conformity. The FS Pres. and VP need to discuss the framework with the Vice Provost which might help clarify a path forward. 8. Closing Remarks – Recap of decisions made, action items, and plans for the next meeting. None 9. Adjournment - The meeting adjourned at 2:33 pm. 4

FSEC (Faculty Senate Executive Committee) Meeting Minutes Date: Wednesday, December 17, 2025 - Time: 10:00 AM – 12:00 noon Pastore Hall, Room 224 - Remote option via ZOOM Action Items: Staff will create a template slide deck for future standing committee initial reports to the full senate for future use.
Staff will communicate to CBUM that it should take the lead on modifications to UM Section 8.20.73.
FS Pres.

passages.text:
FSEC members are asked, for the spring 2026 semester, to be prepared to approve FS agendas two Fridays before the Thursday meeting to avoid any last minute complications around posting requirements and to help ensure that appropriate background materials go out to all members. 1.
Call to Order - Pres.
Williams called the meeting to order at 10:03 AM.
VP Preisser and Senators Meenach, Van Wyk, Trimm and Daniels were present. 2.
Minutes for approval - i.
Minutes of the 12/10/25 FSEC meeting were approved as edited. 3.
Priority Items 3.1 Meeting Recap - 12/11/25 Faculty Senate Meeting - FSEC members were pleased that the senate worked its way through all agenda items efficiently and adjourned ahead of schedule.
For future reference, it was noted that initial reports from standing committees on their goals and priorities for the year might work better if they all follow a standard format.
Staff will try to develop a template for future reports. 3.2 Advance Planning - URI Day at the Statehouse - The date of this year’s URI Day has been released: 3/26/26.
This leaves FSEC plenty of time to craft its presence and message for the event.
Pres.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 1
passages.text:
Williams explained that the goal of this outing is not so much to lobby legislators, but to simply flood the space with URI representatives as a reminder of the URI community’s size and scope.
Based on past experience, hand-outs are not very effective, but the FSEC might consider a poster on behalf of the faculty senate to highlight key pieces of legislation.
It was suggested that state legislators will likely not be conversant in the particulars of university shared governance and faculty senates.
It might be more useful to think about ways the FS representatives to URI Day might effectively represent faculty more broadly. 3.3 Advance Planning - January 22, 2026 senate meeting - FSEC will only meet one more time before the next senate meeting so the draft agenda was reviewed.
The discussion of January’s priorities led to a broader conversation about spring semester priorities, especially those that the administration anticipates action on.
Items that will come up for a vote over the next five months include: the Ombuds updates; Centers and Institutes; UM Chapter 2; JCODL; and the coalescence of the 7- and 14- week calendars for graduate level courses.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 1
passages.text: Regarding the JCODL revisions, the plan is to present the senate with a couple of overarching questions (a - do they 1

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 2
passages.text:
care about non-credit-bearing curricular offerings?; and b - if so, do they have ideas on how to rapidly respond to curricular proposals in that realm?).
Depending on senate input, the draft JCODL document will be refined for presentation.
Regarding the calendar coalescence, this item was always an administration priority rather than a senate one.
Until an administrator provides a gameplan and timeline, the senate should not be expected to devote a lot of time to this initiative.
Regarding Chapter 2 and the Centers/Institutes legislation, some edits are still needed but Pres.
Williams hopes to transmit these drafts to CBUM for review in the very near future so they might be addressed at the 1/22/26 FS meeting. 3.4 AY 27-28 Calendar Issue - missing advising day- Pres.
Williams will communicate with the ACC Chair regarding concerns with the AY 27-28 academic calendar (missing advising day).
The ACC will be asked to devise a solution for consideration by the faculty senate, preferably at the 1/22 meeting. 3.5 Future Legislation Update i.
Establishing College Liaisons - FSEC is still waiting for feedback from deans on this idea.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 2
passages.text:
If the senate decides to move ahead with establishing liaisons, several models might be worth considering - some of which would include drawing from the existing pool of senators and others would involve adding senate seats.
If there is any chance of implementing this change for Fall 2026, some draft legislation needs to be drafted asap. ii.
College By-Laws - It appears that not all colleges have by-laws.
Staff is trying to confirm.
Sen.
Preisser and staff are meeting later today to wrap up the compilation effort. 3.6 Amend UM 8.20.73 - A Request had been received from Past FS President Mike Rice asking that FSEC examine the referenced policy with regards to its prohibition against transferring credits from other institutions to URI in pursuit of undergraduate certificates here.
FSEC agreed with Prof.
Rice that there seems to be no basis for the prohibition.
FSEC members also agreed it was important to leave a cap in place on outside and previously earned credits so as not to devalue the URI Certificates.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 2
passages.text:
Staff will communicate to the CBUM Chair that his committee should take the lead on modifications to UM Section 8.20.73. 3.7 Proposal to update attendance policy to account for special medical needs (inquiry from Sen.
Martin; see UM 8.51.15) - FSEC desires to understand this issue better.
It is unclear at present whether the existing policy is itself inadequate (requiring a legislative solution), or if the policy is sound but individuals require reminders or clarifications around their compliance with it.
Pres.
Williams will continue with his fact-finding and bring the issue back to FSEC as appropriate. 3.8 CASC proposal to standardize program descriptions and program requirements - Sen.
Trimm met yesterday with the FS Specialist and CASC Chair.
A meeting is being set with Enrollment Services and the Catalogue Coordinator to explore ways that Kuali might be utilized to bolster standardization.
FS staff needs to understand NECHE requirements and other variables better before creating templates.
Sen.
Trimm will keep FSEC informed. 4.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 2
passages.text:
Continued Items 4.1 Faculty Concerns submitted through the FS Webpage - Two new concerns: Regarding the first of these, FSEC members agreed there was a cultural aspect (such as needing to wash for religious observances) that it had not previously considered in its discussion of single user restrooms.
It was agreed that this argument will be used in future advocacy efforts aimed at increasing the number of such facilities and improving access to information about how to find and utilize them on campus.
Regarding the second comment, Pres.
Williams offered a timeline of high-level communications that occurred in 2

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 3
passages.text:
furtherance of decision-making about final exams/assignments in light of the Brown shooting and he emphasized that he, as FS President, was looped in and provided a faculty perspective all along the way.
He added that while there is merit to the concerns about academic integrity in making a sudden shift to online assessments, no decision made under such tight time constraints and in such circumstances was ever going to be perfect.
The administration weighed the stress on all persons affected and chose to place the greater burden on those who were more equipped to bear it (i.e. instructors rather than students).
Additionally, leaving the decisions to individual faculty members would have likely exposed those individual faculty to personal inquiries, complaints, etc.
By issuing a blanket statement, the resources of Green Hall and the whole administration could be brought to bear in fielding questions and concerns.
Additional feedback from FSEC members on the challenges faced by faculty in this situation was provided so that Pres.
Williams might share those concerns with administrators.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 3
passages.text:
Two important potential initiatives were the result of the discussion: first, explicit information should be posted/provided in every classroom about securing students and emergency procedures specific to that room.
Second, the university should do more contingency planning.
Recent events made clear that trying to devise a one-size-fits-all emergency exam protocol on the fly is less than ideal.
A set of proactive principles and guidelines could be developed so future interruptions to learning might cause less chaos.
Perhaps a working group should be convened to start thinking about options and looking at best practices.
Pres.
Williams will take these suggestions back to administrators in his next meeting with them. 4.2 Chapter 2 revision – current 11/2/25 version - Pres.
Williams reported that a draft is nearly ready for consideration.
His goal is to give the current document a final pass and then send it on to CBUM for review with an eye toward action on this chapter at the January 22, 2026 FS meeting.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 3
passages.text:
It was noted that the administration is listed as the primary steward of this chapter so the report on the updates and revisions should likely come from a senior member of the university president’s team.
A decision needs to be made on who will lead this presentation prior to the agenda being set. 4.3 Committee Assignment Updates, if any - No new appointments 5.

Daniels noted he attended a productive meeting of the CTI this week wherein TLS Director Michelle Rogers shared information about the “Brightspace” clean-up project.
Pres.

Relocating MPS to College of Education - No update ii.
Copyrights policy/Required Syllabus Statements - no official response from the General Counsel’s office has been received.
This initiative is becoming time-sensitive.
The TAAC will need to complete a review of related policies, guidelines, and the Manual for consistency, which could take some time to complete. iii.
Centers and Institutes - The updates were introduced at the last senate meeting.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 3
passages.text:
The biggest outstanding issue that needs to be resolved with the administration is the matter of KPI credit. iv.
SCLC proposal re.
Subcommittees - Sen.
Van Wyk’s response to the subcommittees proposal should be reviewed by FSEC members and, assuming there are no major edits, it will be passed along to SCLC on behalf of the executive committee. v.
Other 3

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 4
passages.text:
6.
Report of the Coordinator - In light of the imminent retirement of the current Vice Provost for Academic Personnel and Budget (Matt Bodah), restructuring of the faculty senate office to be administratively housed under the Vice Provost for Academic and Faculty Initiatives (currently, Sue Adams) was briefly discussed. 7.
New Business – Open for additional items not listed in the agenda.
Sen.
Van Wyk offered that the student senate is in touch with the SCLC about advancing a resolution to the faculty senate aimed at calling for enhanced public safety on campus.
FSEC members agreed, given the events that unfolded over the weekend at Brown University, that some discussion might be in order.
Sen.
Van Wyk and the SCLC hope to refine draft language before bringing anything to FSEC for formal consideration.
Student Senate representatives are being advised to meet with the campus police chief as an initial step to gain a better understanding of existing security protocols and measures in place before trying to advocate for changes.
In other new business, Sen.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 4
passages.text:
Trimm noted that the recently approved curricular streamlining initiative could end up making more work for the FS office staff if certain checklists and backstops are not instituted to improve proposal quality in the early stages of the curricular proposal process.
Sen.
Trimm met with the Specialist and CASC Chair and agreed that a couple of things need to happen if this transition is to run smoothly.
First, some kind of master checklist needs to be rolled out to the college curriculum committees to ensure that they are reviewing proposals with enough checks and balances to ensure that only high quality proposals advance.
Second, Kuali can and should be used to help automate some best practices which should help ensure that approved proposals don’t have implementation problems that would cost FS, Enrollment Services, or other staffers a lot of time cleaning up.
Sen.
Trimm and Sen.
Preisser agreed that a meeting (preferably in-person with a mandatory attendance requirement for committee chairs) should be set with ample notice to share new procedures with those affected.
Sen.
Trimm will continue to work with staff on this initiative. 8.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 4
passages.text:
Closing Remarks – Recap of decisions made, action items, and plans for the next meeting.
None. 9.
Adjournment - The meeting adjourned at 11:35 am. 4

Williams is point-person on the JCODL legislation and will continue to refine the language for further discussion at the March FS meeting.

passages.text:
Williams called the meeting to order at 12:30 pm.

Invited Guest: Amy D’Agata, CRCA Chair at 1:00 PM - Chair D’Agata reminded FSEC of the scope of her committee and noted the responsibilities are both varied and numerous.
She explained that even with recent UM updates that refined the committee’s priorities and added members, the committee still struggles to give every issue under their purview its due.
FSEC indicated a willingness to consider structural changes if they would improve efficiency and ensure a manageable workload.
Chair D’Agata noted she views their most important responsibility to be that of providing advice to the VP RED regarding research-related activities.
It has been an especially challenging year in that regard due to dramatic shifts in the research funding landscape.
Considering the very close relationship of the Committee with the VP RED’s office, it was suggested that it should perhaps be a Joint rather than a Senate Committee to help ensure adequate expertise and staffing levels to accomplish priority tasks.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 1
passages.text:
If this is not workable, it was suggested that perhaps the Competitive Grants Subcommittee, at a minimum, could move in that direction since that group is so reliant on administrative help from the Research Office and on volunteer reviewers that are not part of the senate.
Such configuration might also help ensure expertise is brought to bear from across research-centric academic units.
Sen.
Meenach, liaison to the CRCA, noted that the grants activity is a huge service burden and it requires the participation of expert reviewers.
She concurred that the best structure would be to make it a Joint Committee under the VPRED with senate representation provided for alongside other faculty members and administrators.
The group moved on to discuss the F&A oversight (Facilities and Administration, also known as ‘overhead’) responsibilities of the Committee.
Chair D’Agata and Sen.
Meenach noted that with the budget model transition, which involves a new and somewhat opaque subvention formula and which has increased Dean discretion, the Committee’s ability to influence decision-making has become constrained.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 1
passages.text:
Committee members have inquired if the level of effort involved in the review and assessment is really worth it.
FSEC agreed that the CRCA Chair and her committee, along with the FSEC liaison, should develop a formal proposal to restructure their committee.
It may involve shedding its subcommittee and it may involve a conversion from ‘Senate Standing’ to ‘Joint’ committee.

passages.text:
Williams has knowledge of the history of the CRCA and the Council for Research that preceded it.

It is hoped that a specific proposal can be approved by FSEC, assigned to other reviewers as required (CBUM, past CRCA Chairs. . . ) and advance to the Senate floor when ready. 3.

passages.text:
Williams will explore language that provides for “notification and consultation” rather than a formal approval process (not even a pared-down or expedited one).

Williams, who is the point-person for this legislation.

Faculty Senate Executive Committee Report #2024-2025-12 Introduction: April 10, 2025 Faculty Senate Meeting For Approval: May 1, 2025 Proposed Revisions to Appendix C of the University Manual By-Laws of the Faculty Senate Amendments pertain to converting the Special Budget and Administration Committee to a Permanent Standing Committee (According to Section 12.1 of the By-Laws, amendments require two meetings and a two-thirds majority vote of senators present to pass.) RATIONALE: According to Article II, Section 4 of Appendix B of the University Manual (Constitution of the Faculty Senate), the Senate shall establish such standing and special committees as it deems necessary to carry out its functions.
During AY 2023-2024, the University community faced operational changes, including various administrative policy initiatives and the planned transition to a new budget model, then known as IBB.
The proposed pace of change and the sheer quantity of new initiatives strained the ability of the Faculty Senate Executive Committee (FSEC) to respond appropriately and react in a coordinated, meaningful, and timely fashion.

passages.heading: #24-25-19 | Page 2
passages.text:
The FSEC concluded that creating a special committee to advise them in these and related matters would improve the efficiency and effectiveness of the Faculty Senate.
A new group, known as the Special Budget and Administration Committee (SBAC) was created in May 2024 and was designed to exist through AY 2025-2026.
The charge of the committee was generally to advise the Senate on administrative policy developments, assist in analyzing and making recommendations regarding any major operational changes emerging under the university strategic plan, and analyze the effects of the new budget model and its implementation, as well as any other specific operational expenditures relevant to faculty.
The current FSEC has found the Special Committee to be useful and effective and has noted that other faculty senates at peer institutions have permanent committees focused on budgetary matters.
The FSEC therefore recommends that the special committee now become a permanent standing committee.

passages.heading: #24-25-19 | Page 3
passages.text:
MOTION: THAT THE FOLLOWING LANGUAGE BE INSERTED INTO APPENDIX C 4.90 The Budget and Administration Committee (BAC) shall comprise five faculty members, three of whom shall be faculty senators.
The chair shall serve a two-year term and will be elected by the committee following input from the faculty senate executive committee.
The Committee shall provide reports on their activities to the Faculty Senate at least annually and more often as directed by the FSEC or the Senate.

passages.heading: #24-25-19 | Page 3
passages.text:
Any specific BAC proposals for action will flow from the Committee to the FSEC and then to the Senate. 4.91 Activities of the Budget and Administration Committee will include but not be limited to: the review and, if necessary, the development of measures for tracking major or incremental expenditures, with the aim of ensuring balanced support of faculty interests; requesting information on the university’s performance toward any new goals set up under the prevailing budget model and under any proposed changes to the budget model, and raising questions about the correspondence of these allocations against performance metrics (KPIs) and the university’s Strategic Plan; monitoring administrative policies with the aim of supporting academic freedom and faculty efforts.
The Committee shall make recommendations to the executive committee and the senate about formal responses to: any plans or proposals by the committees and individuals tasked with the implementation and functioning of the budget model; any positions or policy initiatives of the institutional research office, administrative policy groups, purchasing, capital projects, and similar groups as they may identify or that arise.

passages.heading: #24-25-19 | Page 3
passages.text: They may also engage in advocacy on behalf of the faculty for support of research, instruction, professional development, travel, course caps, and service time, so that faculty thrive in their work given their contractual roles.

Sen.

It would explain the serious, multi-hour commitment per week associated with FSEC membership and would note that such involvement by a faculty member stands to benefit the affected college and should thus be reasonably accommodated.
Financial support for FSEC participation in AY 26-27 is still undetermined as the budget for the fiscal year starting on July 1 is not yet fixed.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 2
passages.text:
3.2.
Recap - May 7 FS meeting - Impressions of the final meeting of the academic year were generally favorable, although there was some disappointment that not all curricular reports were approved and the JCODL legislation did not advance.
The final reports, including the Athletics presentation were informative, and the approval of the Honors legislation and UM Chapter 5 updates were important achievements.
A discussion ensued about best legislative practices, especially in terms of how floor debates proceed.
When specific concerns about or objections to legislation are known in advance, FSEC members should do their best to help resolve them before the floor is opened to discussion during a meeting.
This can include communicating with FS President and Vice President, as well as reaching out to (the) relevant committee chair(s).
Delayed decision-making about curricular reports is especially problematic at year-end, since it affects the start date for courses and programs.
Regarding the JCODL overhaul, the notice of suggested amendments was not received by all relevant parties in time to meaningfully address each point.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 2
passages.text:
According to parliamentary procedure, amendments must be taken up one at a time, which is also especially unwieldy at the last meeting of the year when so much business must be attended to.
A plan for addressing the JCODL legislation in the fall was discussed and FSEC leaders will try to compile a “response to comments” document, designed to address all known objections and concerns, to be distributed with the bill in advance.
The JCODL bill will not be approved over the summer by FSEC in lieu of the full senate, because that power is reserved for emergencies.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 2
passages.text:

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 3

wherein building and classroom safety and active shooter training were part of the discussion.
URI has a solid plan in place for dangerous scenarios but more communication about it seems needed; outreach and training are ongoing.

Williams noted a number of important items are on the docket for next week’s meeting but some of them are for discussion only and no action will be taken.
For example, concerns were expressed by faculty about the Security Cameras policy and APC staff is expected to present comments received and their response to them and to advance a new draft policy that incorporates some of that feedback.
A vote on the new draft will not occur until a subsequent meeting.
Pres.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 3
passages.text:
The policy has been developed with the help of a newly retained archivist who has broad responsibility for records, which include some academic records but other kinds of records as well.
Pres.
Williams also noted that he had asked for some changes to the Textbook and Course Materials adoption policy based on faculty feedback, and he believes his suggestions are being incorporated into a new draft.
Depending on the status of those revisions, that Policy may or may not be subject to a vote at next week’s meeting. 6.

VP Preisser noted he has arranged for a ‘FacultySenatePresident@uri.ed’ email to be rolled out on May 18.
This will be transferable annually to the new FS President and should be a helpful organizational tool for future officers, and it could provide a repository of ‘issue histories’ that may become important reference sources for senate leaders. 7.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 3

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 1
passages.text:
This initiative will need to be finalized under President-elect Preisser’s leadership.
A specific bill can perhaps be ready for action early in the fall, 2026 semester. 4.3 BAC survey regarding the budget model: results and their presentation - Some faculty have verbalized dismay at the survey results as presented on 4/16 and have suggested that the negative perceptions of the framework and its roll-out so far warrant a vote of no confidence in the current model.
Some have suggested that the faculty senate take up a Resolution to this effect.
FSEC members noted, however, that given the low survey response rate, it was difficult to draw any firm conclusions about budget model perceptions campus-wide.
Also, while the data itself may have limited utility due to the response rate, it can still be used in the on-going dialog with the administration as they continue to 1

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 2
passages.text:
schedule ‘town-halls’ on this subject.
Rather than take a dramatic action that could be counterproductive, faculty might instead commit to using the data available to shine a light on the need for improvements to both the model itself, and the outreach and communications around it.
FSEC members ultimately agreed that any formal resolution or ‘vote of no confidence’ would need to come at the end of an exhaustive process aimed at improving operations and communications.
If such an effort fails, a vote may become necessary, but because the conversation with administrators is continuing, it is likely not yet appropriate.
Senators and faculty are advised to keep collecting specific examples of the failings or shortcomings (‘pain points’) of the model and passing them along to relevant administrators to determine what/if solutions and remedies are available.
VP Preisser will add this to the list of items that need to be monitored next year and Pres.
Williams will continue to follow up with BAC Chair Triki and about appropriate use of the data (if any). 4.4 JCODL - It was noted that this item has been on the agenda many times and really deserves a vote on 5/7.
Pres.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 2
passages.text:
Williams will circle back with the CBUM and TAAC about their comments on the draft and ensure their support for the proposal.

Updates i.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 2
passages.text:

Williams, VP Preisser and VP-elect Trimm sat with the University President and Vice Provost this week for a very collegial and pleasant year-end meeting.
One item continues to be debated within the group, and this pertains to the perceived degree to which faculty input on various search committees is meaningful.
Many faculty report feeling like they’ve wasted time serving on these committees if, in the end, they are not afforded the opportunity to rank or vote to recommend candidates.
Apparently experiences across colleges and departments differ to some degree: when recruiting other faculty members, there may be some opportunities to vote or rank, but this is not true in all departments and is not true in the case of hiring administrators.
Faculty would like to see a more standardized approach, and would also like to feel like their efforts are not in vain.
An ideal outcome would be for the Provost’s office to promulgate standard procedures for searches and these should make clear that faculty 2

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 3
passages.text:
understanding of their respective disciplines is valued and an essential component in running recruitment efforts. c) Sen.
Daniels reported on a recent meeting with CIO Fariello on overhauling or possibly replacing the LMS.
Decision-making around this issue will likely be a lengthy process, initial steps of which will include identification of stakeholders across all colleges.
The Brightspace contract runs for five years and there is hesitation to lock into a long term without thoroughly examining needs and options.
Sen.
Daniels also reported on the status of the IT policies overhaul, noting that there was agreement among the working group members but the review by the General Counsel’s office had slowed all progress.
The process for advancing policies through the APC and that group's methods for addressing concerns/resolving comments was explained.
Pres.
Williams and VP Preisser are attending next week’s APC meeting and hope to report back on the status of these policies. d) Sen.
Trimm indicated he would request updates on faculty concerns about door locks and classroom safety during the upcoming PSCAC meeting.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 3
passages.text:
There is a need for systematic training, facilities upgrades, and bolstered security policies.

This suggestion has been passed to the APC in hopes a revision will be forthcoming. 5.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 1
passages.text:
VP Preisser introduced additional upcoming legislation regarding the Second Grade Option Bill, noting that undergraduate deans recently raised concerns following the Senate’s action to approve the Bill, identifying potential issues.
Discussion highlighted that colleges may retain flexibility to override the first grade.
A technical concern was also raised: if a student carries credits from a fall course into the spring and subsequently fails, adjustments to their credit load could be required, potentially resulting in significant financial implications for the student.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 2
passages.text:
2 iv.
SCLC Ombuds Bill: The SCLC Ombuds Bill remains largely unchanged; the committee expressed hope that a finalized text can be presented to the Senate for a vote in April.
It was emphasized that the Senate’s role is to update the manual, not to manage the Ombuds Office, and that the Ombuds should function independently without undue oversight.
Pres.
Williams noted that the University President supports the Ombuds being housed within the President’s office, but for logistical convenience, not for managerial control.
He will continue to provide updates as the situation evolves. v.
Continued discussion, Spring 2026 end-of-semester calendar: Continued discussion of the Spring 2026 end-of-semester calendar reflected broad agreement with earlier feedback favoring no immediate changes.
Vice Provost Adams reported that deans do not see a need for an additional instructional day.
VP Preisser suggested making up a missed Monday, while Sen.
Daniels noted that prior schedule adjustments for holidays are typically known in advance and that last-minute changes create burdens.
Sen.
Meenach raised logistical constraints related to classroom scheduling.
Pres.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 2
passages.text:
Williams emphasized that early-semester disruptions are typically managed in the classrooms over time and clarified that choosing not to act now does not preclude future changes.
Sen.
Trimm recommended a more formal Senate action to provide clarity, while VP Preisser proposed a middle-ground approach: communicating that the consensus is to make no changes at this time, while allowing for objections that could prompt a formal vote.
Pres.
Williams agreed to draft a carefully worded message to faculty reflecting this approach and preserving the option for a special session if needed. vi.
Student Senate Legislation: The Undergraduate Student Senate intends to propose legislation regarding a Syllabus Bank.
There has been no update provided at this time. 4.
Continued Items 4.1.
Faculty Concerns submitted through the FS Webpage: No new faculty concerns were submitted through the Faculty Senate webpage.
Follow-ups from previously submitted concerns were reviewed, and all items have been addressed. 4.2.
Resource guide for student mental health challenges: A resource guide for student mental health challenges was discussed.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 2
passages.text:
Emphasis was placed on improving awareness of and accessibility to information about existing resources. 5.
Updates/Ongoing Items 5.1.
Updates (meetings with administrators, other committee meetings): i.
President’s Stewardship Committee: This meeting focused primarily on the proposed creation of a medical school.
Key points included waiting for the state to approve initial funding as part of their budget process, followed by a URI Board of Trustees vote.
If approved, a founding dean could then be hired, initiating the recruitment of additional personnel.
The first student cohort could

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 3
passages.text:
3 enter as early as Fall 2029.
Start-up costs would be covered by state appropriations beyond the current University budget, plus significant additional donor funding with named donors targeted.
Consultants emphasized that the medical school would be fully integrated into existing university academics, offering a distinctive MD degree, and its students would be placed across the state in community healthcare settings, hospitals, and clinics.
The intent is to recruit heavily from Rhode Island and Southern New England, and to retain graduates in the state to address the state’s healthcare shortage. ii.
Meeting with President, Provost, Vice Provost 3/27/26: Topics included the end-of-semester calendar and the proposed medical school.
Discussion also included plans for the coming year to increase engagement with associate deans.
A follow-up meeting with deans is planned to continue these conversations. iii.
CASC work on program description standardization: The program description standardization initiative is ready to proceed; however, due to necessary summer 2026 updates to Kuali, implementation cannot begin over the summer and will be postponed to the fall. iv.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 3
passages.text:
Summer 2026 Kuali Updates: The Kuali Curriculum Management program will be updated to align with FSEC Bill 25-26-01 (“curriculum slimming,” revisions to UM Appendix E).
A plan for implementing these updates was presented, and coordination will occur between university leadership and the Senate office to communicate the updates and timeline to the university community. v.
Appeal from GSA re. closure of Graduate Village: The appeal remains on the to-do list and will be shared with the general faculty prior to the April Senate meeting. vi.
Other: Discussion included exploring options for rebalancing the workload and composition of curriculum committees. 6.
Report of the Coordinator: Apportionment letters with ‘notices to elect’ have gone to the colleges.
Results are to be transmitted to the FS office by 4/15/26. 7.
New Business : Sen.
Meenach raised a discussion regarding the evaluation of associate dean positions, noting that currently some associate deans are reviewed only by their dean.
She questioned whether new associate dean hires should also undergo a formal evaluation process.

passages.heading: Minutes | Page 3
passages.text:
It was noted that the Dean of Engineering does not review his associate deans, and concerns about this gap had been cited during evaluations of him.
Sen.
Williams indicated he will discuss the matter with university leadership, as the process is largely top-down and may vary depending on college bylaws.
Questions were also raised about faculty involvement, noting challenges in recruiting Senate members to participate in dean reviews and how this could extend to associate dean evaluations. 8.
Adjournment: The meeting adjourned at 2:20pm.

passages.text: JCODL Annual Report for AY 2023-2024

passages.heading: JCODL Annual Report for AY 2023-2024 | Page 1
passages.text:
Joint Committee on Online & Distance Learning Final Report 2023-2024 Committee Membership The committee’s roster for the 2023-24 was as follows: 1.
Farhad Atash, College of the Environment and Life Sciences (faculty) 2.
Amy Correia, College of Education (faculty) 3.
Jay Fogleman, College of Education, General Education Committee Chair (faculty) 4.
Chris Lavan, Associate Vice Provost, ATL, JCODL Chair (staff) 5.
Michelle Peach, College for the Environment & Life Sciences (faculty) 6.
Joannah Portman-Daley, Associate Director for Online Education & Instructional Design, ATL (staff) 7.
Nilton Porto, College of Health Sciences (faculty) 8.
Michelle Rogers, Director of Teaching & Learning Services (staff) 9.
Alicia Vaandering, URI Libraries (faculty) 10.
Anne Veeger, Vice Provost for Academic & Faculty Initiatives (faculty) Purpose of the Committee The purpose of the Joint Committee on Online and Distance Learning is to propose, examine, and recommend institutional policies and practices for developing, planning, and evaluating online and distance learning with a focus on quality, sustainability, and connection to the University’s mission, with approval of the Faculty Senate and Provost.

passages.heading: JCODL Annual Report for AY 2023-2024 | Page 1
passages.text:
Further, JCODL, considers faculty training, quality in delivery of online offerings, student learning outcomes, and ADA compliance regarding online and distance learning, as well as develops and implements strategic plans for online courses, certificate, and degree programs. (University Manual 5.78.10 - 5.78.11).
Executive Summary The committee discussed several topics during the 2023-24 academic year, and ultimately attempted to bring forth two proposals for review and consideration to the university’s Faculty Senate.
These two proposals (listed below) largely continued the work of this committee from the previous academic year (2022-23), focusing on two issues that the members of the committee supported to change or add to the university’s manual. 1.
Exam Proctoring Policy for Online Courses 2.
Adoption of Official Learning Modalities for URI Courses Exam Proctoring Policy for Online Courses On April 18, 2013, the Faculty Senate adopted Bill #12-13-33 entitled, “Exam Proctoring Policy for Online Courses”.
Due to evolving best practices in the field of online education, as well as

passages.heading: JCODL Annual Report for AY 2023-2024 | Page 2
passages.text:
the need to continue to provide a flexible and student-center educational experience at URI, the JCODL saw the need to recommend to the Faculty Senate that this policy be rescinded.
Members of the JCODL discussed this policy at length, then submitted their recommendation to the Teaching, Advising, and Assessment Committee (TAAC) for their consideration.
Ultimately, TAAC agreed, and proposed that this policy be rescinded during the Thursday, February 22nd Faculty Senate meeting.
Those voting members present for that meeting agreed to rescind the policy and this decision is noted in the Faculty Senate’s meeting minutes dated Thursday, March 28, 2024.
It is noted in those minutes that the President also agreed to this decision on March 6, 2024.
Adoption of Official Learning Modalities for URI Courses Over the course of the 2023-24 academic year, members of the committee discussed proposing new course modality definitions that would provide a more accurate summation of teaching approaches that are currently represented within the University’s academic catalog.
The final list of proposed modalities are listed below: 1.

passages.heading: JCODL Annual Report for AY 2023-2024 | Page 2
passages.text:
In-person - All instruction occurs in a specified physical location and on specified days/times. 2.
Hybrid - Instruction combines both in-person meetings on specified days/times and online asynchronous instruction.
The schedule of instruction and the weekly time commitment to online asynchronous instruction are clear to students in the syllabus on the first day of class. 3.
Online synchronous - All instruction occurs online at specified days/times. 4.
Online mixed - All instruction occurs online in a combination of synchronous meetings on specified days/times and asynchronous instruction.
The schedule of instruction and the weekly time commitment to online asynchronous instruction are clear to students in the syllabus. 5.
Online asynchronous - All instruction occurs online with no synchronous meetings required at specified days/times (outside of optional online office hour meetings).
The weekly time commitment to online asynchronous instruction is clear to students in the syllabus.
These modalities were supported by all members of the JCODL, recommended to TAAC, and— through a round of email communications—were ultimately agreed upon by both committees.

passages.heading: JCODL Annual Report for AY 2023-2024 | Page 2
passages.text:
Despite achieving support from both committees, the proposal was not able to gain the support needed to be discussed on the floor of the final Faculty Senate meeting of the year.
Additional Considerations of Note 1.
Attempt to revise the membership of JCODL - Immediate Past Vice Provost, Anne Veeger, and Associate Vice Provost and JCODL Chair, Chris Lavan, met with Faculty Senate Executive Committee (FSEC) leadership on behalf of JCODL regarding a proposal from FSEC to revise the structure of the JCODL.
Ultimately, action was not

passages.heading: JCODL Annual Report for AY 2023-2024 | Page 3
passages.text: taken on that proposal this year. However, discussions are ongoing regarding the committee’s charge and membership structure for the future. 2. ATL Blended Learning Specialist Search - The Office for the Advancement of Teaching & Learning, which directly supports the work of JCODL, held a search for a full-time staff position focused on blended learning and hybrid pedagogy. In the end, the search did not result in a new hire. However, JCODL supported the search, and discussions were had to revise and open the search again in the future with the potential to bring someone on board to provide greater expertise for faculty professional development around the new set of course modalities if approved in the future. Conclusion & Plans for the 2024-2025 Academic Year The following provides a short list of opportunities that members of JCODL could continue to explore and potentially recommend to the Faculty Senate for future consideration. 1. Recommend approval of the aforementioned course modalities and definitions to the general body of the Faculty Senate. 2. Develop a plan for enhanced instructor professional development around those course modalities, if approved. 3. Increase the understanding among members of the Faculty Senate (and beyond) that currently there are four pathways for URI instructors to become qualified to teach online. 4. Review current pathways for URI instructors to become qualified to teach online, discussing the maintenance, adjustment, and/or increase of current pathways. Discussion should include how to communicate to URI instructors the value and importance of these qualifications in regard to accreditation expectations, federal government educational standards, and intra-state educational guidance.
