Admission requirements: Applicants with an undergraduate degree in any field are considered for admission.
Applicants must submit an official URI Graduate School application, official transcripts of all academic work, two letters of recommendation, a resume outlining professional experience, a statement of purpose, and GMAT/GRE scores.
The GMAT/GRE score requirement is waived for applicants who meet at least one of the following criteria: (1) 5+ years of full-time relevant work experience, (2) URI graduate in any major with a 3.5 or higher GPA, (3) graduate from an AACSB-accredited business school in any major with a 3.5 or higher GPA, (4) hold a master’s or doctorate degree, (5) licensed as a CPA or CFA, or (6) passed Level II of the CFA exam.
For the M.S. degree, the graduate school requires an undergraduate grade point average of approximately 3.0/4 or above.
Typically, students are required to take the GMAT/GRE examination.
In some circumstances, the GMAT/GRE requirement is waived with a 3.5/4 or better GPA from many undergraduate majors, or a master’s degree or doctoral degree from any major.

Applicants for whom English is not the native language will be expected to demonstrate proficiency in written and oral communications through submission of TOEFL or IELTS scores taken within the last two years.
The URI Graduate School requires an undergraduate GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale for admission to the M.S. program of study.

Program requirements: All graduate-level courses offered in accelerated online programs by the College of Business are open to matriculated graduate students only. Constitution, By-Laws and University Manual Committee Report # 2020-2021-2 to the Faculty Senate Faculty Senate Meeting February 18, 2021 Proposal to Change Faculty Senate Committee Structure The following recommended changes update the University Manual language passed by the Faculty Senate referring to the recently revised Faculty Senate committee structure (FS Bill # 20-21-14).

passages.text: Constitution, By-Laws and University Manual Committee Report # 2020-2021-3 to the Faculty Senate Faculty Senate Meeting February 18, 2021 Proposal to Revise Definition of General Faculty Definition of General Faculty The Faculty Senate Executive Committee and the Constitution, By-laws and University Manual Committee recommend that the following changes be made to the UM in order to clarify the definition of General Faculty. This recommended change makes it clear that all faculty are members of the General Faculty and are welcome and have the right to participate in General Faculty meetings and the right to vote on matters requiring a vote of the General Faculty such as conferral of degrees and changes to the Constitution. Motion: accept recommended change to 4.11.10; 4.11.10 Membership in the University Faculty, also referred to as the General Faculty, shall be based on appointment by the President and on direct participation in or supervision of any of the following activities: teaching, librarianship, and research and creative activities, within the University. General Faculty includes those appointed to full-time tenure-track and non tenure-track positions. The General Faculty shall consist of tenure-track professors, associate professors, assistant professors, instructors (see 7.10.10); t The President, the Provost and Vice President for Academic Affairs, the Vice President for Research and Economic Development, the Vice Provost(s), and the academic dean and associate dean(s) of each college or school and of the library are also part of the General Faculty. #15-16-29

Landscape Architecture Landscape architecture is a 126-credit curriculum leading to the Bachelor of Landscape Architecture (B.L.A.) degree.
Accredited by the Landscape Architecture Accreditation Board of the ASLA, the curriculum is designed to prepare undergraduates for professional careers in public and private practice.
Landscape architecture is a profession that involves the design, planning, preservation, and restoration of the landscape by applying art, science, and technology to achieve the best use of our land and water resources.
Landscape architects design and plan parks, plazas, and recreation areas; residential, institutional and commercial developments; transportation facilities, new towns and campus landscapes, and green infrastructure.
They are also involved in planning and designing landscapes in coastal and inland developments impacted by climate.
The requirements of this curriculum include preparation in the basic arts and sciences.

passages.heading: #20-21-17B | Page 8
passages.text:
The major includes 63-64 credits of professional core classes (LAR 101, 201, 202, 243, 244, 300, 301, 302, 343, 344, 345, 346, 353, 354, 443, 444, 445, 447, 450); 28-29 credits of supporting requirements (ART 207; GEG 101; PLS 150; CHM 100, 101 or 103 or PHY 109, or GEO 100, or 103; CPL 410, CPL 434, 538; MTH 111103; and PLS 200); and 7-8 credits of supporting electives.
Students will also take general education classes and 6-7 credits of free electives.
Students accepted into landscape architecture are required to maintain a grade point average of at least 2.50 with no landscape architecture grades below a letter C.
Students failing to maintain this minimum may be removed from the program and required to reapply once this requirement is satisfied.
Students are required to own a P.C. laptop computer by the time they enter the program.
Specifications are available from the Landscape Architecture Program Office or from the URI Bookstore (Ramtech).
URI's Landscape Architecture Program (LAR) is competitive.
Accreditation standards regarding staff and facilities limit the number of students accepted into the major to 20 per year.

passages.heading: #20-21-17B | Page 8
passages.text:
While enrolled in the program, students will be reviewed twice during their course of studies: first for admission into the lower-division design sequence and again for acceptance into the upper- division B.L.A. major.
Admission into the lower-division design sequence courses (LAR 243 and 244) requires department approval.
Approximately 50 percent of the openings are filled by students who enter as incoming freshmen and who maintain a minimum 2.50 grade point average with no grades in LAR courses below a C.
The remaining openings are filled by matriculated students wishing to transfer into landscape architecture from other majors.
These students are required to apply to the program and to submit an essay and transcript of grades.
Applications and transcripts are evaluated in March each year for acceptance into the lower-division (LAR 243) design sequence for the following fall.
Acceptance into the upper division (junior design sequence) is based on submission and review of a portfolio of lower-division work, a current transcript, and written essay.
A maxi mum of 20 students per year are accepted into the upper-division B.L.A. curriculum.

Sports Media and Communication Catalog Description (2021-2022) In URI’s BA program in sports media and communication studies students gain critical and theoretical knowledge and practical experience in sports media, including, but not limited to, sports journalism, broadcasting, public relations, writing, communication, and sports data and analytics.
Courses range from critical-cultural analysis to quantitative and critical-analytical studies of sports media and communication.
Course work is coupled with practical and professional experience in various aspects of the sports media and communication industry via a required internship.
The program allows students to tailor specializations for careers in the sports media and communication industry by providing recommended elective courses across three suggested sequences from a variety of programs in the Harrington School of Communication and Media.
While students play an important role in curriculum planning, his or her program is closely supervised by an academic advisor.

Summary description of proposed program (not to exceed 2 pages).
The Department of Mathematics’ name does not accurately and fully reflect the research work, course and degree offerings, and trajectory of the department.
A more representative name for the department is the Department of Mathematics and Applied Mathematical Sciences.
Furthermore, with national trends leaning towards applied math, it is imperative that students (current and prospective) and colleagues (at URI and outside of URI) are aware of our applied math research and programs.

passages.heading: #20-21-17B | Page 14
passages.text:
This name change is expected to help us in recruiting students, developing research collaborations (both within and outside the institution), and attracting new hires in applied math.
According to the U.S.
Bureau of Labor of Statistics, “Employment in math occupations is projected to grow 27 percent from 2019 to 2029, much faster than the average for all occupations, and will add about 56,100 jobs.
Growth is anticipated as businesses and government agencies continue to emphasize the use of big data, which math occupations analyze.”1 Applied mathematics is very broadly defined as using mathematics to solve problems in a wide variety of fields of study.
The name applied mathematical sciences is more focused on applying mathematics to sciences, (including a recent trend in mathematical biology, a direction in which we intend to grow) and will include the department’s involvement in the fields of actuarial science (currently done as a double major with finance) and our growing work in data science.
The department officially voted to change the department name to Department of Mathematics and Applied Mathematical Sciences on September 14, 2020. 1 https://www.bls.gov/ooh/math/home.htm

passages.heading: #20-21-17B | Page 15
passages.text:
Degree Offerings.
The department has two track options at all levels, B.S. general and applied math option, M.S. pure and applied math track, and Ph.D. pure and applied math track.
The applied math tracks, at both the B.S. and Ph.D. level, have been offered for decades.
The B.S. applied math option is selected by the majority (over 67%) of B.S. math majors.
Because of this track’s popularity, in 2018 the faculty broadened the applied track offering at the M.S. level and also created the accelerated five-year B.S. – M.S. program in applied math.
Currently, more than half of our M.S. and Ph.D. graduate-level students are in the applied math track.
Additionally, the department is now in the process of creating a one-year graduate certificate in Applied Mathematics and exploring a Biomathematics minor.
With the College of Business, the department developed a curriculum outline that leads to a double major in finance and applied math (unofficially called pre-actuarial science track).
This curriculum prepares students for the first actuarial exam and provides a foundation for successful employment as an actuary.

passages.heading: #20-21-17B | Page 15
passages.text:
When funding was available, the department also brought students on well-received day trips to PricewaterhouseCoopers (PwC) in New York.
In fact, one of our recent applied math graduates, Lauren Black, has taken a position as an associate actuary at PWC directly after graduation.
A senior manager at PwC, Larry Rubin was consulted with structuring our current curriculum.
According to the U.S.
Bureau of Labor of Statistics, “Employment of actuaries is projected to grow 18 percent from 2019 to 2029, much faster than the average for all occupations.”2 Currently there are 9 double finance and applied math majors and the department seeks to expand interest in the area of financial mathematics.
Course Offerings.
The department has always had two course codes, MTH and AMS (Applied Mathematical Sciences) and offers numerous applied math courses, e.g.
MTH 441 Introduction to Partial Differential Equations, MTH 418/518 Matrix Analysis, MTH 471/571 Numerical Analysis, MTH 472 Numerical Linear Algebra, MTH 481/581 Optimization Methods, MTH 572 Numerical Partial Differential Equations, AMS 490 Intermediate Topics in Applied Mathematics, and AMS 590 Advanced Topics in Applied Mathematics.

passages.heading: #20-21-17B | Page 15
passages.text:
We also plan to propose, with the AMS course code, the following courses: AMS 210 Introduction to Mathematics Biology, AMS 310 Mathematical Modeling, AMS 410 Mathematical Biology, AMS 528 Mathematical and Computational Analysis of Data, and AMS/DSP 393G Introduction to Predictive Analytics.
Research/Activities.
In addition to having some faculty members with earned doctorates in Applied Mathematics, our faculty conduct research in applied math topics.
Areas include, but are not limited to, Numerical Linear Algebra, Mathematical Biology and Modeling, Financial Mathematics, Applied Probability, Combinatorics, Graph Theory, Partial Differential Equations, and Difference Equations.
Below is a brief summary of some of the work being done by our faculty. - Development of a statistical/linear algebra method that is used for computing the Principal Component Analysis (PCA) for extremely large data sets.
Used in numerous applications (e.g. image processing, genomics, robotics).

passages.heading: #20-21-17B | Page 15
passages.text: It was featured as a chapter in the book Handbook of Big Data, a bases for svds.m in the commercial software MATLAB, and the R-package (irlba) has been downloaded over 2,500,000 times.3 2 https://www.bls.gov/ooh/math/actuaries.htm 3 https://ipub.com/dev-corner/apps/r-package-downloads/ (need to type in irlba under Packages – select cumulative) 2

passages.heading: #20-21-17B | Page 16
passages.text:
- Development of probabilistic methods in different contexts: discrete structures as well as high- dimensional spaces.
Discrete random structures are essential in the design of algorithms and error correcting codes.
They are also used to model a large variety of objects in physics, biology, and network science.
Methods of high-dimensional probability play a central role in applications in dimension reduction in data science, signal processing, matrix completion, theoretical computer science. - Development of a new model for measuring connectedness in networks using local information that can be used in detecting artificially inflated importance in social networks. - Research in pursuit-evasion games on graphs provides theoretical underpinnings for real-life search and retrieval strategies - Research is being conducted on the statistical and econometric properties of the market microstructure (which happens every millisecond making this system hard to analyze).
Nowadays, trading is performed using an electronic double auction system where offers to buy are matched with offers to sell.

passages.heading: #20-21-17B | Page 16
passages.text:
Most stock exchanges in the world are operating within this new framework and while every exchange has its own rules, many follow the same principles.
An array that stores and displays the information of the price and the quantity at which people are willing to buy or sell certain asset is called a Limit Order Book.
Understanding its statistical properties has become of critical importance to many financial institutions such as banks, hedge funds and independent market participants to improve the way they perform their trades: via algorithmic trading. - Research is done in developing a systematic understanding and numerical methods in relation to polynomial and rational eigenvalue problems.
These problems arise either directly or as approximations of more general nonlinear eigenvalue problems.

passages.heading: #20-21-17B | Page 16
passages.text:
Some applications leading to nonlinear eigenvalue problems include vibrations of fluid-solid structures, structural dynamics, computational quantum chemistry, electromagnetic modeling of particle accelerators, and stability analysis of time-delay systems. - Classical mathematical models from population biology and epidemiology including the Leslie matrix model and the Lotka-Volterra predator prey and cooperation and competition models are based on difference or differential equations.
More recent models such as a model for the Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) and different respiratory viruses such as H1N1 and Covid-19 are investigated using as principal tool difference or differential equations.
In fact, the basic reproductive number as major indicator of severity epidemics is derived from the stability analysis of the basic difference equation model of epidemics.
In addition, difference equations models are used in modeling some phenomena in population genetics, cell biology, and physiology as well.

passages.heading: #20-21-17B | Page 16
passages.text:
Dept. of Math. of URI is major research center with 6 published leading monographs over 300 published papers and more than 20,000 citations in Google Scholar on the subject as well as more than 30 Ph.Ds completed.
Further, one of our math faculty is now the Program Director of Data Science (Nancy Eaton) and several of our math faculty are directly involved in the Data Science program (James Baglama, Jonathon Chavez-Casillas, Vasilije Perovic, and Lubos Thoma).
Lastly, the department has established a student chapter of the Society for Industry and Applied Mathematics, SIAM. 3

3HI UNIVERSITY OF RHODE ISLAND OFPICE OF THE PROVOST THINK BIO .005M MEMORANDUM To: Jeannette Riley,Dean,Collegeof Arts and Sciences From: Donald H.
De Hayes, Provost and Vice President for Academic Affairs Re: Interim Governance Date: October 28, 2020 Iam writing to designate you, as Dean of the College of Arts and Sciences, the interim authority responsible for the oversight of the Center for Peace and Nonviolence at The University of Rhode Island.
In that role, you will replace the Provost as the authority overseeing the Center.
In that role, please appoint an Interim Director and oversee the facuity senate process to formally transfer the responsibility for the Center from the Office of the Provost to the Dean of the College of Arts and Sciences.
In this designee role, you will have overall responsibility for the Center and its budgets.
The Interim Director, and ultimately the Director, will have responsibility for managing the operations, programs, and staff of the Center.
The Interim Director will report to you as the designated authority for the Center.

passages.heading: #20-21-29C | Page 7
passages.text:
Center History and Purpose My understanding is that the Center for Nonviolence & Peace Studies was given permanent status as a "Center" in 2002 and has reported through the Provost Office since that time.
The Center continues to be an important component for study and activism at the University of Rhode Island.
Asyouknow,we have begun working through the faculty senate process to transfer the responsibility for and the location of the Center from the Provost Office to the Dean of the College of Arts and Sciences.
In addition, our intention is to transfer the existing budget and also the course code relating to any existing or future courses offered by the Center.
However, until review and approval by the faculty senate has been completed, 1 ask that you serve as my designee responsible as the reporting authority for the Center and its Director.

passages.heading: #20-21-29C | Page 7
passages.text:
Assuming positive action by fhe faculty senate at some future date, the Center will then be officially relocated within the College of Arts and Sciences, although faculty and student involvement should continue to span colleges and departments at the university in keeping with the decidedly interdisciplinary purpose of the Center articulated when it was established.
As articulated in the original Center proposal, which was supported by the College of Arts and Sciences Curriculum Committee, the Center is “an interdisciplinary partnership for research, teaching, and outreach related to nonviolence and peace studies as applied to individual and community development, conflict resolution and reconciliation, and constructive social change.

passages.heading: #20-21-29C | Page 7
passages.text: A notable feature of the URl Center is the joining together of academic accomplishments of nonviolent leadership and social change of the past century, such as those of Gandhi and Martin Luther King Jr." The stated mission of the Center isas follows:"To institutionalize and internationalize nonviolence as a transformative educational process that reduces human suffering and promotes a global beloved community; to foster mutual understanding among people, in which nonviolent processes are used to reconcile conflicts and to build peaceful sustainable,and inclusive communities;to collaborate with and strengthen relationships with other organizations,agencies,and governmental departments engaged in peace building and nonviolence work at the local, national, and global levels; and fo accomplish this mission, the Centerfor Nonviolence &Peace Studies organizes and provides training and education opportunities for individuals,organizations,and com m unifies seeking to engage in the fundamental study of nonviolence and peaceful alternatives to conflict and violence." I appreciate your willingness to take on this additional responsibility.

Please let me know if you have questions, Thank you. c: M.

FACULTY SENATE OFFICE UNIVERSITY OF RHODE ISLAND FACULTY SENATE February 18, 2021 Faculty Senate Curriculum and Standards Committee Report 2020-2021-6 At the February 4, 2021 meeting of the Curriculum and Standards Committee, the following matters were considered and are now presented to the Faculty Senate.
SECTION II Curricular Matters Which Require Confirmation by the Faculty Senate PROGRAM CHANGES: COLLEGE OF ARTS & SCIENCES: Dept. of Criminology & Criminal Justice: (See Appendix A) Criminology and Criminal Justice major; Bachelor of Arts degree Updates to requirements: One set of changes involves elective classes only.
We propose removing CCJ 330, and replacing it with CCJ 280, “Introduction to Policing.” We propose a new upper level course, CCJ 480, “Critical Issues in Policing,” that follows in sequence after CCJ 280.
Both courses will count as criminal justice electives for our major.
We propose CCJ 280 in two modalities: face to face and online.
The other set of changes involves CCJ’s senior capstone requirement, general education, and elective courses.

passages.heading: #20-21-23B | Page 2
passages.text:
Historically, CCJ 476 has been the only capstone option; CCJ now proposes that students may choose between CCJ 476, CCJ 403, and CCJ 410.
This will 1) allow students greater agency in designing their curricular pathway by selecting a Crime and Justice "capstone" class that is focused on Policy (476), Race (CCJ 410), or Gender (CCJ 403) and 2) allow the CCJ program increased course scheduling flexibility by helping to alleviate some of the CCJ 476 graduation "bottleneck." As part of these proposed changes, we propose standardizing these courses so that each is similarly named and fills the same major and general education requirements.

Nutrition and Dietetics This curriculum leads to a Bachelor of Science (B.S.) degree.
This major prepares undergraduates for careers in nutrition-related fields.
Two options, dietetics and nutrition, are available.
The MS in Nutrition includes an Accelerated Bachelors to Masters of Science (ABM) option for students enrolled in the BS degree, described below.

passages.heading: #20-21-23B | Page 11
passages.text:
The major requires 23 credits in sciences (four in general chemistry [CHM 103/105], four in organic chemistry [CHM 124/126], three in biochemistry [CMB 210], eight in biology [BIO 220/221; 222/223], and four in microbiology [CMB 201]), 4 credits in applied general nutrition (NFS 210), 4-7 credits in introductory professional courses (NFS 110 and 212G and/or 276G); and 30-38 credits in the concentration including the following courses: NFS 336, 394, 395, 410, 440, 441, and 458 [capstone].
WRT 104, COM 100, and STA 220 are required and may be used to fulfill general education requirements.
There are 9-18 credits of supporting electives and 8-11 credits of free electives.
A total of 120 credits is required for graduation.
Students will be admitted to the nutrition and dietetics degree program after completing a minimum of 30 credits, including CHM 103/105, 124/126; BIO 220/221; NFS 210, 212G or 276G, 375 or 394; WRT 104; COM 100; and STA 220.
Students must have earned a 2.50 average in these classes with no less than a C in any one class to be admitted to the nutrition option, or a 3.00 average in these classes with no less than a C in any one class to be admitted to the dietetics option.

passages.heading: #20-21-23B | Page 11
passages.text:
Students may repeat NFS courses once.
Because of national accreditation requirements, students must complete a separate application form for admission to the dietetics option.
All students meeting the admission requirements for the dietetics option will be accepted.

This option is required of all students planning to become registered dietitians.
URI’s dietetics program is accredited by the Commission on Accreditation Council for Education in Nutrition and Dietetics (ACEND), 120 South Riverside Plaza, Suite 2190, Chicago, IL 60606, 800.877.1600, ext. 5400; https://www.eatrightpro.org/acend/.
Please see the department website for complete program information (https://web.uri.edu/nfs/ ).
In addition to the core courses specified for the major, the following courses are required: NFS 337, 375, 376, 443, 444, and BUS 341.
SOC 100 and PSY 113 are also required and may be used to fulfill general education requirements.
Students must maintain a 3.00 average in all required courses (NFS courses, science courses, and the remaining degree courses), with no less than a C in any one class, in order to graduate.
Students are encouraged to use supporting elective and free elective courses to study disciplines related to the field.
After completing their B.S. requirements, students can qualify for the professional title of Registered Dietitian by completing supervised practice requirements and passing a national exam.

passages.heading: #20-21-23B | Page 12

The supervised practice requirement is met by completing an ACEND- accredited dietetic internship program available to students on a competitive basis nationwide.
Admission to internship programs is highly competitive; students are encouraged to review the latest admission information on the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics website (https://www.eatrightpro.org/acend/students-and-advancing- education/information-for-students).
Internships may be combined with graduate programs in universities leading to an advanced degree.
Students who complete the academic and supervised practice requirements are eligible to take the national registration examination.

Summary description of proposed program (not to exceed 2 pages) The information age has brought advancements in technology and data collection techniques that produce an abundance of accessible data in all sectors and created a new paradigm for science, based on data-intensive computing.
The ever-increasing data is often unstructured and requires development of new techniques for storage, analysis, and effective decision making.
Data science is the study of complex data or big data.
It involves developing methods to collect, record, store, analyze, and interpret data to effectively extract useful information and detect patterns, trends, and relationships in data sets for decision-making purposes.
The data scientist is often a storyteller presenting data insights to decision makers in a way that is understandable and applicable to their interests.

passages.heading: #20-21-19C | Page 6
passages.text:
2 The field of data science, including data mining and machine learning, is interdisciplinary at its core, drawing upon skills in computer science, mathematics, statistics, and ethics.
Its primary goal is to gain insights and knowledge from any type of data, both structured and unstructured, and provide important resources to organizations that make data-driven decisions.
As new technologies are developed, data science will continue to grow in importance to business, industry, science, many academic disciplines, healthcare, and government in the years ahead.
Data scientists are employed in many settings, including finance & insurance, professional services, healthcare & social assistance, retail trade, and manufacturing.
Top industries hiring data scientists: Information Technology & Services, Computer Software, Internet, Financial Services, and Higher Education.
Although Hanover’s Market Opportunity Scan: National Degree Programs (Updated), prepared for URI in July 2018, does not explicitly address programs in data science, it does address the potential for a graduate certificate in Artificial Intelligence, which is closely related to machine learning, a core subject of data science.

passages.heading: #20-21-19C | Page 6
passages.text:
The market analysis suggests using the development of such a graduate certificate as "a vehicle for career advancement that requires less time and resources than a master’s degree.” Furthermore, the analysis suggests that "the labor market demand for artificial intelligence professionals is strong, and that related fields (including computer and information research science and software development) are projected to add 121,000 jobs per year between 2016 and 2026.” Indeed, not many online certificate programs in artificial intelligence exist today outside of one at Johns Hopkins and one at Stanford.
Regarding data science, Lewis University has an online Graduate Certificate in Data Science and Cornell has an online Graduate Certificate in Data Analytics, which has a business focus.
Today, the job prospects for Data Scientists are strong.
Currently, of the approximately 134,000 open job announcements for data science or data scientist listed on Indeed.com, approximately 1,700 are entry level positions.

passages.heading: #20-21-19C | Page 6
passages.text:
Since its inception five years ago, Glassdoor ranked Data Scientist as one of the top 10 best jobs in America, based on median base salary, the number of active job openings, and employee satisfaction rates, with a #1 ranking in 2016, 2017, and 2018.
LinkedIn’s 2020 Emerging Jobs Report ranks Data Scientist as #3 in the list of Top 15 Emerging Jobs in the U.S.
The report states, “It’s a specialty that’s continuing to grow significantly across all industries.
Our data indicates some of this growth can likely be attributed to the evolution of previously existing jobs, like statisticians, and increased emphasis on data in academic research.” Robert Half Technology, a search firm, produced the Salary Guide 2020, in which they list salaries for Data Scientists between $105K and $180K, depending on the geographical location, experience, and expertise of the employee.
They state that “upskilling” is a priority for most IT departments as they grow skill sets in-house.
After conducting a survey, they found that 90% of technology managers are upskilling some of their employees.
Data science and machine learning are among the most common areas for professional development.

passages.heading: #20-21-19C | Page 6
passages.text:
Companies upskilling in-house employees represent a potential market for this program, as they may fund their employees to enroll in this program as part of their professional development.
The time is right.
With the growth in jobs, will come learner demand and URI will have one of the first Online graduate certificate programs in data science offered by an accredited university.
This certificate, as is suggested in the Hanover report, will be marketed as a “vehicle for career advancement that requires less time and resources than a master’s degree.” There are many reasons why someone might seek a certificate in data science.
One may be looking to switch to a more lucrative career or improve their skills to achieve a higher level within their profession.
With job prospects decreasing in some areas, adding data science skills could greatly enhance career opportunities.
One may even wish to pursue a master’s degree but get started with a certificate that is more quickly obtainable.

passages.heading: #20-21-19C | Page 6
passages.text: This program targets professionals seeking recent data analysis methods and technologies that could be applied into their current work roles; recent graduates (including those from URI) that are looking to expand their skills and land into data science related jobs; recent graduates who are interested in graduate programs in data science and related fields; students interested in data visualization to develop and communicate insights about the data; professionals who need data science skills to contribute to other fields; and current students in graduate programs seeking skills in data science to apply to their discipline.

passages.heading: #20-21-19C | Page 7
passages.text:
3 This program is offered in the accelerated 7-week calendar format, a delivery method that provides flexibility to domestic and international students, working professionals, and active and reserve service members.
It complements URI’s undergraduate Data Science Program.
A master’s degree program in data science is being planned and this program is designed so that the credits earned from this program will partially satisfy the requirements of the master’s degree.
The Program’s main objectives are to 1) prepare students for careers in data-driven industries and sciences, 2) provide students who have domain area knowledge with the skill set to solve data-driven problems, and 3) prepare students for further graduate studies.

passages.heading: #20-21-19C | Page 7
passages.text: After completion of this Graduate Certificate program, students will have the ability to: ● work with large scale datasets from the perspective of database structures and storage ● manipulate and prepare data for program analysis ● identify and use the correct statistical methodology to solve real data-driven problems ● form data-driven questions and conduct analysis using perspectives of computer science, machine learning, statistics, and mathematics ● recognize the ethical implications of data on individuals and society ● extract insights from data through state-of-the-art data visualization techniques ● go beyond the data and the software to effectively communicate to non-technical audience ● synthesize knowledge and categorize data from various sources to solve problems in various fields ● use computational skills in interdisciplinary teams to solve problems in data-driven domains ● program in Java, R, Python, and SQL Students complete a research project in a domain area of their choice.

passages.heading: #20-21-19C | Page 7
passages.text:
This program prepares data scientists to excel in machine learning, management, analysis of large and/or unruly datasets, and visualization through an approach that privileges problem solving and collaborative research.
We expect 50-70 unique students to enroll in the certificate program each year, entering during any one of the six 7-week sessions.
Applicants will be expected to provide 1) college transcripts certifying successful completion of a Bachelor’s degree 2) two letters of recommendation from peers, mentors, or colleagues attesting to the student’s ability to complete graduate level coursework, and 3) a personal written statement explaining why the student is seeking a University of Rhode Island Online Graduate Certificate in Data Science.
One needs to have prior education in calculus, linear algebra, probability and statistics, programming in Python.
Students may be admitted under provisional status, followed by full admission once they complete the missing prerequisites.
Pre-requests may be completed at URI or at another institution, including open source courseware.
Accepted students will complete a sequence of five 3-credit classes for a total of 15 credits.

passages.heading: #20-21-19C | Page 7
passages.text:
They may take one course each 7-week session and complete the program in less than one year.
Since this is an online program, the expectation is that it will be funded through revenues generated by the program itself and no other revenue will be needed.

Form maintained by faculty senate office -08/16 Joint Committee on Academic Planning Pre--Proposal for New Programs Program Name: Data Science Degree Type: MS(thesis, non-thesis) and certificate program Proposer: Data Science Graduate Curriculum Committee (Joan Peckham, chair; Marco Alvarez (A&S), Ashley Buchanan (Pharmacy), Steven Cohen (A&S), Jeremiah Dyehouse (A&S), Nancy Eaton (A&S), Lisa Harlow (Health Sciences), Chris Hemme (Pharmacy), Gulver Karamemis (Business), Chris Parker (A&S), Gavino Puggioni (A&S), Jon Puritz (CELS), Yang Shen (GSO), Seung Shin (Business), Yan Sun (Engineering), Lubos Thoma (A&S), Maya Vadiveloo (Health Sciences)).
Department(s): Collaborative among several participating departments.
College(s): Collaborative among several participating colleges.
A&S, CELS, Pharmacy, Engineering, Health, and GSO.
Nursing has signaled interest in participating with one representative on the undergraduate curriculum committee.
Only a subset of these colleges will participate in the initial proposal and others will join later once they have human resources in place.
Part 1.
Briefly describe program.

passages.heading: #20-21-19C | Page 29
passages.text:
This is an interdisciplinary program in which all colleges and departments are invited to participate.
The program will have a set of core courses from CS, MTH, and STA that can be used in a thesis or non- thesis MS as well as a certificate program.
Using a model similar to that of the graduate programs in CELS, additional classes will be chosen by the student’s committee.
Faculty will be invited to affiliate with the program as eligible major advisors and curriculum committee members.
The curriculum committee will vet requests for affiliations.
The student and major advisor will submit a proposal to the graduate data science program for approval of the thesis topic and courses.
Faculty who are not affiliated with the Data Science Program will be permitted to submit similar proposals.
The Graduate Data Science committee will decide if the thesis topic and planned courses are sufficiently data driven and aligned with the intent of the data science program.
Please find attached a draft of the courses (and tracks) that are currently under consideration.
We have not included a required ethics class in the curriculums.
However, ethics is a required element of any data science program.

passages.heading: #20-21-19C | Page 29
passages.text:
The core courses will have required ethics modules and and/or include discussions that help students to understand that data science is never done in total isolation.
The intent will be to help data scientists learn to put into place practices that uncover and prevent intentional and unintentional misuse of data science techniques that may invade personal privacy, harm individuals, or discriminate against individuals or groups.
Resources needed: We will request that the provost work with the deans to appoint an interdisciplinary director for the program who will also lead the advisory committee.
In addition, the following will be needed: • Stipends to create the new classes that are needed • Data science faculty to teach new classes in the departments that are offering them

passages.text: Form maintained by faculty senate office -08/16 Part 2. How does the program connect to the mission of the University and the strategic themes and goals of the Academic Plan 2016-2021? There is explicit language in the Academic plan devoted to Big Data, HPC and Data Science and the development of research and academic programs. See Goal 2, Strategy 5 Part 3. Signatures Proposer: Date: 5/3/19 Chair(s): Date: Dean(s): Date: JCAP Review Committee Response: Date: May 28, 2019 XX We urge you to move the proposal forward for further development We urge you to re---consider the proposed program Comments: The committee voted unanimously that the degree plan is encouraged to move forward, with the following important feedback: • Consider modeling the program’s governance structure on the requirements of the Graduate School (e.g., who are the core faculty, and who are not core faculty, in order to set up student thesis committees.) • There is still a great deal of work to be done on the curriculum - the core classes make sense, but consider narrowing the focus away from having so many courses and tracks. • A data science focus may be more valuable to employers and would be easier to sustain, rather than all of the concentrations. • Consider adding a data science pod or track to existing bachelor’s degrees to build subject matter expert skills in particular areas. • Consider making the path to the degree go through the College of Business. • Consider “stackable” certificates – i.e., three 12 credit certificates makes a Master’s or something similar.

Summary description of the proposed organizational change The proposed change is to transfer the Department of Landscape Architecture from the College of Arts and Sciences to the College of the Environment and Life Sciences.
The transfer will result in the relocation of a design program that offers an accredited BLA and educates students about profession of landscape architecture and focuses many of its project assignments on addressing issues of community and urban design, sustainable design and coastal resilience, and ecological and environmental design and planning.
At any given moment, the average number of students in the department averages between 55 and 70.
It should be noted that our sophomore class is typically filled and capped at 20.
Our average graduating class of is 16.6 over 10 years.
LAR will also bring to the college an existing Graduate Certificate in Community Planning, minors in both CPL and LAR and the desire to create a new master's program.

passages.heading: #20-21-28C | Page 4
passages.text:
This relocation will strengthen the college by adding a design unit with visualization capabilities and a track record for collaborative problem-solving and award-winning service-learning studio project.
The move will enhance LAR'S positioning for research, and it will make it easier to collaborate with the 2

RATl ONALE: There should be a demonstrable purpose and documented need for the proposed organizational change. 1.
Explain why the organizational change is being proposed.
Background: Collaborative Discipline - Landscape architecture is a collaborative discipline that interacts with diverse fields and disciplines, such as art and architecture, planning and engineering, and the natural and social sciences.
It is profession whose practitioners and students work to solve problems that affect our communities and neighborhoods, natural and built environments and coastal cities and towns.
Its students learn to use planning and design, art and technology, and construction and visualization while working with professionals and stakeholders with a range of skills.
Their work requires that they develop skills in design, CAD, GIS, modeling.
Photoshop and other visualization technologies for developing and illustrating plans and proposals for neighborhoods, parks and streets and coastal communities.
The students also learn to work in teams, with different disciplines and with stakeholders on challenging projects around the state.

passages.heading: #20-21-28C | Page 6
passages.text:
As the profession has matured and environmental problems become more complex, the need for interdisciplinary teamwork and professionals able to lead and integrate others into their work is a recognized quality that is often found in landscape architects. s a e (o) po g ua and preparing students for careers in the profession.
Many offices in Rhode Island, Boston and New York hire our graduating BLA's.
Out of 16 BLA graduates in 2019, and in Raleigh Durham, Nc, four found jobs in landscape construction, one works in a planning office in MA and another went to get a graduate degree at RISD.
Interdisciplinary studios - LAR Studios have included MESM, Marine Affairs (MAF) and visiting architecture students in its studios.
Some have also collaborated with classes from Ocean Engineering and Environmental and Natural Resources Economics service -earning studios have worked for many of the cities and towns across the state as well as on projects for the University of Rhode Island.
A move to CELS comes with recognition of the role that interdisciplinary and trans disciplinary collaboration plays in design practice today and it would become more available to students and 4

Why a move to the College of Environment of Life Sciences: Over the past 15 months meetings between Landscape Architecture (LAR), the Provost and the Dean of Arts and Sciences exposed a change in college priorities suggesting that LAR did not fit the new model for A&S, which would impact future resources for the department, including for faculty.

After discussion with John Kirby, the dean of the College of the Environment and Life Sciences, we believe we will have those opportunities by joining CELS, and it will allow requesting to move into a college (CELS), with which we are familiar and share many of the same interests, values and concerns.
We will continue offering an accredited BLA with the intention of developing a master's degree in the future.
Our department will remain a standalone unit.

We can partner on research proposals, provide design services to local cities and towns, instruct students at URl and abroad while preparing students for careers addressing the key issues of our time.
We can add graduate students at URl and our five general education classes can increase the numbers of students taking our classes.
We are confident that by leading interdisciplinary and collaborative studios for skilled undergraduate and graduate students, through the BLA and future ABM (accelerated bachelor and masters) and/or professional masters, as well as working to improve the EPD track of MESM, and the Graduate CPL Certificate that LAR will be able to help the college achieve its goals outlined in the 2018 - 2023 Strategic Plan and referred in section C.1 below.

A move to CELS will allow the department to carry on with its rmission, which is consistent with both the Goals articulated in the University of Rhode Island's Academic Strategic Plan 2016-2021 and in the CELS Strategic Plan 2018-2023 which follow: Both plans stress innovation and focus on providing an education that can Enhance Student Success, lead to competent Research, Scholarship and Creative work, Grow a Global Presence, and Embrace Diversity and Social Justice (UR), all of which the department of landscape architecture provides through courses, field trips, conferences and lectures, and through valuable service learning studio projects conducted for neighborhoods and municipalities.
Through the latter projects, students experience interdisciplinary collaborations, stake holder interactions and numerous professional class visits.
LAR student work often leads to public recognition and awards, and ultimately to jobs.
Difficult as it is to do, the department also encourages students to study abroad, and to understand the important role that diversity, history and culture play in shaping the landscape.

passages.heading: #20-21-28C | Page 8
passages.text:
The LAR curriculum addresses the University academic and research goals of Educational Excellence through innovation and student success, Research and Perspective, and Diversity and Social Justice.
Themes in LAR current projects and future research include Local to Global Environmental Change, (connectivity), Agriculture and Food Systems (design, provide and protect), Human and Environmental Health and Communities, and seeing things with a multi-scale view from microbes to humans. 6

2.
For the past fifteen months we have discussed a possible relocation to CELS and Individual faculty from LAR have met with department chairs and other faculty, but additional meetings are needed to work on strategies for greater collaboration, enhanced interdisciplinary studio-learning, and new methods for using upper-level students and alumni to offer assistance to non-majors needing workshops for learning basic design and graphic technologies.
There will also be increased opportunities for LAR students, in particular, graduate students, to take classes from departments within CELS.
D.
INTER INSTITUTIONAL CONSIDERATIONS: The organizational change should be consistent with all policies of the Council on Postsecondary Education pertaining to the coordination and collaboration between public institutions of higher education. 1.
The Bachelor of Landscape Architecture program is the only degree of its kind offered at any public institution within the State.
There are four accredited BLA institution), University of Massachusetts, University of Connecticut and University of Rhode Island.

passages.heading: #20-21-28C | Page 9
passages.text:
Because of their distant locations from each other, there is little interaction that occurs between these schools.
Proposed changes will have no significance to the structure of the institution, nor do they change the opportunity for students from Rhode Island to receive an accredited degree, which is one requirement for becoming licensed in the state as a landscape architect.
Statistically, there are 97 accredited landscape architecture programs in the US and 27 institutions have a single degree of BLA or BSLA. 2.
There are no cooperative arrangements with other institutions to provide landscape architecture classes or faculty to other institutions.
The Department of Landscape Architecture BLA degree is associated with the New England Regional Student Program offering tuition incentives to students from Maine, Vermont and New Hampshire.
This status will not change. 3.
There are no external affiliations associated with the Department of Landscape Architecture.

One of the structural revisions and innovations of the online MPA program is the creation of three certificate programs that offer students with both core training in public administration and policy but also specializations mirroring the Public Management and Policy Analysis concentrations in the current program. The three 12-credit graduate certificates in the online MPA program are the Professional Certificate in Public Administration and Policy, Public Management, and Policy Analysis. (See Appendix C) 1 New Program

Summary description of proposed program (not to exceed 2 pages) Since its founding in the 1970’s, the mission of the Master of Public Administration (MPA) program at the University of Rhode Island is to instill public values, knowledge, and expertise to

passages.heading: #20-21-22C | Page 4
passages.text:
2 prepare our graduates to solve problems related to governance, nonprofit management, and policy with integrity, professionalism, and excellence to improve our communities and society.
To train our students to meet the challenges of the 21st Century, the MPA program is embarking on a series of program revisions and a transition to a fully online program to meet the current and anticipated future needs from employers and various stakeholders across Rhode Island, the region, and nationally.
Although the MPA program will transition to a fully online, accelerated (7-week) format and replace its current blended, 14-week modality, the MPA program will retain many of its successful core features, including the requirement that MPA graduates earn 36 credits.
The accelerated online MPA program also incorporates new curricular innovations that will expand student recruitment and student flexibility.
Additionally, the programmatic and curricular revisions outlined in this proposal are critical for the program to become accredited by the Network of Schools of Public Policy, Affairs, and Administration (NASPAA) – a long-standing goal of the program – in the coming years.

passages.heading: #20-21-22C | Page 4
passages.text:
One of the structural revisions and innovations of the online MPA program is the creation of three certificate programs that offer students with both core training in public administration and policy but also specializations mirroring the Public Management and Policy Analysis concentrations in the current program.
The three 12-credit graduate certificates in the online MPA program are: the Professional Certificate in Public Administration and Policy, Public Management, and Policy Analysis.
Students in the online MPA program will need to complete the Professional Certificate in Public Administration and Policy graduate certificate, at least one of the other two MPA graduate certificates, earn at least 36 credits, and complete the capstone course to complete their MPA degree.
The core certificate that forms the basis for the MPA online program is the Professional Certificate in Public Administration and Policy.

passages.heading: #20-21-22C | Page 4
passages.text:
Students completing this certificate program will have an opportunity to learn about the historical and theoretical foundations of public administration and policy (PSC 501), ethical decision-making strategies (PSC 504), diversity and inclusion in the public sector (PSC 502), and an elective course focused on developing core skills or experience for a career in government, non-profits, or policy.
All students who want to earn their MPA degree will be required to complete this graduate certificate.
In addition to the certificate in Public Administration and Policy, students choosing to graduate with an MPA degree can choose to complete either one or two additional MPA-offered certificates that form the basis of an added credential or specialization that will make graduates competitive in the job market.
The first is a certificate in Public Management.
The coursework required for this certificate will help students become competitive applicants for positions requiring financial and budgetary expertise (PSC 506 & PSC 507), leadership skills, knowledge of administrative law and procedure (PSC 573), and the management of agency personnel (PSC 503).

passages.heading: #20-21-22C | Page 4
passages.text:
Currently, there is an acute need in many cities and towns for Finance Director positions, which can be a town or city’s highest paid municipal position.
Additionally, these are skills increasingly

passages.heading: #20-21-22C | Page 5
passages.text: 3 sought by nonprofit organizations. By creating a certificate program, we hope to fulfill this workforce need in the state of Rhode Island and beyond by offering incumbent employees and new students the opportunity to develop a competency in Public Management. Our aim is to have incumbent workers trained so that they will have opportunities for advancement, and their advancement will, in turn, create entry-level opportunities for others pursuing a certificate in Public Management or our students completing the MPA program. The second of these optional certificates is the Policy Analysis certificate. The coursework required for this certificate will help students develop research and analytical capabilities (PSC 583 & PSC 510), evaluate public programs (PSC 505), and navigate the public policy process (PSC 524 & PSC 510). These skills will allow them to become effective at shaping public policy either within public agencies or as part of a broader policymaking process. Students pursuing this certificate will develop skills that will allow them to be policy advocates, policy researchers, and/or communication specialists. The underlying philosophy of the URI MPA online program is that its modular design will guide students along pathways that will allow them to align their graduate study with their career ambitions. MPA graduates will have earned no less than 36 credits while completing the program. All students completing the full 36-credit program will: • Complete the Professional Certificate in Public Administration and Policy (12 credits);

passages.heading: #20-21-22C | Page 6
passages.text: 4 • Complete either the Policy Analysis certificate (12 credits) and/or the Public Management certificate (12 credits); • Complete the remaining 12 elective credits if only one certificate program is chosen between the Policy Analysis certificate or the Public Management certificate. Graduates may choose to pursued a stackable certificate in another program to add alongside the two MPA certificates. Upon approval of the online MPA program, the Department of Political Science will develop an Advanced Bachelors-to-Master (ABM) program for undergraduates seeking to enter the MPA program by completing twelve credits during their senior year. These courses would not be offered by URI Online but are instead delivered through our traditional 14-week program. These courses will include: • PSC 402-Environmental Politics and Policy (4 credits), • PSC 405-Politics of Health and Aging (4 credits), • PSC 590-Internship in Public Administration (4 credits), • 4 credit policy or public-management related courses. Another potential entry into the MPA online program will occur at the certificate level where students may decide to enroll in the MPA program during or following the completion of one of the certificate programs. B1.
State the program objectives.
The mission of the URI MPA Online program is to instill public service values, knowledge, and expertise to prepare graduates to solve problems with integrity, professionalism, and excellence to improve our communities and society.
Goal 1: to lead and manage in governance. 1.1 Describe and analyze the theoretical, legal, and conceptual foundations of the fields of public administration and public policy. 1.2 Gather information and analyze the internal and external environments surrounding public and nonprofit agencies to develop leadership or policy strategies.
Goal 2: to participate in and contribute to the policy process. 2.1 Identify, diagnose, and convey to policymakers real policy or management-related problems and solutions that affect the policy process, public management, or public policy outcomes.

passages.heading: #20-21-22C | Page 7
passages.text:
Goal 3: to analyze, synthesize, think critically, solve problems and make decisions. 3.1 Apply appropriately tailored analytical skills to interpret and solve real policy or management- related problems.
Goal 4: to articulate and apply a public service perspective. 4.1 Inform and advise policymakers about policy or management-related problems in ways that advance the public interest, respect the rule of law, promote democratic participation, and treat people fairly. 4.2 Demonstrate personal integrity and inspire public confidence and trust in public service by developing, individually and in teams, work products that adhere to the highest standards of professional conduct.

passages.heading: #20-21-22C | Page 8
passages.text:
6 Goal 5: to communicate and interact productively with a diverse and changing workforce and citizenry. 5.1 Effectively communicate with multiple audiences in policy or public management related settings. 5.2 Collaborate with a diverse collection of stakeholders to solve public policy and public management-related problems.
B2.
Explain and quantify the needs addressed by this program, and present evidence that the program fulfills these needs. a.
What is the economic need and workforce data related to the program?
The design of the MPA online program is not only aligned with NASPAA accreditation guidelines but also meets the growing workplace needs in Rhode Island, the region, and nationally.
To gauge the current and future hiring needs of employers in the public and nonprofit sectors, the MPA director, Dr.
Aaron Ley, conducted a series of meetings with key government and nonprofit stakeholders throughout the state over the last two years.
The meetings included the Rhode Island League of Cities and Towns, the Rhode Island City and Town Managers Association, and various other state agencies like the Rhode Island Secretary of State’s office, among others.

passages.heading: #20-21-22C | Page 8
passages.text:
These meetings revealed the growing need of individuals with management and finance backgrounds because employees currently holding these positions are beginning to reach the age of retirement.
These discussions were confirmed through the Director’s own anecdotal experience in Bristol where the town’s finance director chose to take a position closer to home.
During that hiring process for the replacement, the town observed that very few people in its applicant pool were qualified to fill this position.
Nationally, municipal Finance Director positions are among some of the highest paid municipal employees.
In order to address this workforce need, and as part of our migration of the MPA program to an online format, we are proposing the development of a stackable Public Management Certificate that will allow our students to enter our program in order to develop skills relating to public budgeting and finance.

passages.heading: #20-21-22C | Page 8
passages.text:
This will allow incumbent workers and entry-level workers to quickly earn a competency in public management by completing a suite of four courses to fulfill this certificate, while also giving them the option of remaining in the program to complete the MPA Online program by completing the other 24 credits.
We hope that the training of incumbent workers will create opportunities for their advancement, which will create entry-level opportunities for others pursuing a certificate in Public Management or our students completing the MPA program.
This stackable certificate can be used by MPA students desiring a special competency in the area of public management, or for students in other graduate programs wanting to use their remaining electives to gain public management skills.

passages.heading: #20-21-22C | Page 9
passages.text:
7 These information gathering meetings on public and nonprofit sector workforce development needs also revealed a need for the upskilling of incumbent workers and the training of more entry-level employees with analytical skills relating to public policy.
One case in point was a conversation with Rob Rock, the Director of Elections at the Rhode Island Secretary of State’s (SOS) office, and an alum of the URI MPA program.
Mr.
Rock stated that the high priority legislation that is being pursued by the SOS office requires a lot of research and analysis of data.
His observations were confirmed during conversations with Rhode Island Secretary of State Nellie Gorbea.
To fulfill this workforce need, we are proposing the creation of a stackable Policy Analysis certificate, which can be pursued by MPA students in conjunction with the Public Management certificate or by students in other programs who are wanting to use their electives to pursue a credential that bolsters the student’s policy analytical skills. b.
Provide information on jobs available as a result of successfully completing the certificate or degree: job titles, job outlook/growth, and salaries.

passages.heading: #20-21-22C | Page 9
passages.text:
Students completing an MPA degree with the Professional Certificate in Public Administration and Policy, along with a certificate in Policy Analysis and/or Public Management will be competitive applicants for positions requiring financial and budgetary expertise, leadership skills, knowledge of administrative law and procedure, the management of agency personnel, policy and grant writing, and analytical skills.
Currently, while there are no data regarding salaries for employees earning certificates, there is extensive survey research that exists on salaries of alumni holding an MPA/MPP degree.
According to a 2018 survey administered by the Network of Schools of Public Policy, Affairs, and Administration (NASPAA), over half of all graduates surveyed with an MPA made over $65,000 after three years of having earned the degree (https://www.naspaa.org/data-center/alumni-survey).
Of those receiving an MPP/MPA degree, 48% were employed in government careers, 22% in nonprofit careers, and 18% were employed in the private sector.

passages.heading: #20-21-22C | Page 9
passages.text:
Four percent of respondents completing the 2018 survey were unemployed, while 8% of respondents chose “other.” An ideal federal placement for a student with an MPA and a certificate in Public Management, Policy Analysis, or the Graduate Certificate in Public Administration and Policy would be as a “Contract Specialist” at the Department of Navy’s Naval Undersea Warfare Center.
The salary for such a position is $64,873 to $111,062 per year.
The basic requirements for contracting positions include a Bachelor’s Degree and 24 semester hours of finance, legal, and management-related training.
More about this position can be found at the following link and the table below describes a variety of employment opportunities that are offered by the federal government

passages.heading: #20-21-22C | Page 10
passages.text: 8 when “Rhode Island” is used as the search term for location: https://www.usajobs.gov/GetJob/ViewDetails/556347400. It should also be noted that as the URI MPA program moves fully online and we continue our pursuit of NASPAA accreditation, our program will compete regionally and nationally, expanding the geographical range in which our graduates will be applying for positions.

passages.heading: #20-21-22C | Page 11
passages.text: 9 Agency Position Description Salary Dept of US Financial $52,905 – Navy Management $178,000 Analyst (GS 9-15) Community Planner (GS 5-15) $33,949 - $166,500 Program Manager (GS 5-15) $33,949 - $166,500 Management and Program Analyst (GS 5-15) $33,949 - $166,500 Department Management and Program Analyst (GS 12) $76,721 of Treasury Tax Analyst (GS 12) $76,721 An ideal municipal placement for a an MPA graduate already having a history of professional experience along with a certificate in Public Management would be a position that at the time of this writing is being advertised by the Town of Burrillville for Finance Director. Depending on experience, a position as Finance Director for a small town the size of Burrillville would come with a salary of about $70,000 to $85,000. According to the Bureau of Labor Statistics, the job outlook for positions relating to public finance, budgeting, and public policy is positive. MPA graduates with the

passages.heading: #20-21-22C | Page 12
passages.text:
10 Public Management certificate will be well-positioned to compete the positions requiring a public finance and budgeting background.
For financial management positions, the agency predicts that there will “be high demand over the decade” (https://www.bls.gov/ooh/management/financial-managers.htm#tab-6).
These types of positions are on the higher end of the job scale for MPA graduates successfully completing the certificate program and would very likely be those already with significant professional experience.
The median salary in 2019 for a financial manager is $129,890.
The Bureau of Labor Statistics expects this employment sector to experience higher than usual growth at a 16% rate between 2018-2028 and could be where incumbent workers find opportunities for advancement.
A more likely scenario would be an MPA graduate receiving a certificate in Public Management, Policy Analysis, or the Professional Certificate in Public Administration and Policy and later being employed as a budget analyst.

Budget analysts are responsible for financial management in public organizations and, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics, receive a median 2019 salary of $76,540 (https://www.bls.gov/ooh/business-and-financial/budget-analysts.htm).
The BLS expects that this job-related sector will experience 4% growth from 2018-2028.
Other potential job titles related to the MPA degree and the Public Management Certificate are listed on the Bureau of Labor Statistics database as clerk ($35,390 median pay; little job growth), emergency management director ($74,590 median pay; faster than average growth at 5%), human resources manager ($116,720 median pay; faster than average growth at 7%), purchasing manager, buyer, or agent ($69,600 median pay; decline in growth), urban and regional planner ($74,350 median pay; much faster than average growth at 11%), social and community service managers ($67,150 median pay; much faster than average growth at 13%), administrative services manager ($96,940 median pay; faster than average growth at 7%), and community and social service specialists ($43,790 median pay; no estimate for growth).

C1.
Explain how the program is consistent with the published role and mission of the institution and how it is related to the institution’s academic planning.
Our program’s mission is to prepare students to solve problems related to governance and policy with integrity, professionalism, and excellence to improve our communities and society.
By bringing the MPA program online and creating three additional credentials

passages.heading: #20-21-22C | Page 13
passages.text:
11 in Public Management, Policy Analysis, and the Professional Certificate in Public Administration and Policy, our objective is to allow graduate students to learn the management, budgeting, financial, and analytical skills necessary to govern effectively and advance in public management, policy analysis, and governance-related positions in Rhode Island and beyond, which will advance URI’s core mission values of ethical leadership, engaged learning, and civic leadership.
Specifically, the three online certificates and the overall MPA Online program will “[e]xpand online course offerings for all students and for targeted populations (adult learners) [Strategy 1]…[and] Facilitate[s] the implementation of new learning pedagogies and expand[s] modes of course delivery…by leveraging space and time in new ways [Strategy 3].” The 7-week accelerated nature of the online program is also aligned with Strategy 6 of Goal 1, which encourages programs to “ensure timely completion of advanced degrees” because it introduces students to accelerated versions of our MPA core courses that can be used toward the overall fulfillment of the MPA degree requirements.

passages.heading: #20-21-22C | Page 13
passages.text:
Our Professional Certificate in Public Administration and Policy, which all MPA Online graduates are required to complete, specifically contains a curriculum that embraces aspects of URI’s goal related to embracing diversity and social justice.
Public management professionals work daily with diverse populations in the workplace and so students completing the online program will be required to complete a 3-credit course called “Diversity and Inclusion in Public Administration and Policy” that explores issues of diversity, equity, and inclusion, with content related to institutional and systemic racism, policy issues relating to diversity and inclusion, equitable hiring policies and recruitment for the public sector, and cultural competency.

The MPA Online program will be deeply interconnected to many of the current URI degree and educational programs due to the creation of three certificates associated with the program.
Some graduate students, for instance, may be interested in careers relating to public health, the environment, nonprofit management, or other governance-related fields.

passages.heading: #20-21-22C | Page 13
passages.text:
Students entering these policy fields may wish to add either the Public Management or Policy Analysis certificate to bolster these skills.
There is also the potential of “stacking” our certificates along with other online certificate programs around the university (e.g., Community Planning, Labor Relations, Human Resources, Cybersecurity) in such a way so that the combination of earned certificates creates a clear pathway to the acquisition of an earned master’s degree in our MPA program.
To earn an MPA degree, students can use these certificates or elective courses from other programs to satisfy the final 12 elective credits needed for the MPA degree if they do not opt to complete all three of the MPA-related graduate certificates.
Our development of certificate offerings will create opportunities for other students around the university to pursue certificates that align well with their career

Bringing our MPA program online will also bring our program back into line with the MLIS program, which has transitioned to a fully online program, so that students interested in public service careers related to libraries and other professions related to that degree can fulfill those career ambitions through our joint MLIS-MPA program.

The Roger Williams University online MPA program requires the completion of 36 credits and currently offers certificate programs in Public Management and Healthcare Administration.
One of the key differences between our proposed MPA online program and RWU’s is the structure of course delivery and the certificates that are available through the program.

RWU MPA students are not give the opportunity to complete a certificate in Policy Analysis.
In addition to tailoring our focus on the budgetary, financial, and personnel management skills needed to excel as public managers, and the analytical skills that are needed to effectively shape public policy, students wishing to pursue only a certificate through our program can do so by completing four courses (12 credits), whereas RWU students must complete a minimum of five courses in order to be eligible for the certificate (15 credits).

Descriptions of New Courses PSC 502 - Diversity and Inclusion in Public Administration and Policy (3 credits) This course examines issues of diversity and inclusion in the public and nonprofit sector, particularly how representative public organizations can be created and how public policy can be designed in order to serve people of all diverse backgrounds.
PSC 508 - Policy and Grant Writing (3 credits) This course explores grant writing, grant seeking, and grants management in the public and nonprofit sector, as well as effectively writing public policy proposals to contribute to the shaping of public policy.

1 Budget Justification MPA Online Program Description: The MPA Online program is an accelerated online program that allows graduate students to learn the professional, public management, and policy analytic skills necessary to govern effectively and advance in public management and governance-related positions.
After graduating from our program, our students will be able to lead and manage in governance; participate in and contribute to the policy process; analyze, synthesize, think critically, solve problems, and make decisions; articulate and apply a public service perspective; and communicate and interact productively with a diverse and changing workforce and citizenry.
Students graduating from our program will have completed 36 graduate credits and the completion of at least two of the following three graduate certificates offered by the MPA program: Professional Certificate in Public Administration and Policy, Public Management Certificate, and a Policy Analysis Certificate.
Enrollment Estimates: We calculated enrollments estimates in consultation with the Office for the Advancement of Teaching and Learning.

passages.heading: #20-21-22C | Page 51

Due to the online program having a flat rate for tuition, we did not need to distinguish between in-state and out-of-state students.

Based upon ATL’s experience with bringing other programs into an online format, our consultation with that office led to conservative estimates of 75 students (which roughly translates into 300 3- credit courses) beginning in the program for FY2022, growing to 135 students (which roughly translates into 540 3-credit courses) in the program in FY 2025.
Please see the notes section in the budget form for an explanation Tuition Revenue Estimates: The cost of in-state tuition per student, which will be the One Rate Tuition, for FY22 is currently $803 per credit.
