The Master of Art in User Experience/User Interface (UX/UI) Design is a stackable master's that combines the four-course Graduate Certificate in User Experience Design, developed by WRT, and the four-course Graduate Certificate in User Interface Design, created by ART, augmented by two additional courses.
The thirty-credit program will prepare students for meaningful careers in the burgeoning fields of UX/UI.
This online accelerated dual-focus curriculum offers students— including those with full-time jobs—a flexible path to gaining proficiency with the tools and approaches of the closely related fields of UX and UI research and design, opening a broad range of lucrative career opportunities.
Students emerge from this program as versatile professionals capable of addressing complex design challenges.
Their skills span from the intricate details of UI elements to the strategic considerations of holistic user experiences.
Armed with the knowledge of both UX and UI, graduates become adept at designing solutions that merge aesthetics, functionality, and human-centered values.
The program is unique in its emphasis on the ethical implications of research and design processes and products.

passages.heading: #23-24-20 | Page 133
passages.text:
The UX Certificate nurtures an understanding of user behavior, needs, and expectations through rigorous research, ensuring accessibility and accessible design.
UX courses guide students in creating designs that prioritize inclusivity, social justice, sustainability, and user well-being.
They also offer students cutting-edge approaches to UX writing and interaction design.
The UI Design Certificate provides students with the crucial knowledge, and the technical and practical skills, to become proficient UI designers.
Students will create interface projects integrating branding, animation, patternmaking, and front-end visualizations to depict intuitive user experiences, enabling them to craft interactions that leave a lasting impact.
Students in the Master's Program are able to take UI Visual Principles for Non-designers, which helps them develop a unique approach to the design process with the user interface experience in mind (advanced designers may also select an approved elective from other URIO offerings).
The two certificates then culminate in WRT/ART 509: UX/UI Portfolio.

passages.heading: #23-24-20 | Page 133
passages.text:
In this cross-listed course (WRT and ART), students integrate and apply the knowledge and skills they have gained in their UX and UI Design Certificate courses to create compelling, effective, polished portfolios that demonstrate their expertise to potential employers and clients.
Additionally, the course will focus on professionalization for careers in UX, UI, and related design fields.
Graduates of this program will have the capability to examine how individuals navigate real-life scenarios, empowering them to enhance experiences by creating new design-centered connections.
They will possess the abilities to recognize limitations and openings for enhancing interactions between objects, systems—whether virtual or physical—as well as the people who interact with them.
In an ever-evolving technological landscape, the Master of Arts in UX/UI Design equips students to stand at the forefront of innovation, transcending traditional boundaries between the two fields.
Graduates leave prepared to meet industry demands and set new standards that enrich the lives of users, making a positive impact on society.

passages.heading: #23-24-20 | Page 133
passages.text:
Strategy 1 in the Agenda for Change is deeply embedded in the goals and learning outcomes of this program.
The Master's in UX/UI emphasizes the application of ethical, collaborative design practices to solve real-world problems, focusing on inclusive design, design justice, person-first design, and designing for the social good.
Students will learn to engage in design processes that prioritize the needs and perspectives of diverse user populations.
By understanding the principles of inclusive design, they will acquire the ability to create solutions that cater to a wide range of users, ensuring accessibility and usability for all.

Action 2: Grow URI Online to increase access for all students at every life stage.
The online accelerated program will open doors for recent college graduates as well as working professionals to enter the exciting fields of UX/UI; they will become eligible for positions and promotion in a burgeoning job market.
The program will employ cutting-edge pedagogy to help students distinguish themselves as leaders in today's workforce.

In December 2022, Forbes notes "User experience (UX) design, and the closely related field of user interface (UI) design, will become increasingly valuable skills due to the extent to which digital transformation is effectively turning every company into a tech company and every job into a tech job." News of layoffs in tech is misleading for a variety of reasons (including temporary pandemic-related expansions and post-pandemic contractions).
When examining the UX job market potential, The New York Times states that “a majority of tech jobs are at companies outside the tech sector in industries like banking, retail, health care, and manufacturing.” Along these lines, UX/UI professionals are also essential to nonprofit organizations, and our program uniquely positions students to work in the service and civic design fields.
UX/UI is an in-demand facet of web development and digital design, which, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics is growing at a rate of 23 percent.
Websiterating.com records a minimum of 1.97 billion websites in existence as of January 2023 with more than 4 million apps.

1 year 30 30 1 0 No UX Certificate WRT 501: Ethical Foundations of UX explores the ethical considerations and responsibilities involved in designing digital experiences for users.
Through a combination of theoretical concepts, case studies, and practical exercises, students will gain an understanding of the ethical challenges faced by user experience designers and develop strategies to create user- centered and ethically sound designs.
Students will explore UX as a research and development method, especially as it relates to inclusive design and design justice.
Students will learn about foundational concepts in UX design, including terminology, history, and evolution of the field.
Using a critical lens, students will investigate issues of social justice, equity, sustainability, accessibility, and inclusion.
WRT 502: UX Research and Methods is an introduction to methods, research design, and data analysis in user experience projects, and aims to prepare professionals for designing, conducting, analyzing, and reporting their own user research studies.

passages.heading: #23-24-20 | Page 137
passages.text:
This course will train students in how to determine the best methods and metrics for their projects, as well as design studies for effective data collection.
This course will also teach students how to communicate research results for decision-making purposes to a variety of stakeholders.
Students in this course will gain hands-on practice at every phase of the user research process, from identifying design problems or questions to developing their own test protocols, recruiting users, conducting user tests, and analyzing their results.
WRT 503: UX and Microcopy Writing is designed to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of the role and impact of effective writing in user-centered design.
Through a combination of theoretical concepts and practical applications, students will develop the skills necessary to create clear, concise, and engaging microcopy for digital interfaces and interactions.
WRT 504: Interaction Design focuses on the process of rapid, iterative design that keeps real people at the heart of creating content—a philosophy and design approach known as human-centered design.

passages.heading: #23-24-20 | Page 137
passages.text:
Students in this course will learn agile design workflows, conduct rapid prototyping and wireframing, and share reflections on the process and results of user research meaningfully for public and industry audiences.
Students will gain hands-on, applied knowledge of the human-centered design process by creating their own design and refining it based on user feedback.

ART 505: UI Design: Styling and Prototyping introduces students to the theory and practice of user interface design, focusing on visual communication tools and skills to facilitate prototyping.
Students will acquire a knowledge of the UI design thinking process, centering on the user's visual experience, which is crucial to how users interact with an interface.
Students will learn how to collaborate as a visual designer in creating interactive screen-based interfaces for websites and apps, creating visual components while considering their interactive properties, look and feel, responsiveness and interactivity and recognizing the multiple human factors, audiences and contexts that govern their design decisions.
ART 506: UI Motion Design introduces motion design in user experience within a framework of the three foundational principles of communication, orientation, and correlation.
Students will learn how motion design can complement visual affordances to provide users with more meaningful experiences and interactions.
It explores motion design as a sequence of movements that affects the user’s perception of any interface a user interacts with.

passages.heading: #23-24-20 | Page 138
passages.text:
ART 507: UI Icon Design introduces and develops the skills needed to conceptualize and design icons for user interfaces.
The context, design and application of UI icons will be critiqued based on the effectiveness and appropriateness of the design language.
Students will learn to generate UI icon sets through a process that explores visual rhetoric and shape form creation through a logical visual process.
This course provides an overview of the nature and purpose of icons in user interfaces, their key characteristics, and aesthetic rules commonly used in websites and apps.
ART 508: UI Information Visualization Design focuses on the design, creation, understanding, application, and evaluation of information visualization for user interfaces.
Students will learn strategies and techniques to organize, visualize and communicate information and how to implement them on multiple platforms.

passages.heading: #23-24-20 | Page 138

Faculty Senate Executive Committee Report 2023-2024-02 - Proposed amendments to Appendix G Faculty Senate - March 28, 2024 Rationale: The primary change proposed relates to increasing clarity in the reference to Policy #80-1 in Appendix G.
When the Faculty Senate authorized migrating administrative policies previously listed in Appendix G to the Administrative Policies website, an error was introduced wherein Policy #80-1 regarding Faculty Senate jurisdiction over policies was inadvertently deleted.
The Faculty Senate Executive Committee found no evidence that the Faculty Senate ever rescinded the missing Policy, gave an informational report on this matter to the Faculty Senate on October 19, 2023, and reposted a link to the policy in Appendix G along with a brief explanation about what had occurred.
Because Policy #80-1 codifies a power and duty of the Faculty Senate relating to the approval of administrative policies, it is appropriate and important to include not only a link to the policy in this Appendix but also clear details about the content of the policy and the codified role of the Faculty Senate in the administrative policy development and approval process.

passages.heading: #23-24-20 | Page 144
passages.text:
Additional changes aim to 1) accurately reflect the relationship between academic policies and collective bargaining agreements and state and federal statutes and regulations, 2) clarify the nature of the University Manual as the official policy document where policies are not only described but also codified through legislative processes, and 3) correct an error in fact (it is not the President of the Faculty Senate, but rather the entire body of the Faculty Senate that has the authority to jointly own policies).
Proposed changes to Appendix G: University Policies In recognition that the University Manual has been created through the framework of shared governance between the university faculty and administration under the University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees, it is the source of information regarding the structure, rights, regulations, and practices that govern university life.
The Manual is considered to be the official university policy document articulating shared governance and, as such, takes precedence over other internal policy statements inconsistent or conflicting with the Manual.

Program Description The Major.
Film/Media is an interdisciplinary major offering hands-on experience in documentary, experimental, narrative, and new media production, balanced with an emphasis on international cinemas, �lm/media history, criticism, and theory.
Our curriculum re�ects the dynamic and diverse nature of this �eld, approached from a perspective of �lm history and media theory.
Students learn to work with the evolving and overlapping technologies involved in the production of moving images (including �lm, digital video, 3D animation, game design, and new media), with an understanding of the broadening and globalization of their cultural and aesthetic contexts.
A wide range of courses is available to the �lm/media student—courses that examine the historical, theoretical, and global approaches to the analysis and creation of moving images.
The �lm/media program prepares students for careers in such areas as independent �lmmaking; animation and media design; �lm and television industries; advertising, marketing, and public relations; and media criticism.

passages.heading: #23-24-22 | Page 16

Graduates of this program are also prepared to continue with graduate studies, either in �lm and media production for an M.F.A., or in a master’s or doctoral program in �lm and media studies.
Students majoring in �lm/media must complete a minimum of 31 credits (maximum 46) in approved courses toward the major.
FLM 101 or FLM 101H is a required prerequisite.
All students must complete the core courses: FLM 110, FLM 203 (or ENG 302), FLM 204 (or FLM 205 or 206), including the senior-level seminar FLM 495 (or FLM 496); a minimum of 6 credits from the production and technique category and 6 credits from the critical studies category; a minimum of 3 elective credits in courses that count toward the �lm major from the Production and Technique and Critical Studies categories (see below).
This wide range of choices in �lm/media courses permits students to design a major that will meet both personal and professional goals.
Students must have a plan of study approved by an academic advisor in the �lm media program before beginning their coursework in the major.

The study and practice of journalism require the acquisition and application of a broad base of knowledge, so journalism majors at URI pursue a course of study that is strongly grounded in the liberal arts.
Along with general education and elective courses from other disciplines, the major requires students to explore the concepts and professional practices of contemporary journalism in a diverse society.
While studying the social, historical, legal, and ethical contexts of journalism, students also learn how to gather and critically assess factual information and communicate it clearly to a variety of audiences in all forms of media.
Journalism “skills courses”-through individual and collaborative assignments-focus on reporting, writing, editing, and producing news for all forms of news media: print, broadcast, and multi-media. “Conceptual” courses provide students the intellectual foundation and framework to be responsible journalists.
Through its general education course offerings, the Department of Journalism provides non-majors a forum for studying the importance of journalism and the role of the mass media in society.

passages.heading: #23-24-22 | Page 22
passages.text:
Students majoring in journalism must complete a minimum of 3130 credits (maximum 45) in journalism.
All journalism majors must complete JOR 115, 220, 221, 310, 410, and 411420.
In addition, students must select nine credits from skills courses: JOR 320, 321, 330, 331, 340, 341, 420, 430, 441 and three credits from conceptual courses: JOR 210, 211, 215, 311, 313, 415.
Any journalism courses may be chosen for the remaining three credits.
Students are encouraged to consult with their advisors about the mix of journalism courses that best meets their goals.
The only journalism courses open to freshmen are JOR 110 (for non-majors), 115 (for majors), and 220.
Students must earn a grade of C or better in JOR 220 to enroll in the next-level course.
Only three credits of JOR 220 may be used to satisfy graduation requirements.
The Harrington School of Communication and Media requires students in each of the six undergraduate majors to also complete the Harrington core requirements.: SCM 105 and capstone course (FLM 495, FLM 496, JOR 420, SCM 495, PRS 490, or WRT 495).
A total of 120 credits is required for graduation.

The Major.
This major is designed for undergraduate students who seek to expand their repertoire of writing for various professional and public audiences.
Graduates will have a strong foundation in Writing Studies theory balanced with a wide range of situational practices common to contemporary professional and public writers.
Coursework includes in-class learning, writing technology practice, peer and instructor feedback, and experiential �eldwork in real-world settings.
All graduates design their own digital electronic portfolios prior to graduation, demonstrating their ability to work with a range of technologies to produce and distribute their audience-focused, effective writing.
Professional and Public Writing majors must complete 30 credits (maximum 51) including the core courses of WRT 104, 235, 371G, and 495.
At least 15 credits for the major must be completed from writing courses numbered 300 or above.
Majors are strongly encouraged to complete a practicum experience, such as an internship (WRT 477) or a �eld experience course (WRT 383 or 385).
A maximum of three credits for each of these experiential courses can count towards the major, unless the project substantially changes.

passages.heading: #23-24-22 | Page 29
passages.text:
Undergraduates wishing to take a 500- or 600-level course must secure the instructor’s permission.
Students selecting this major may but are not required to pursue a concentration in either Technical Writing or Professional and Civic Writing.
To complete a concentration, students take nine credits from among the following: Technical Writing: WRT 306: Writing Health and Disability; WRT 332: Technical Writing; WRT 334: Science Writing; WRT 375: Human-Centered Design; WRT 477: Internship in Writing and Rhetoric; WRT 533: Seminar in Graduate Writing in the Life Sciences; WRT 534: Visualizing Environmental Advocacy Professional and Civic Writing: WRT 227: Business Communications (to be renamed Professional Writing); WRT 235: Digital Writing and Rhetoric; WRT 302: Writing Culture; WRT 303: Public Writing; WRT 305: Travel Writing; WRT 321G: Writing Disaster —the Ethics of Representation; WRT/PRS 331: Writing Public Relations; WRT 388: Proposal Writing for Clients; WRT 404: Writing with Community Partners.

Students choosing Professional and Public Writing at URI can pursue careers as professional and technical writers, which are required by a vast array of industries, nonprofits, and governmental organizations.
A double major in Professional and Public Writing is advantageous for students across the University, as the major increases their value to potential employers.
According to the 2021 NACE Job Outlook Report, excellent written communication is in the top five attributes required by employers.
Some of the many jobs available to graduates with this degree include Technical writer Science writer UX writer Content designer/creator Social media manager Medical writer Grant writer Copywriter Editor Publications manager Contracts associate/manager Policy writer Proposal writer Press secretary Development/advancement associate/manager Marketing associate/manager Communications associate/manager In particular, the U.S.
Bureau of Labor Statistics asserts that technical writing occupations will grow 12 percent from 2020 to 2030, faster than the average for all occupations; the median wage for technical writers is $74,650.

passages.heading: #23-24-22 | Page 33
passages.text:
The Bureau projects the growth of jobs for writers and authors at 9 percent with a median pay of $67,120.
Students completing this degree are also prepared to pursue graduate degrees in publishing, writing studies, and other fields.
Students from ME and CT who major in WRT are eligible for reduced tuition through the New England Regional Tuition Plan.
Several universities in the region offer degrees in writing in various forms, but we offer unique courses, expertise, and highly innovative pedagogical approaches.
Based on our research, we anticipate that the proposed changes will make our major more competitive and better situated to attract and retain students and enhance our ability to prepare them for the workforce.
With our community partnerships with organizations such as iFixit, IGT, the National Park Service, Providence Stormwater Innovation Center, the Manissean Tribe, South County Habitat for Humanity, the Rhode Island Food Bank, and others, we are strategically positioned to meet the needs of regional organizations and to serve as a catalyst for localizing civic, technical, science, and professional writing.

The Early Childhood Care and Education (ECCE) undergraduate certificate program for Post Baccalaureate, Pre-K-2 Certification is for those who have completed their undergraduate degree to be certified as a teacher and advance in their teaching profession.
At least 30 hours per week of the incumbent workforce candidate’s active teaching are required; other non-traditional work conditions with RIDE approval can be considered.
The ECCE program will be offered fully online through URIOnline with field experience in the candidates’ own PreK-2 teaching setting, running 7-week accelerated sessions, including a summer session, for 2 years.
The Pathway 2: Undergraduate Certificate, Pre-K-2 Certification requires a bachelor's degree in Science or in Art and to complete pre- professional course requirements prior to admission.
The ECCE program is designed to meet the needs of the incumbent early childhood care and education workforce to access high-quality teaching certificate programs in order to improve teacher quality and student learning.

passages.heading: #23-24-22 | Page 55
passages.text:
Aligned with the URI mission, the SOE & CEPS strategic plans, and the Early Childhood Care and Education (ECCE) Strategic Plan for Rhode Island, this program is designed to ensure that the incumbent workforce of early childhood educators has accessible, high- quality, and meaningful pathways toward credential attainment, career advancement, and higher compensation.
This program is supported by The RIDE Educator Pathways Planning Grant.
As the State’s public learner-centered research university, the University of Rhode Island values (1) creativity and scholarship, (2) diversity, fairness, and respect, (3) engaged learning and civic involvement, and (4) intellectual and ethical leadership (URI mission statement).
Enriching its mission, with a long history in teacher education and working with clinical educators in the workforce, URI ECCE is capable of fulfilling its mission and is capable of developing and offering the 6 most innovative and accessible pathways for both undergraduate level and TCP candidates in the ECE workforce in RI.

passages.heading: #23-24-22 | Page 55
passages.text:
It is also aligned with the URI visions and goals, supporting student success through the most affordable accessible degree programs and the teacher certificate program (TCP), in particular.
The proposed program for working professionals, along with this certificate program, is well aligned with the URI Strategic Plan: Enhancing Students Success (Goal 1).
Developing and offering the most innovative and accessible pathways for the ECCE workforce is a viable means of ensuring that we fully meet URI Goal 1.
In short, this ECCE Educator Pathway Program is well aligned with the URI goal 1, strategies 2 and 6, in particular.
As stated in the URI goals, the URI ECCE team will focus on the most affordable institute to support the underrepresented and economically disadvantaged in the state population’s incumbent ECCE workforce by facilitating the implementation of new learning pedagogies and expanding modes of course deliveries.
The proposed program will strengthen Early Childhood Teacher Education at URI and across the state of Rhode Island by supporting student success through the most affordable, accessible degree program for the target population.

Changes Program Description Program Educational Objectives.
Three to �ve years after graduation from the B.S. in mechanical engineering program, graduates will: 1) Successfully practice mechanical engineering to serve state, local, national, and international industries and government agencies. 2) Work professionally in one of the two major stems of mechanical engineering: mechanical and/or thermal systems or related �elds. 3) Achieve personal and professional success with an understanding and appreciation of ethical behavior, social responsibility and diversity, both as individuals and in team environments. 4) Pursue continued life-long learning through further graduate education, short courses or other training programs in engineering or related �elds.
Student Outcomes.
Mechanical engineering students demonstrate knowledge in all outcomes required by ABET, Inc. which are listed in the college’s student outcomes section of this catalog.
Program Description.
The curriculum provides a thorough and well-rounded foundation in basic science, mathematics, engineering science, and general education to prepare the graduate for a professional engineering career.

passages.heading: #23-24-22 | Page 80
passages.text:
The curriculum is also excellent preparation for graduate school.
The program is strong in providing a background in design, solid and �uid mechanics, systems engineering, and the thermal sciences, including energy and energy transfer.
Computer applications are stressed throughout the curriculum.
All undergraduates are invited and encouraged to join the student section of the American Society of Mechanical Engineers, which sponsors industrial plant visits, special lectures, and other activities.
Students may also join chapters of the Society of Automotive Engineers (SAE) and the American Society of Mechanical Engineers (ASME).
The work in the �rst two years consists of basic courses in science (math, physics, chemistry), applied science (mechanics, electricity and magnetism, basic computer literacy and computer-aided problem solving), manufacturing processes, and general education requirements (humanities, social sciences, English communication).
Two introductory engineering courses are included in the freshman year.

passages.heading: #23-24-22 | Page 80
passages.text:
The junior year concentrates on fundamental mechanical engineering courses (thermodynamics, �uid mechanics, systems engineering, engineering analysis, heat transfer), materials sciences, and design of machines.
Further general education studies are also covered.
The senior year includes the capstone design sequence, mechanical engineering experimentation, and a wide variety of professional electives such as mechanical control systems, advanced �uid mechanics, advanced mechanics of materials, mechatronics, internal combustion engines, applied energy conversion, tribology, product design for manufacture, air conditioning, heating and ventilation, vibrations, �nite element method, and experimental stress analysis.
The program also includes two laboratory courses in the junior and senior years.
Further general education studies are also covered.
Computer techniques are integrated throughout the curriculum.
Computational facilities including PCs and workstations are available in the College of Engineering’s Engineering Computer Center (ECC) and the University’s O�ce of Information Technology Services (ITS).

Currently there is not an existing stand-alone degree program in NFS to prepare students for careers outside of the prescribed program for preparation of Registered Dietitian training.
In the past, students have found confusion around what to do with the Nutrition subplan outside of Dietetics due to the subplans under the same B.S. degree.
This stand alone degree will provide students who do not wish to pursue the RD credential a more clear degree pathway.
These students will examine how food and nutrition impacts systemic, biochemical and molecular health, the relationship to the food system and real world applications to physical and mental health.
The coursework in the NFS Nutrition degree is very well suited for a variety of post-baccalaureate careers as well as preparation for numerous graduate and post-professionals programs in health-care related fields and settings.
Eight of the top 15 most needed jobs according to indeed.com are health-related jobs, making it one of the desirable areas of study for both job security and income.

passages.heading: #23-24-22 | Page 100
passages.text:
Graduates with this degree can find employment at major research centers, biotechnology, pharmaceutical, and nutraceutical industries, community nutrition programs, non-governmental organizations, the fitness industry and more.
A Nutrition degree can be the foundation for career opportunities in areas such as: Food and Nutrition Management, Public Health Nutrition, Education and Research, Consultant, Related Health Professionals (such as Chiropractor, Dentist, Naturopathic Doctor, Physical Therapist, Physician, Physician Assistant, Podiatrist, Veterinarian, and Nursing), Business and Industry, Media, International Food Organizations, Public Policy / Government.
This degree will have approximately 50% course work in Nutritional Sciences, dietetics and real-world health application with 50% course work in sciences, psychology and healthand science-related electives.
This suggested coursework will prepare students for direct job placement, further education in post-professional health related programs, research-based graduate programs or jobs related to nutrition and public health.

Most other public, state universities in New England offer two B.S. degrees, one in Nutrition and one in Dietetics.
The proposal of a new B.S. degree in Nutrition will keep URI in alignment with other competing universities in New England: UMASS: Nutrition and Society UVM: Nutrition and Food Science UNH: Nutrition and Wellness; Nutrition (2 B.S. degree options) Students will be admitted to the nutrition degree program after completing a minimum of 30 credits, including CHM 103/105, 124; BIO 220/221; NFS 210, 212G or 276G; WRT 104; COM 100; and STA 220.

passages.heading: #23-24-22 | Page 102

This is not a new program, but a differentiation between the prescribed RD program and the customizable Nutrition degree.
We do expect an increase in the number of students who enroll in the Nutrition degree, once the differentiation is made.
With the increasing interest in post-professional health related degrees, research and graduate education and community nutrition, we feel this will be an attractive major.
This major is unique to human health and the relationship to food and energy metabolism.
While other hard sciences majors such as biology and chemistry touch upon these topics, Nutrition relates all scientific processes directly to humans and human health, thus strengthening the preparation for work in the human healthcare field.
We hope to attract new and incoming students by outreach and education of the major in local high schools, as well as draw students with interest in human health who may have entered URI as undeclared, particularly CHS undeclared.
Due to the increased need of health professionals, desire for wellness and nutrition education, this major will draw students passionate about understanding the imperative role of food and nutrition in human health.

COLLEGE OF EDUCATION: Early Childhood Education - TCP - Cert Appendix C To ensure Pre-K to 2nd grade certification program remains relevant and compliant, we propose necessary updates to its course requirements for Post-Baccalaureate TCP in Early Childhood Education.
These updates are prompted by the discontinuation and modifi cation of several key courses, alongside the imperative to align with Rhode Island Department of Education (RIDE) Pre-K to 2 teaching certificate standards.
Summary of Proposed Changes: 1.
Course Replacement for Discontinued Content: EDC 328 is designated to replace HDF 305, which is no longer available.
EDC 316 (3) will replace HDF 308 (4 Credits).
The courses previously cross- listed as HDF 420/EDC 421 will now be consolidated under EDC 421.
These adjustments address the unavailability or the significant c ontent changes in the HDF courses that no longer meet the Early Childhood Education (ECE) degree requirements and the RIDE Pre -K to 2 CASC Report 2023-2024-1B Page 1 of 152 GC Report 2023-2024-11B Page 1 of 152

passages.text:
teaching certificate standards. 2.
Reclassification of EDC 328: Given its specialized content, EDC 328 will be reclassified as a professional core course, aligning our curriculum with professional standards and educational best practices.
These proposed changes are designed to ensure our curriculum not only meets the foundational requirements of early childhood education but also offers flexibility and depth.
A total of 58 credits are required for the PreK-2 teaching certificate but depending on their undergraduate degree, students will complete between 42-58 credits.
The courses required include the following: - Professional Contents: HDF 200, HDF 208, EDC 102, EDC 250, EDC 312, EDC 316; - Early Childhood Education Core Courses: EDC326, EDC 328, EDC 336, EDC 402, EDC 421, EDC 424, EDC 426/350, and EDC 461; - Practical teaching residency: EDC 484 and 485.
Education - MA TCP Appendix D Recently the Rhode Island Department of Education changed the World Language teacher certification system.

passages.heading: #23-24-22 | Page 112
passages.text:
Due to these changes, graduates from our current MATCP Education World Language program are now certified to teach in Rhode Island at all levels of elementary, middle, and secondary education (grades PK -12).
The new program proposal is intended to address the changes in Rhode Island certification regulations, which will require small changes to the requirements for our current BA in Secondary Education with a specialization in World Languages, effectively transforming it into an MATCP Education World Language All Grades Program.
The proposed changes affect significantly less than 25% of the credit requirements.
In the proposed new program, students will take a variety of existing EDC courses in Elementary Education, Early Childhood Education, Secondary Education, and Teaching English as a Second Language / Bilingual Education concentrations so that, upon graduation, they will be more versatile and highly employable educators who are better prepared to teach effectively in a wider variety of educational settings.

passages.heading: #23-24-22 | Page 112
passages.text:
The newly proposed EDP 609 will now be a required CORE course.
The new course (609) focuses on critical theories in education.
This new course aligns with the new program focus of preparing equity-oriented scholars who will apply, critique, design, and implement cutting edge research to improve educational opportunities across all levels of the educational spectrum.
New program plan attached.
The SLOAA map does not change with this minor course adjustment. (Attached) Learning and Development - Cer t Appendix F We are requesting a change of the program name from Learning and Development to Training and Development for the following reasons: · Data from URIOnline Marketing show that potential applicants are confused by what the name of the program means. · Data from URIOnline admissions shows that those who are clicking on the website are not continuing on to request information and submitting an application.
Many people think the program is for K -12 teachers.

passages.heading: #23-24-22 | Page 112
passages.text:
Also, it appears that only people already in the field of L & D understand what the name means so if we want to attract people new to the field or who are interested in the field, we need to move to a name that is more recognizable. · A scan of programs around the country show many use Training or Workforce Development in addition to L & D, further clarifying their purpose.
We believe this change will solve the issues we have had with misunderstanding the purpose of the program.

NEW CERTIFICATES, SPECIALIZATIONS, AND MINORS COLLEGE OF ENGINEERING: Industry 4.0 Graduate Certificate Appendix M In response to the growing demand for Industry 4.0 expertise and the need for accessible education, we propose the launch of a Graduate Certificate Program in Industry 4.0.
This program aims to provide specialized knowledge and skills to a diverse range of students, including recent graduates seeking to enhance their qualifications and working professionals who desire to stay current with the latest technological advancements in their industries.
Industry 4.0, also known as the Fourth Industrial Revolution, is characterized by the integration of advanced digital technologies, such as the Internet of Things (IoT), artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, big data analytics, robotics, and manu facturing process control into traditional industrial processes.
These cutting -edge technologies enable the creation of smart, interconnected factories and production systems that can communicate, analyze, and make data-driven decisions autonomously, ultimately driving greater efficiency, productivity, and competitiveness in the global market.

passages.heading: #23-24-22 | Page 114
passages.text:
The graduate certificate program in Industry 4.0 will offer a curriculum that covers the fundamental principles and practical applications of these technologies in various industries, including manufacturing, logistics, energy, and life sciences.
The progr am will emphasize the development of critical thinking, problem -solving, and hands -on skills, equipping students with the expertise required to design, implement, and manage Industry 4.0 solutions effectively.
Coursework in the program will include topics such as cyber-physical systems, Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT), data analytics and visualization, machine learning and AI in industry, smart manufacturing processes, sensors and SCADA systems, and digital supply chain management.
Students will also be exposed to real -world case studies, industry projects, and internships that provide invaluable insights into the practical challenges and opportunities associated with implementing Industry 4.0 technologies.
The graduate certificate program in Industry 4.0 will be designed with flexibility in mind, allowing students to complete the program on an accelerated basis, depending on their individual needs and schedules.

passages.heading: #23-24-22 | Page 114
passages.text:
The program will leverage online and blended learning formats, as well as face -to-face instruction, to accommodate the diverse learning preferences of students and facilitate seamless integration with thei r professional and personal commitments.
By providing a comprehensive and accessible education in Industry 4.0, this graduate certificate program will empower students to drive innovation, increase productivity, and enhance the competitiveness of their organizations, contributing to the ongoing transformation of industries and the global economy.
COLLEGE OF THE ENVIRONMENT & LIFE SCIENCES: Econometrics and Data Analysis - Cert Appendix N The Graduate Certificate in Econometrics and Data Analysis provides students and professionals with a strong foundation in applied econometrics and quantitative analysis, applicable to public policy, economic development, environmental and natural resource management, agriculture, energy, political science, and many other fields.
The courses will provide students hands-on experience working with large data sets and training in modeling and statistical programming using industry -standard statistical software .

passages.heading: #23-24-22 | Page 114
passages.text:
The certificate is an excellent preparation for graduate study in economics or data sciences using computational modeling of economic decision-making.

Changes Summary description and rationale of proposed changes to program.
If applicable, list any new courses or added existing courses to program.
Recently the Rhode Island Department of Education changed the World Language teacher certi�cation system.
Due to these changes, graduates from our current MATCP Education World Language program are now certi�ed to teach in Rhode Island at all levels of elementary, middle, and secondary education (grades PK-12).
The new program proposal is intended to address the changes in Rhode Island certi�cation regulations, which will require small changes to the requirements for our current BA in Secondary Education with a specialization in World Languages, effectively transforming it into an MATCP Education World Language All Grades Program.
The proposed changes affect signi�cantly less than 25% of the credit requirements.

passages.heading: #23-24-22 | Page 149
passages.text:
In the proposed new program, students will take a variety of existing EDC courses in Elementary Education, Early Childhood Education, Secondary Education, and Teaching English as a Second Language / Bilingual Education concentrations so that, upon graduation, they will be more versatile and highly employable educators who are better prepared to teach effectively in a wider variety of educational settings.
Changes What are the program goals?
Include any connections to Strategy 1 in the Agenda for Change.
The modified program will educate our students to become reflective teachers committed to global citizenship, social justice, and multicultural education.
Our program of study, based on current research and best practices, has been carefully crafted to provide our teacher candidates with ample opportunities to learn about different professional contexts and acquire knowledge about learning theory (social, emotional, and academic), and how to address the individualized needs of diverse learners.

passages.heading: #23-24-22 | Page 149
passages.text:
Through a variety of hands-on teaching experiences at PK-12 academic settings our candidates will have the opportunity to apply what they learn in URI courses in culturally responsive practices but also to learn to work with and from practicing teachers.
The standard program of study that our candidates will follow will provide them with opportunities to develop their teaching skills and acquire knowledge through coursework that focuses on teaching and learning at different developmental levels, and on cutting-edge second language acquisition theories.
Our program will help teacher candidates develop the necessary confidence and experience to effectively engage with a diverse group of students in a variety of educational settings.
Upon completion of our program and after successfully completing the licensure tests, our well- prepared graduates will be ready to apply for the Rhode Island World Language teacher certification in grades K-12.
Attach additional information, not to exceed 2 pages, if necessary.
Rationale Appendix D, Page 8 of 15 GC Report 2023-2024-11B Page 39 of 152

passages.heading: #23-24-22 | Page 150
passages.text: Changes How does the program align with the University’s mission and current Academic Strategic Plan? As stated in the URI’s mission statement , our institutional values are: Creativity and scholarship Diversity, fairness, and respect Engaged learning and civic involvement Intellectual and ethical leadership The program that we are proposing is not only consistent with those key guiding principles, but it can have a significant impact by strengthening those values in our learning community and RI society. Our program, based on rigorous scholarship, will help to shape the face of education in the state. The RI Department of Education approved on Nov. 15, 2022 new high school graduation requirements that include the study of the same World Language for two years. This new version of the MATCP Education - World Language Program could potentially attract more heritage speakers into the teaching profession. This will increase the diversity among faculty in our schools and will provide multilingual students with role models with whom they can identify. We anticipate that our graduates will become leaders and advocates in multicultural and multilingual education. The new proposed program of study will help our graduates develop their intercultural skills and acquire a “glocal” perspective, that is, the capacity to understand how local and global events are interconnected and the effects that they have on each other. Changes What is the demand and regional competition for this program?
Our program will not create any new competition to attract students that will be detrimental for other RI institutions of higher education, as the intent of the program is to adjust an already existing academic offering to the new certification reality implemented by the RI Department of Education.
The impact of the program will not be noticeable to other WL Education Programs around the state, only to the URI students that would benefit from a curriculum that better adjusts to their future professional needs.
To the best of my knowledge there are four other higher ed institutions in RI that offer World Language Education programs (BAs): Salve Regina, Rhode Island College, Providence College and Roger Williams University.
None of these programs is new: such programs have been in place for at least 10 years.
Only Provide College and Rhode Island College offer Masters in World Language Education.

passages.heading: #23-24-22 | Page 152
passages.text:
The new URI World Language Education program will fill a void that currently exists in the world language teacher preparation programs by focusing on providing more comprehensive preparation to our candidates so they can be effective teachers at the elementary and secondary levels, and it will allow us to continue being the leader in preparing future world language educators in the state of RI.

Most Secondary Education MA/TCP applicants have a B.A. or a B.S. in the content area they hope to teach (i.e.
English, Math, History, Biology, etc.).
Graduate applicants with an undergraduate GPA between 2.75-2.99 could be eligible for admission through the conditional acceptance policy.
Please email OCPP for more information.
Graduate applicants with an undergraduate GPA below a 3.0 may also apply after taking 24 hours of graduate coursework and earning a minimum GPA of 3.0.

Changes Describe the potential students and primary source of students.
Individuals passionate about World Languages and cultures will be our main source of students.
This includes recent World Language graduates that discover their vocation for teaching and that they want to make on their communities often apply to our MATCP World Language program.
We have a significant number of inquiries yearly from multilingual professional who already hold a bachelor's degree and wish to change make a change in their careers and become world language teachers in K-12 schools.
Changes To what extent will the program attract new students or draw students from existing programs?
The State of RI (the US in general) is in critical need of World Language teachers.
Such a need will only increase with the new RIDE High School graduation requirements.
We expect that the number of applicants to our program will increase significantly in the near future.

FS Bill #21-22-30G We are requesting a change of the program name from Learning and Development to Training and Development for the following reasons: Data from URIOnline Marketing show that potential applicants are confused by what the name of the program means. Data from URIOnline admissions shows that those who are clicking on the website are not continuing on to request information and submitting an application. Many people think the program is for K-12 teachers. Also, it appears that only people already in the �eld of L & D understand what the name means so if we want to attract people new to the �eld or who are interested in the �eld , we need to move to a name that is more recognizable. A scan of programs round the country show many use Training or Workforce Development in addition to L & D, further clarifying their purpose. We believe this change will solve the issues we have had with misunderstanding the purpose of the program. Attach additional information, not to exceed 2 pages, if necessary. This program prepares learners to execute the critical stages of identifying, planning, and evaluating learning in formal and informal environments applicable across a wide range of uses including corporate training, community education, and nonprofit programming.
In today’s fast changing world where companies are hiring people to do work that did not exist when the employees were in college and communicating one’s mission and information clearly and successfully to a broad audience are increasingly critical, many people are being thrust into education and training roles without the necessary understanding of their learners and how to create effective learning for them.
These learning professionals need to be able to diagnose learning needs, have a full range of learning methods and strategies to bring to bear on those needs, and the ability to evaluate its effectiveness.
Importantly this program focuses on more than the creation of learning.
It includes a focus on transferring the learning into action in their environments and program evaluation overall.

passages.text:
We propose a flexible master’s program that offers an attractive path to an interdisciplinary graduate degree to current students in the URI online certificate programs and post-graduate professionals looking to bolster their skill sets and attain higher leadership positions and salaries.
The program would require students to successfully complete a graduate certificate program offered through URI Online, two elective courses, and four professional skills courses.
The mix of professional and discipline-specific skills and knowledge aims to prepare professionals for a broad range of careers across private industry, local, state, federal agencies, and community organizations.
Graduates of the program will be prepared to implement impactful societal, cultural, and economic initiatives.
The program speaks directly to the desire to foster a 21st-century, 24/7 learning environment.
Offered completely online and asynchronously, this program targets working professionals across various disciplines who wish to obtain their credentials while still holding full-time jobs.

passages.heading: #23-24-22 | Page 214
passages.text:
The ‘a la carte’ nature of this program highlights the intersection of specialties employers are currently looking for while offering a flexible path to obtaining a master's degree.
Furthermore, the appeal of the in-state competitive tuition speaks to the accessibility of the program nationwide and beyond.
This program provides intellectual development for a diverse community of students.
The professional courses and graduate certificates push students to discover the synergies within their certificate areas and business/public administration to foster meaningful and impactful solutions and leadership.
The program integrates online certificate programs offered.
Students completing the certificates are accounted for within their respective programs, so it would not be considered an overlap but rather more of an inclusion.
This proposal describes a PSM framework under which focused tracks will be developed.
There are other master's degree programs that incorporate certificates into the masters (Master's of Public Administration, Masters of Science in Healthcare Management, and proposed Masters of Science in Health Outcomes and Data Analytics).

passages.heading: #23-24-22 | Page 214
passages.text:
They are very specific in their focus and audience.
For example, students entering the public administration realm will likely prefer an MPA over this program.
Similarly, students interested in applying data science to healthcare or focusing on healthcare management would likely choose those options.
This program allows for flexibility and broad appeal for students outside of those specific areas of focus.

Master's degrees are steadily growing in popularity as they are increasingly required for mid-to-senior-level positions in many fields.
This program meets the need of many working post-graduates who are seeking master's degrees in professional studies to become more competitive and relevant in the workforce.
The various certificates offered and anticipated through URI Online reflect diverse subject areas.
Accelerated online certificates are attractive to potential students looking to upgrade their skill sets.
This proposed degree supports students achieving an additional credential by offering multiple degree pathways that meet individual student needs within a flexible structure.
Many different tracks can be created in this model. "PSM programs prepare you for science careers in business, government, or nonprofit organizations, where workforce needs are increasing.
Employers of recent PSM graduates in the range from large, multinational pharmaceutical companies to newer biotechnology companies.
Graduates are also working with the federal government or for university technology transfer operations.

passages.heading: #23-24-22 | Page 215
passages.text:
Regardless of the employment sector, PSM graduates are finding exciting, well-compensated careers." Source: https://www.professionalsciencemasters.org/about None; the program is intended to be revenue-generating.
Many current students in the URI Online certificate programs have already expressed the desire to obtain a master's degree.
This program allows URI to retain these students by offering them a path to the degree that enhances and augments learning from certificate areas.
The option of an additional graduate-level credential may also motivate certificate students who haven’t considered a master's to continue their studies at URI, providing them with the credential needed for more senior career opportunities.
The Professional Sciences Master's is a formal structure and several universities across the country offer PSM degrees (https://www.professionalsciencemasters.org/program-locator ).
URI currently already has two PSM programs (Supply Chain and Applied Analytics and Cyber Security).
This proposal will expand our offerings and ensure we are able to compete for students who are looking for a mix of business/public administration and STEM knowledge and skills.

Industry 4.0, also known as the fourth industrial revolution, refers to the integration of advanced digital technologies into industrial processes, leading to greater efficiency, productivity, and flexibility.
This revolution encompasses the convergence of various technological domains, including artificial intelligence, the Internet of Things (IoT), robotics, big data, cloud computing, and more.
One of the key features of Industry 4.0 is the development of smart factories.
These factories utilize advanced automation technologies, such as robotics and autonomous systems, to improve production processes and reduce human error.
IoT sensors and devices are also used to gather data on the manufacturing process, allowing for real-time monitoring and analysis.

passages.heading: #23-24-22 | Page 241
passages.text:
This leads to more efficient resource allocation, reduced downtime, and optimized production schedules.
In addition to smart factories, Industry 4.0 is transforming other sectors as well.
In logistics and supply chain management, for example, advanced analytics supported by technologies such as RFID, robotics, and machine learning are used to optimize transportation routes, reduce inventory costs, and improve overall efficiency.
In the pharmaceutical industry, digital technologies are being used to monitor production and record histories to FDA-recommended standards for Good Manufacturing Practices.

The goal of this program is to provide students with a strong foundation in applied econometrics and quantitative analysis.
The Graduate Certificate in Econometrics and Data Analysis will prepare students to use advanced statistical methods, design policy evaluation, analyze complex economic models, and contribute to policy and business decisions based on primary empirical evidence.
The courses will provide students hands-on experience working with large data sets and training in industry-standard statistical software.
These skills are highly sought after by employers in many industries, governments, consulting, non-profit organizations and others.
Graduates will be able to apply advanced statistical methods to economic and financial problems with a wide range of applications related to public policy, economic development, environmental and natural resource management, agriculture, energy, political science, and many other fields.
Some types of work include policy evaluation; regulation impact; forecasting prices and costs; risk assessment; climate change and policy impacts; environmental justice; ecosystem services valuation; and public finance.

Moreover, graduate students in professional master’s degree programs (e.g., MBA, MPA, MESM; Goal 2, Action 1 ) as well as other PhD programs (e.g., Business, Public Administration; Public Health) can complement their degrees with skills in econometrics and data analysis based on their interests ( Goal 2, Action 1 ).
The Certificate will also open a pathway towards a PhD degree in Environmental and Natural Resource Economics, leading to increase in PhD student populations ( Goal 2, Action 3 ).
The credits earned through the certificate can be counted towards MS and PhD programs in ENRE.

Description of proposed change.
The Middle School Special Education Educator Certification Endorsement will provide students with confirmation on their transcriptions that they have met the requirements for certification in Middle School Special Education (grades 5-8) by the Rhode Island Department of Education.
This 3-credit endorsement is designed for a person currently enrolled in the MA in Education (with Specialization in Special Education in either Elementary or Secondary Special Education) or for a currently certified special education teacher seeking middle school special education certification. 2.
Rationale of proposed change.

passages.heading: #23-24-22 | Page 261
passages.text:
The endorsement in Middle School Special Education Certification would allow candidates to be certified in elementary and middle level special education certification OR secondary and middle level special education certification.
Rationale: The 2020 Rhode Island teacher certification regulations changed, in which special education certification is a stand -alone certification.
This means that an educator can obtain middle level special education certification as an add-on without having a general education middle level certification (which prior to 2020 was the regulation).
Due to this issue, there is currently only 1 te acher preparation program who has been approved to train middle level special education in the state of Rhode Island.
Middle level special education is a shortage area.
This proposal would prepare all special education candidates to be automatically certif ied in middle level special education.

Summer 2025 Summer 2027 The Master's in Mental and Behavioral Health Counseling program prepares graduates to work with clients in settings including counseling agencies, hospitals, and private practice.
The program meets curricular requirements for the State of Rhode Island's Licensed Mental Health Counselor (LMHC).
Students gain theoretical knowledge and practical skills in individual and group therapy approaches and career counseling with diverse populations.
Responses to JCAP questions about the new LMHC program: JCAP Question 1: Will the program have a hybrid option or will it be only in-person?
The proposed program is designed for face-to-face instruction to align with the courses and programs that currently exist for the PhD programs in Psychology as well as with courses that are offered in Human Development and Family Science that will be shared with the new program.
Once we launch the LMHC program, we are open to considering developing some course experiences to be delivered as hybrid or online courses as long as such alterations are consistent with state licensure guidelines and for our eventual accreditation by the American Psychological Association (APA).

passages.heading: #23-24-22 | Page 273
passages.text:
There are limits to an online approach particularly given the program that is training clinical skills and services that will frequently be delivered face-to-face.
However, students in our Clinical PhD program are trained in best practice in the delivery of teletherapy and the students in the new LMHC program will also be trained in these best practices in online/synchronous therapy.
JCAP Question 2: How will this program compete with existing programs offered at lower price points?
There is only one other LMHC program in RI (i.e., Rhode Island College) that can directly compare to the program we are proposing for URI.
Other LMCH programs in the state are either specialized in focus area (i.e., forensic counseling specialty at Roger Williams University) or are not as evidence based (holistic counseling at Salve Regina) or their LMHC programs are not accredited (Salve Regina, Johnson & Wales).
In addition, RIC's LMHC program is a three-year program with summer start while the proposed URI program will be two years with a summer start and a summer end (August graduation).

passages.heading: #23-24-22 | Page 273
passages.text:
Our program will embed the training of the master’s students within the broader PhD program (i.e., additional resources and mentorship, scaffolded learning opportunities).
Our LMHC students will take much of the same coursework and utilize the same training facilities that are part of our Clinical PhD program.
Our current clinical PhD program already has access to a broad range and number of externship training sites and more diverse externship opportunities than the competition programs.
Compared to the LMHC program at RIC, URI adds a more robust clinical and research experience based as clinicians and researchers).
Students who come from URI's undergraduate programs will bene�t by already being comfortable with the URI campus and our systems.
Our facilities are state of the art including our in-house Psychological Consultation Center with individual and family therapy rooms all connected to our in-house HIPAA-compliant video recording and observation system.
JCAP Question 3: Does the department/college have funding/resources to cover all the start-up costs of this new graduate program, including instruction, student support, advising, space etc?

No Not applicable Not applicable No The current need for mental and behavioral health care in RI is well-documented (i.e., opiate and substance use crises, need for mental health services with emergent needs in child and adolescent mental health).
Furthermore, RI is designated as a Health Professional Shortage Area (HPSA).
Therefore, there exists an urgent need for master’s level mental and behavioral health clinicians to meet workforce needs in RI and nationally to address these mental health and behavioral health needs.
The Department of Psychology currently has more than 1000 undergraduate majors whose bachelor’s degrees are not sufficient for entry into mental or behavioral health counseling positions.
Students who wish to work in delivery of mental and behavioral services require masters-level training that prepares them for state licensure.

passages.heading: #23-24-22 | Page 274
passages.text:
The Psychology Department proposes to develop a professional non-thesis master’s degree in Mental and Behavioral Health Counseling at URI to help prepare committed applicants from psychology and related fields for employment opportunities in our field, helping to address the workforce needs of RI employers and, most importantly, supporting the development of these students into an essential resource to meet the critical mental and behavioral health needs of Rhode Islanders.
Graduates of this program will be eligible, with appropriate post-degree supervision hours, for licensure in the state of Rhode Island to become licensed mental health counselors (LMHCs).
These individuals can work in a range of settings (e.g., hospitals, private practice, community mental health centers) and, when licensed, provide services that can be reimbursed by all major insurance providers.
The Psychology Department has a 50-year history of applied graduate programs in Clinical (PhD) and historically School (master’s and PhD) focus areas.
Our PhD program in Clinical Psychology has been fully accredited by the American Psychological Association since 1972.

There would be modest overlap with the Master of Science program in the Human Development and Family Science department insofar as both Programs would lead to licensure at the Master's level.

passages.heading: #23-24-22 | Page 275
passages.text:
However, the HDF program's graduates are eligible only to be licensed as Marriage and Family Therapists (LMFTs) whereas the graduates of the Masters in Mental and Behavioral Health Counseling will be eligible only to be licensed as Mental Health Counselors (LMHCs).
Although the two programs provide training in counseling and use external placements for their training, the two programs differ in terms of the requirements for licensure of the supervisors providing the training (students in the HDF Master's require supervisors to be LMFTs; students in the Masters in Mental and Behavioral Health Counseling program will have supervisors who are LMHC, MSWs, or PhDs).
The two programs are working together to share resources to the benefit of both programs (e.g., students in each program will be required to take class(es) in the other program).
The Masters in Mental and Behavioral Health Counseling program will also overlap with the Clinical Psychology doctoral program; yet, we see this as tremendously advantageous to both programs.

passages.heading: #23-24-22 | Page 275
passages.text:
Many courses in the Doctoral program will be shared with the Masters program ensuring fully enrolled classes that run each year (currently, several classes in the clinical program run every other year due to low enrollments).
In addition, the doctoral program has an excess of clinical externship sites requesting students for training.
The new Master's program would help to meet this demand and offer training opportunities to students in placements that have long-standing training collaborations with the doctoral program.
Finally, the Masters program will offer courses (e.g., Group Counseling) that students in the doctoral program may wish to take.

Adams).pdf Our proposed program in Mental and Behavioral Health Counseling will build upon the longstanding mission of the Psychology Department while also offering an important degree path for undergraduate psychology and related majors to meet the workforce needs of RI employers and the mental and behavioral health needs of Rhode Islanders and others in our region.
Over the past five decades, demand for master’s degree programs in psychology has demonstrated strong and consistent yearly increases, evidencing a thriving field with strong growth potential (US Department of Education, 2022).
According to the Bureau of Labor Statistics, job growth in Substance Abuse, Behavioral Disorder, and Mental Health Counselors is expected to show 22% growth by 2031 (US Bureau of Labor Statistics, 2021).
Program graduates will meet the curricular requirements for licensure as a Licensed Mental Health Counselor in RI (and other states).

passages.heading: #23-24-22 | Page 276
passages.text:
Licensed Mental Health Counselors in Rhode Island face a promising landscape of job opportunities, with high demand for counselors in various settings such as private practices, healthcare institutions, and community agencies.
Salaries for Licensed Mental Health Counselors in Rhode Island typically range from $65,000 to $110,000 annually, reflecting the importance placed on mental health and the valuable contributions these counselors make to the well-being of individuals and communities.
While we do not plan to offer teaching assistantships or similar funding to students in the new Master's program, there is a potential for funding some students if the Psychology department's allotment of TA positions exceeds the number of doctoral students with the ability to fill them.
In addition, students in Masters program would be eligible to apply for the competitive Dr.
Janet M.
Kulberg Memorial Fund in Psychology.
The Kulberg Award is awarded annually to students in the Department of Psychology at the University of Rhode Island with an interest in serving children and adolescents.

passages.heading: #23-24-22 | Page 276
passages.text:
The monetary award of up to $2,000 supports students of promise to pursue research and/or practice in broadly defined areas relevant to child and adolescent psychology.
According to the US Bureau of Labor statistics, employment of mental health counselors is projected to grow the fastest among similar mental health occupations, increasing 22 percent from 2022 to 2032.
Approximately 42,000 position openings are projected annually.
Regional competition includes a three-year Clinical Counseling Program with a specialization in either rehabilitation counseling or holistic mental health at Salve Regina University.
Roger Williams offers a Forensic Mental Health Counseling masters program geared to those wanting to provide services in forensic settings with populations including incarcerated individuals, those court-ordered to treatment, etc.
Both of these programs, however, offer education and training that is more specialized than the proposed Mental and Behavioral Health Counseling program.

Rhode Island College (RIC) offers a three-year Masters in Clinical Mental Health Counseling.
The program is accredited by the Council for Accreditation of Counseling and Related Educational Programs (CACREP).
The RIC program is also aimed at working professionals as the majority of their courses run in the evening.
The proposed Masters program at URI would be limited to 2-years plus an additional summer and considered a full-time program, with classes held in-person and typically during the day.
Additionally, we will be seeking accreditation from the American Psychological Association (not CACREP).
Johnson and Whales University offers an unaccredited 18-month masters in Clinical Mental Health Program.
We anticipate that the master’s program, when running at full capacity, will enroll approximately 20 students per year.
The program is expected to attract a large number of applicants, owing both to the size of our psychology major (currently the largest major in the University with over 1000 students) and the excellent reputation of our doctoral program in clinical psychology.

passages.heading: #23-24-22 | Page 277
passages.text:
The Clinical Psychology doctoral program attracts 200-300 applicants each year and offers admission to fewer than 4% of all applicants.
We anticipate that a number of applicants who are unsuccessful in gaining entry into our doctoral program will choose to apply to the professional masters program.
Admission requirements include the following: personal statement addressing professional and research experience, interests, and goals; statement detailing how background and experiences demonstrate a commitment and ability to engage with issues of diversity and inclusion, three letters of reference, and a curriculum vita.
All graduate students in the Department of Psychology are expected to be full- time students.
The program is a 2-year program with a summer start and a summer end (August graduation).
Applicants are admitted to begin in the summer semester only.
The completed application and all supporting materials must be electronically submitted by Jan 15.
A program page on the Psychology Department website will provide a program overview and detailed information for prospective applicants.

passages.heading: #23-24-22 | Page 277
passages.text:
A link to the centralized application service can be obtained from the Graduate School website, and the completed application package must be submitted online.
Applicants are evaluated on the basis of previous academic achievement, previous professional experience (in applied and research settings), letters of reference, and match between applicant and program goals.
Finalists may participate in a personal interview to complete the evaluation process.
The potential students will have a bachelors in Psychology or closely related field.
In fall 2023, the Department of Psychology had 1017 undergraduate majors and has averaged averaged 860 undergraduate majors since 2017.
Of those, approximately 75% are enrolled in the BA and the remainder in the BS, none of whom can practice applied work in mental and behavioral health without masters level training and subsequent licensure in their state of residence.
Many of these students will be applying to LMHC or related programs in their senior year or soon after.
We estimate that a pool of 25-40 URI Psychology majors would apply to our Masters program per year.

passages.heading: #23-24-22 | Page 277
passages.text:
In addition, another 30-50 applicants per year would come from bachelors prepared students in the region.
In addition, our PhD program receives 200-300 applications per year, only 3-4% of which will be offered admission.
We anticipate that 15-30 of these students might apply to our masters program.
We anticipate that enrolling an initial class of 8-10 students with eventual increase to 20 students per year will be smooth and be based more on availability and sufficient funding for appropriate staffing than on interest from current URI undergraduates, regional students with Bachelors degrees, or a subset of applicants to our PhD program.
Once approved, we will advertise our new LMHC program to our current students and regionally.

This course provides foundational knowledge in the theory and practice of career development interventions in the 21st century within the context of mental and behavioral health counseling.
Topics include career development theories and decision-making models; career information systems; career development programming; assessment instruments and techniques relevant to career planning; and career counseling processes, strategies, and evaluation application to diverse populations in a global economy.

PSY 642: Psychotherapy Skills (3 crs.) This course focuses on transdiagnostic and principle-based psychotherapy skills, understanding client dynamics, cultural and ethical considerations, and integrating theory with practice for effective mental health intervention.
